President Valmont: "Medical check-ins, who was there to witness, ward alerts, Black Circle instability flags. Not your private life."

Elira: "And politically?"

Rhea did not rush the answer.

President Valmont: "Politically, he will argue that every unlogged hour is where you are quietly controlling her."

Anger rose cleanly behind my ribs, separate from the Black Circle yet sharp enough to bite. Right across the open oak in full view of the mirror, Elira laid her hand over mine.

Leon looked studiously at the ceiling. Cassian muttered something approving out of frame.

Elira: "Then we do not let implication write the record."

President Valmont: "Meaning?"

Haru: "We answer what the Council has authority over, and refuse the rest."

Elira laced her fingers through mine.

Elira: "Together."

Rhea studied us for two long seconds, then nodded just as the mirror chimed a third time, dropping the kitchen lamp a shade lower.

Rhea turned away from her desk to patch in the incoming seal. Pale silver bordered the glass, carrying Magistra Senna Voss' mark.

Senna's relay opened without chamber walls or spectators, showing only her gray-sleeved shoulder, Rhea's witness seal in the corner, and a Valemere clerk's poised stylus. Krail's containment aide tried to slip onto the side channel.

Magistra Voss: "I reviewed your eleven o'clock filing minutes before this petition surfaced. State your boundary before Krail's office drafts one for you."

Elira finished her broth before answering. That small refusal to let panic spoil warm bread steadied the room better than a ward.

Elira: "I will answer medical questions. Whether Haru's presence helps or harms my recovery, whether I requested it, whether I can refuse touch, and whether hostile magic tried to hijack my consent."

The clerk's stylus scratched across vellum. Elira pressed her palm gently over the pendant.

Elira: "I will not submit an inventory of affection. Touch, sleep, clothing, private fear, and comfort remain private unless I judge a detail medically relevant."

No one softened a syllable.

Magistra Voss: "Boundary entered into the record."

Rhea's witness seal flashed crimson, and Krail's silent containment aide snapped off the channel before he could open his mouth. On the Aurelis side of the glass, Aira drew one sharp ink line under the heading on her copy; here at the kitchen table, Elira marked her own summary sheet with a decisive stroke and set the pen down.

Elira: "Mine."

The link closed, leaving only warm tea, the quiet lake beyond the panes, and the strange steadiness of having drawn a line before dark.

---

Night returned Lake Velis to black water and pale moonlight.

Elira stood by the sitting room window with the remade pendant resting against her collarbone. I came up beside her, close enough to share the draft off the glass.

Haru: "How does it feel now?"

Elira touched the dark stone lightly.

Elira: "Less like a shield someone strapped onto me. More like a promise I helped write."

Something locked behind my ribs loosened at the words. Outside, moonlight laid a silver track across the water. Elira watched it for a long moment.

Elira: "Do you remember the vow in the Moonlit Archive?"

Haru: "Every word."

Elira: "We spoke it before anyone knew. Before Lucien pushed this far. Before Cael. Before death."

She turned away from the glass to face me.

Elira: "I want another one."

The Black Circle went dead quiet beneath my skin.

Haru: "Now?"

Elira: "Now."

We walked down to the dock with a single lantern between us. Damp planks smelled of rain and cedar; her fingers held mine warm and steady in the cool air. At the end of the dock she stopped and faced me under the moon. No tribunal. No relay. No witnesses except the water and the life we had fought to keep from becoming someone else's exhibit.

Elira: "The first vow guarded your secret."

Haru: "And your trust."

Elira: "This one is for how we live now."

My throat closed around the shape of it. Not my danger alone. Not her recovery alone.

Elira: "I choose you after seeing what the world can break in us. I choose you without pretending love makes either of us safe. When I am tired, angry, or frightened for reasons that still hurt, I choose Haru: not a weapon, not a wall, not an answer to every storm."

Her fingers shook against mine, and she let them shake without pulling back.

Elira: "Choose me the same way. Not as the girl you failed to catch. Not as proof you have kept control. Just Elira."

Moonlight caught the pendant in black, gold, and silver. I had to steady my breath twice before I could speak.

Haru: "I choose you after death tried to turn love into a weapon. I choose you without asking you to be fearless so I can feel forgiven. I choose your temper, your terrible mornings, your slander against my braiding, the nights when thunder sounds like relays, and your hand whether it reaches for mine or tells me to stop."

Her eyes shone in the lantern light. Mine burned too.

Haru: "I will guard you when you ask for guard, and listen when you tell me to stand down. I will not put the Black Circle between us, and I will not love you less because loving you scares me. I will stay answerable."

Lake water lapped softly under the boards.

Elira: "Then stay."

Haru: "I will."

Elira: "Not as a guard."

Haru: "Beside you."

Her breath caught.

Elira: "Then I stand beside you too."

No sigil flared under our shoes. No ancient voice sealed the air. We kissed under the open moon with cold water moving beneath the dock and the Council waiting past the treeline, and for the first time since the Wounded City, tomorrow felt less like an ambush we had survived into and more like a life we were allowed to want.

When we carried the lantern back inside, a sealed notice waited in the folding mirror I had propped on the sitting-room mantle under Rhea's crest and Senna's countermark.

**DISTRIBUTED WITNESS REVIEW: SECOND HEARING DATE SET**

**SUBJECTS: BLACK CIRCLE STABILITY, DOMINION SEVERANCE LIABILITY, NOCTIS STUDENT PROTECTION, PROXIMITY WITNESS VALIDITY**

Beneath the formal lines, Aira had somehow smuggled one smaller line of ink:

**SLEEP FIRST. WORLD LATER.**

Elira let out a soft laugh, then caught my hand and led me upstairs.

At the bedroom door, she stopped, not from fear, simply to mark that the threshold was hers to cross.

Elira: "Haru."

I looked down at our joined hands before raising my eyes to hers.

Haru: "Tell me."

Color warmed her cheeks, though her gaze never wavered.

Elira: "Stay with me tonight."

My breath caught in my chest.

Haru: "Only if you are sure."

Elira stepped in until the pendant brushed the black ribbon tied around my wrist.

Elira: "I died with my choice stolen out of my hands. Tonight, I want this choice to be mine."

Beneath my skin, the Black Circle went utterly still, listening. I lifted a hand to her cheek, and she leaned into my palm before I could ask whether I was permitted.

Elira: "You do not have to be afraid of wanting me."

My voice dropped nearly to a whisper.

Haru: "I am afraid of hurting you."

Elira: "Then listen to me."

Haru: "Always."

She kissed me softly once, then not softly at all.

The second kiss shattered days of bruised caution. Elira rose onto her toes, fingers fisting in the front of my shirt, and pulled me down like someone done asking the world's permission to want anything. Heat flashed through me so fast the bedside lamp flame shivered; I reined the mana back before it could answer.

She felt the restraint and kissed me harder.

Elira: "Haru."

My name sounded different on her mouth, stripped of warning and sharp with wanting. I eased her back against the bedroom door, bracing one palm beside her temple and the other at her waist, halting the instant her breath hitched.

Haru: "Too much?"

She pulled me straight back in.

Elira: "Not enough."

I kissed her slower then, memorizing the warmth of her skin, her hair slipping loose across my fingers, the dark pendant pressing cool between us before warming to her pulse. She laughed breathlessly against my mouth.

Elira: "Even here, you are thinking."

Haru: "I am trying very hard to stop."

Elira: "Let me help."

Then the sore ribs beneath her shawl gave a faint catch. She tried to hide it by kissing me again, and I caught the shift anyway.

Elira: "Do not look triumphant."

Haru: "I am not triumphant."

Elira: "You noticed before I confessed. That is your version of triumph."

Haru: "My version is mostly quiet panic."

Her laugh broke wide enough that she lost her footing. I lunged to catch her, she grabbed my collar, and for one graceless second we nearly went down in a tangle on the floorboards.

After peeling out of our damp shoes, hanging our coats on the peg, and changing into warm sleeping clothes, we got under the blankets because she asked and because I wanted nothing more than to stay. We kissed until wanting stopped feeling like another emergency, then talked in the dark about nothing the Council could ever subpoena: the crooked-finned wooden fish, Cassian's ribbons, whether Aira had ever obeyed a page limit in her life, and Maelin's exact face if either of us skipped breakfast.

Just before sleep took her, condensation crept across the cool bedroom glass in seven thin branching arcs that curved toward each other without closing, splitting at the center into two small points: one black, one gold.

**CONSENT ANCHOR STABLE UNDER PRIVATE PROXIMITY**

**EXTERNAL REVIEW PRESSURE EXPECTED**

Elira opened one tired gold eye, read the faint pale script over my shoulder, and let out a low, unimpressed laugh against my collarbone.

Elira: "The house has terrible timing."

Haru: "At least it waited until midnight."

Elira: "Barely."

The pale letters faded back into plain mist on the glass before dawn could claim them, and moments later Elira drifted off with one fist curled tight in the fabric of my shirt.

## Coda: Seven Uneven Lights

Before sleep finally pulled the room under blankets-just after we had come upstairs past the hall lantern to the quiet bedroom threshold-Elira lingered by her desk and let seven small lights hover in the dark.

They burned uneven and stubborn above the blotter, each one a consent line that had refused to turn into a leash. Old magic prized symmetry; Councils prized signatures; Noctis prized obedience dressed up as clarity. The lights simply stayed lit.

I stood quietly in the doorway, watching her profile against the pale lake window. I did not ask whether she was exhausted, or whether speaking the new vow had hurt. It had, and some questions only pressured people into performing endurance.

Elira pointed at the smallest spark, where a crooked streak of pale amber flickered through the gold.

Elira: "This one is ugly."

Haru: "It answered anyway."

Elira turned her head toward me. Out beyond the panes, Lake Velis moved softly against the dark shore, and inside the quiet room the smallest spark steadied.

Elira: "Then we keep ugly answers too."

The Black Circle beneath my skin pulsed once, quiet as agreement and nowhere near command, as she let the sparks fade and crossed to the doorway to take my hand.

===== EPISODE 19 =====

# Episode 19: **The First Hearing**

The morning after the vow did not feel like morning.

Light entered the Lake Velis bedroom in long pale bands. The lake outside lay quiet enough to look like a promise. White curtains stirred in the window breeze, and somewhere in the kitchen, the old house kettle clicked once before settling back down.

Elira slept with one hand tangled in my shirt. Not the stolen one. Mine.

The distinction mattered less than it should have.

For a while, I stayed still and let myself count nothing: not breaths, not pulse, not window wards. At her throat, the new pendant crystal rested dark and calm, warm from her skin. Seven open consent lines now nested inside it instead of one closed protection route.

If Dominion tried to call her rescue an entry again, it would have to pass through questions first. Who is choosing? What is being saved?

Who is being named as cost?

Is Haru acting as protector, owner, or witness?

The last question had been Professor Valen's addition. I hated it.

I had agreed to it anyway.

Elira's fingers tightened before her eyes opened.

Haru: "I'm here."

Elira: "I know."

Her voice was rough with sleep.

Then she looked at me, really looked, and the memory of the night before passed between us without needing words. Her cheeks warmed. Mine probably did too, though I refused to offer evidence.

Elira: "You are thinking very loudly."

Haru: "I am thinking carefully."

Elira: "That is the same thing when you do it."

I looked toward the window.

She laughed softly and touched my jaw with the backs of her fingers.

Elira: "No regret."

The words struck deeper than I expected.

Haru: "No regret?"

Elira: "None."

The Black Circle did not stir. It listened.

Elira saw the relief I failed to hide. Her expression softened, then sharpened with the old Elira Vale precision that had survived death, grief, fear, and my worst instinct to become a wall.

Elira: "Do not make my certainty into something you must earn every morning."

I closed my eyes.

Haru: "I will try."

Elira: "No. You will practice."

Harder. And truer.

The folding check-in mirror we had brought upstairs to the far chest chimed once. Neither of us moved.

It chimed again. Elira sighed.

Elira: "If that is Aira, she gets one joke before I end the call."

The mirror brightened.

Magistra Senna Voss appeared instead, framed by the clean black-glass lines of an Inter-National Schools Council hearing chamber. Her silver-gray robe was fastened at the throat with a narrow white seal. Behind her, three floating transcript crystals turned slowly above an empty witness rail.

Magistra Voss: "Good morning. I apologize for the early contact."

Elira pulled the blanket higher with one hand.

I propped myself up beside her, careful to keep my shoulder clear of the mirror's line. She caught the habit anyway. One eyebrow lifted, and I shifted farther aside.

Senna noticed too, because Senna noticed everything and filed it away in polite grammar.

Magistra Voss: "The second distributed witness review has been advanced."

The room lost warmth. Elira sat upright.

Elira: "Advanced by whom?"

Magistra Voss: "High Councilor Krail's faction filed an emergency petition overnight. It claims that Haru Aerlen staying alone with you after the Black Circle appeared amounts to unsupervised, unranked influence over a key witness."

The old cold pressure gathered behind my sternum. Ozone. Metal.

The house wards did not flare. The crystal did not chill. Only me.

Haru: "They are turning recovery into contamination."

Magistra Voss: "That is the exact framing."

She scored a sharp ink line down the folio braced against her arm, softening nothing.

Elira's hand found mine under the blanket. Her grip was steady.

Elira: "And our answer?"

Magistra Voss: "Aurelis has already rejected the premise. Professor Valen, Head Healer Maelin, President Valmont, and the registered witnesses filed a joint medical and safety objection. Even so, Krail gathered enough signatures to force a public preliminary hearing."

Elira: "When?"

Magistra Voss: "At noon."

The old house kettle clicked again in the kitchen.

This time the sound felt absurd enough that Elira almost laughed. Almost.

Senna looked directly at me.

Magistra Voss: "Mr. Aerlen, the petition asks for three immediate limits before the full review. First, keeping you physically apart from Elira Vale outside supervised medical care. Second, banning any unscheduled use of the Black Circle. Third, forcing you to demonstrate the Black Circle's limits before a Council containment panel."

The room went very quiet.

Haru: "No."

The word left me before I could dress it up.

Magistra Voss: "That is also my legal reading."

Elira's thumb moved once across my knuckles.

Elira: "He cannot demonstrate a thing designed around restraint without being pressured into the exact failure they claim to fear."

Magistra Voss: "That is the argument I intend to preserve."

Haru: "Preserve?"

Senna's eyes narrowed in quiet warning.

Magistra Voss: "The Council has started receiving outside legal briefs from schools that are not even party to this case. Noctis Dominion College is under formal investigation and cannot take part directly. Someone is pushing their case through neutral schools, private donors, and rank-protection groups."

Lucien.

I did not say the name aloud. The mirror answered anyway.

For one heartbeat, Senna's reflection fractured. Black frost drew a smile across the glass where no mouth belonged. Then the fracture vanished. Senna turned her head as someone shouted just beyond the mirror's edge.

The transcript crystals behind her dimmed from white to gray.

Magistra Voss: "This line is being tested. I am ending contact. Do not travel alone. Do not answer any summons not sealed by Aurelis and my office together."

Elira: "Magistra-"

The mirror went dark.

Downstairs, the front latch clicked quietly as the house's six registered witness anchors crossed the door without waking the outer stranger chime; three breaths later, hurried boots climbed the stair landing.

Then Aira's voice came from the hallway.

Aira: "I came with breakfast and political dread."

The bedroom door opened exactly two inches. Aira did not look inside.

Aira: "Are you both dressed enough for bread?"

Elira pressed her face into her hands.

Elira: "No."

Aira: "Terrible answer. I will leave bread outside the door like a civilized friend."

Leon: "You said you would not mention the door."

Aira: "I did not mention anything specific about the door."

Cassian: "This is the loudest discretion I have ever witnessed."

Rhea's voice cut through the hall.

President Valmont: "Everyone downstairs."

That did it.

Elira threw a pillow at the door. It struck the wood with enough force to satisfy nobody.

By the time we dressed, brought the folding mirror back down, and crossed past the boarded west window into the sitting room, the restoration house had stopped pretending to be peaceful.

Rhea had turned the largest table into a field office. Council notices hovered over it in separate stacks. Aira had arranged breakfast by tactical importance: tea near Elira, bread near me, documents near herself, and one plate of honey buns in the middle as morale or bribery.

Leon stood at the window with crossed arms, watching the east road through a water-thin reflection. Cassian sat backward on a chair, outwardly relaxed, one hand near an unfinished red sigil suspended in the air. Professor Valen read the dawn copy of Senna's emergency dispatch with a scholar's calm and a soldier's jaw. Maelin counted Elira's pulse, then mine, then looked offended by both.

Maelin: "No fever. Elevated stress. Predictable foolishness approaching."

Haru: "The Council?"

Maelin: "You."

Elira smiled into her tea. I tried not to.

For a few seconds, the room remembered it could hold something besides danger.

Then I noticed the bread beside Aira's plate.

She had crushed one end of the loaf without realizing it. Flour marked the front of her uniform. The hem of her cloak was wet from the lake road, and one fastening sat in the wrong loop. Aira Solen never misfastened clothes. She treated uneven buttons as a personal accusation.

Haru: "You ran."

Aira looked down at herself as if the evidence had betrayed her.

Aira: "I traveled with urgency and very poor terrain cooperation."

Leon did not turn from the window.

Leon: "She sprinted from the academy steps straight down to the departing coach-passed me on the stairs-and then hopped off at the village stall when our axle stuck in mud on the turn."

Aira: "You were not invited to improve his evidence."

Leon: "You stole my spot beside the bread basket."

Aira set the wounded loaf on the table. Her fingers stayed on it.

Aira: "Senna's dawn relay failed twice before it found Rhea. The first time, the return seal went black. The second time, it showed this house with no lights."

Her voice stayed brisk, though her thumb pressed deeper into the crust.

Aira: "I knew there was probably a normal explanation. Dawn. Bad angle. No one awake because some people had finally made a medically reasonable decision."

Cassian opened his mouth, caught sight of Elira's face, and changed direction mid-breath.

Cassian: "I have never made a medically reasonable decision at dawn. It sounds exhausting."

Aira ignored him with less force than usual.

Aira: "I still ran. Then I bought breakfast because arriving empty-handed felt like admitting I expected a body."

The room went still, with no Council mirror waiting to turn her fear into a statement. Leon left the window and pulled out the chair beside her without looking at her. Cassian slid the honey buns closer. Rhea lowered one hovering document until its blue light stopped cutting across Aira's face.

Elira reached for the crushed loaf.

Aira: "That part is structurally compromised."

Elira tore off the flattened end.

Elira: "So am I. It remains bread."

She put half on Aira's plate. Aira stared at it.

Elira: "Eat."

Aira: "I brought this breakfast."

Elira: "Then take responsibility for it."

Leon sat. That gave Cassian permission to stop performing ease. He turned his chair around and sat properly, though with visible resentment. Valen folded Senna's transcript. Rhea stayed standing for three more seconds before Elira pointed at the empty chair beside the field-office stack.

Elira: "You too."

President Valmont: "There is an active containment petition."

Elira: "It will remain active while you chew."

Rhea sat.

Maelin looked pleased in the dangerous way healers looked when a patient enforced orders on other people.

Maelin: "Miss Vale, this is the soundest judgment you have demonstrated since restoration."

Elira: "I regret giving you material."

Food moved around the table. Cassian claimed the honey bun Aira had been avoiding under the excuse of evidence preservation. Leon poured too much tea into his own cup while watching the road reflection instead of the pot. Valen caught the spill with a corner of her sleeve and said nothing. Aira ate the crushed bread in small, furious bites.

Watching them, I finally understood what the field office had hidden.

They had not come only because Krail filed a petition.

They had come because Senna's dawn return relay had blacked out at Aurelis and each of them had pictured a different way we might be gone again.

Elira saw the realization land. She always did.

Elira: "You can stop watching us as if blinking is a breach of duty."

Leon answered before anyone could lighten it.

Leon: "Can you promise you will still be here when I look back?"

Elira's hand stilled around her cup. The honest answer cost her.

Elira: "No."

Leon looked down.

Elira: "Neither can you. That is not permission to spend the morning rehearsing grief."

Cassian tore his bun in half.

Cassian: "What if I am naturally gifted at it?"

Elira: "Then practice something harder."

His smile returned crooked instead of bright. Better.

I wanted to promise all of them that no relay, Councilor, doctrine, or old magic would take anyone from the room again. The Black Circle could have made the promise sound almost plausible.

So I kept it behind my teeth.

Haru: "Thank you for coming."

Aira swallowed.

Aira: "Obviously."

Rough at the edges, and completely hers.

Rhea slid a document toward me.

President Valmont: "Krail's petition has three layers. The surface goal is containment. The immediate move is separation. The hidden goal is setting a precedent."

I read the header.

**Emergency Motion Regarding Extra-Classification Influence and Witness Integrity**

My false Green Circle had once been a mask. Now every official sentence tried to turn my real name into a cage.

Aira tapped the lower section.

Aira: "This is the nasty part."

I read it. The petition never claimed Elira was weak or that I had harmed her. Instead, it argued that staying close to an unclassified mage after a traumatic resurrection could create a dependency that looks just like consent. Every word was clean. Every word was poison.

Elira read it over my shoulder. Her expression hardened, not frightened, insulted.

Elira: "They are using my trauma to erase my choices."

President Valmont: "They are."

Rhea set her emergency seal flat against the dark wood.

Elira: "Then I will answer them."

Maelin: "You will answer from a seated position after eating."

Elira opened her mouth, and Maelin aimed a healer's pen straight at her.

Maelin: "Miss Vale, I have now watched you die, return, nearly panic yourself unconscious in a storm, and redesign a pendant with ancient witness geometry before breakfast. If you argue with me about bread, I will sedate politics itself."

Cassian brightened.

Cassian: "Can you do that?"

Maelin: "I am willing to attempt it."

Elira picked up the bread.

The lake wards chimed before she finished it.

Everyone at the table shifted at once. Leon's water reflection snapped from the road to the front gate. Cassian's unfinished red sigil closed around his knuckles. Rhea was on her feet before her chair scraped back. Around my wrist, Elira's black-and-silver ribbon tightened as my hand curled, and the faint dark scar beneath my skin went cold on instinct, an old reflex trying to answer a sudden chime.

Two crests waited beyond the gate seal.

Valemere white-and-blue. Registered visitor marks. One Red Circle, one Blue weakened at the casting hand, both flanked by the paired escort lights Senna now required for travel.

Rhea read the names off the ward.

President Valmont: "Soren Ashvale. Talen Mire."

Cassian let his sigil die.

Cassian: "Our most tasteful possible invasion."

The gate opened only after Rhea verified Valemere's seal against Senna's joint authorization twice. Soren stood outside in a plain training coat, cold mist beading in his dark hair, holding a wooden box narrow enough for practice cords. Talen stood beside him with his braced hand tucked against his chest and a shallow metal bowl under his other arm. Neither carried testimony papers.

That was the first surprise. Soren's opening line was the second.

Soren: "Valemere's eleven-o'clock practice hour remains registered."

Rhea scanned past him for a hidden relay, lawyer, or diplomatic trick.

President Valmont: "The tournament is suspended."

Soren: "The brackets are suspended. The practice hour was not canceled."

He delivered it with the calm precision of someone who had spent years forcing officials to respect the gap between a rule and what they wished it meant.

Soren: "Elira and Haru are bound to Lake Velis by leave rules. We brought the hour here."

Talen shifted the bowl against his hip.

Talen: "I asked to come."

The sentence landed small and ready to defend itself. Rhea looked at him instead of Soren.

President Valmont: "For practice?"

Talen: "For one hour in which no one asks me what Lucien did, what Noctis meant, or whether my hand proves a larger pattern."

His braced fingers trembled against the dark wool of his coat. He did not hide them.

Talen: "I would like to spill water badly among students."

Behind Rhea, Professor Valen's expression warmed. Maelin's did not.

Maelin: "No one here is medically cleared for heroism."

Soren: "Good. We did not bring any."

Cassian leaned toward Leon.

Cassian: "I dislike him more when he is efficient."

Leon: "You dislike competition with posture."

Cassian: "I dislike posture that competes successfully."

Rhea inspected the wooden box. Four lengths of plain practice cord lay inside, each dyed Valemere white-and-blue at one end and Aurelis silver-blue at the other. No spells. No challenge seals. No ranking tokens waiting to turn an hour into precedent.

Under them sat a folded registration card.

**SUSPENDED BRACKET PRACTICE. NO STANDING CHANGE. NO OUTPUT RECORD. NO MEDICAL INFERENCE.**

Aira read over Rhea's shoulder.

Aira: "This is the most romantic document I have seen all week."

Elira: "You saw a containment petition ten minutes ago."

Aira: "Exactly. My standards are wounded."

Talen's gaze found the honey buns on the table. His mouth twitched toward a smile.

Talen: "Valemere served bitter tea after the memorial because sweetness was considered undignified."

Aira covered the plate protectively.

Aira: "I remember. I also remember you requested cinnamon bread with admirable courage."

Talen: "I have reconsidered. Survival may require compromise."

She handed him a honey bun. He took it with his unbraced hand, and when the paper beneath it slipped, Soren's fingers twitched toward the catch and stopped. Talen trapped the paper against the bowl with his wrist. Clumsy, and completely his.

Maelin missed none of it.

Maelin: "East garden terrace only, clear of the boarded west brace. Inside the visible ward line. No high-output casting. Miss Vale remains seated. Haru does not solve anything with the Black Circle. Talen stops the instant pain changes category."

Talen: "Who defines category?"

Maelin: "You. Then me if you become foolish."

Talen considered that.

Talen: "Acceptable."

Elira finished the bread before Maelin could point at it again.

Elira: "Now?"

Maelin: "You are far too pleased by restrictions."

Elira: "I am pleased by practice. Restrictions are just the ugly frame around it."

The east garden terrace sat on higher ground above the shore road, silver with cold dew and bare storm-stripped rose trellises dividing the flagstones into narrow lanes, while Lake Velis moved dark across the lower slope beyond the house gable. The surviving east boundary wards ran along the low wall in soft white points once Rhea sealed the gate behind us. No Council mirrors followed. Aira checked twice, then once more out of stubborn habit.

Soren set the cord box on a stone bench. Talen carried the metal bowl to the center square and lowered it carefully. Water inside shivered with the same rhythm as his braced fingers.

Talen: "Water-bind support. Three-breath hold. No movement target."

Leon studied the bowl.

Leon: "That is beginner work."

Elira, seated beneath Maelin's blanket while pretending the blanket did not exist, gave him a flat look. Leon winced.

Leon: "I mean the structure is basic. Not that performing it is."

Talen: "It was basic before my hand stopped agreeing. You do not have to rescue the sentence."

Leon looked like he wanted the flagstones to swallow him. Cassian patted his shoulder.

Cassian: "An excellent start. You offended the injured guest before I did. I feel liberated."

Talen crouched beside the bowl. Silver joints and dark leather braced his casting palm, guiding movement without pretending damaged channels could be forced back into their old shape. He placed two fingers above the water.

A faded Blue Circle appeared at his wrist. The water rose crookedly, one side pulling ahead until the sheet folded, slapped the rim, and spilled half the bowl across the stones.

Soren caught the bowl before it tipped.

Talen recoiled as if the catch had struck him.

Talen: "Don't."

Soren let go immediately.

The bowl hit stone with a flat metal ring. More water spilled. Nobody rushed to fill the silence.

Soren stared at his own hand, still curved around nothing.

Soren: "I thought it would fall."

Talen: "It did."

Soren: "I could prevent damage to the bowl."

Talen: "The bowl is not learning."

Wind shifted through the storm-stripped rose trellises. Soren's shoulders dropped a fraction. Talen pressed his good palm flat against the wet stone.

Talen: "If you catch everything before I fail, we only learn what you can hold."

Soren: "And if the failure injures you?"

Talen's jaw tightened.

Talen: "Then ask whether I want the catch."

The scar across Soren's right hand paled where his fingers closed. He had earned it moving too late once, and the reflex died hard.

Soren: "Do you want me to catch the bowl?"

Talen looked at the spilled water, then at his brace.

Talen: "Not unless it is going to hit someone."

Soren: "Understood."

There was no neat apology. Soren fetched a cloth only after Talen nodded, and together they dried enough stone to keep the next attempt clean.

Leon paced once around the bowl.

Leon: "Your pressure drops at release, not lift."

Talen: "I know."

Leon: "The usual bind asks the casting hand to hold shape and height with the same channel."

Talen's eyes sharpened. Leon stopped before advice became ownership.

Leon: "Do you want an inelegant alternative?"

Talen looked genuinely surprised.

Talen: "How inelegant?"

Leon: "Valemere instructors would object on aesthetic grounds."

Cassian: "Now he is seducing the room."

Leon ignored him.

Talen: "Show me without touching my hand."

Leon knelt across from him and shaped a thin Blue ring at water level, deliberately weaker on Talen's side.

Leon: "Let the bowl carry height. Bind only the surface tension. Your brace does not have to pretend it is the wrist you had two years ago."

Talen studied the ring, fighting his first reflex to bristle.

Elira leaned forward in her chair.

Elira: "May I ask something?"

Talen turned to her.

Talen: "Ask."

He adjusted the leather strap across his casting hand.

Elira: "When the release fails, does the pain start before the water drops or after you try to correct it?"

He thought for a moment while she gave him room to answer. Talen flexed his braced thumb once.

Talen: "After. The first drop frightens me. I force the channel wider. Then it locks."

Elira: "Then Leon's ugly version may work if you let the fall stay a fall. No correction surge."

Leon: "It is not ugly."

Elira: "You introduced it that way."

Leon: "For consent, not accuracy."

Talen let out a quiet breath that took me a moment to recognize as a laugh.

He reset his fingers over the water. Leon dismissed his demonstration ring so nobody could confuse explanation with aid. Talen built the shape himself: a narrow Blue line resting across the surface rather than beneath the whole mass.

The water lifted an inch, tilted, and spilled a thin sheet over one lip.

Talen's shoulders jerked. His Circle flared to force the slip back.

Elira: "Let it spill."

He glared at her for half a heartbeat, then let go. Water hit the stone while the rest hung suspended. One breath. His braced hand shook. Two. Light fractured across the quivering sheet. Three.

Talen lowered it back into the bowl. The final edge slapped metal and soaked his sleeve.

Soren did not reach out.

Talen sat back on his heels, breathing as if he had run uphill.

Soren: "Again?"

Talen flexed each finger inside the brace, listening to his own nerve lines.

Talen: "No."

No apology in it.

Maelin: "Pain?"

Talen: "Present. Not climbing. I want to stop while that remains true."

Maelin nodded once, offering neither praise nor disappointment.

Leon handed Talen a dry cloth, waiting until Talen reached for it.

Talen: "That was very inelegant."

Leon: "It held."

Talen: "Three breaths."

Leon tried not to look pleased and failed. For the first time all morning, the garden felt like a place students could inhabit even if the Council vanished.

Soren opened the wooden box.

Soren: "Good. Now the part no healer can mistake for medical rehab."

He lifted out the four cords.

Soren: "Common-square footwork. No Circles. No reinforcing with mana. One cord at the waist. Steal an opponent's without leaving the marked stones."

Cassian accepted a cord and tested its knot.

Cassian: "Can I leave the marked stones if I do it beautifully?"

Soren: "You lose the point beautifully."

Leon tied his cord at the exact regulation height.

Leon: "What counts as leaving? Full foot or any touch beyond the line?"

Soren: "Any contact."

Cassian: "Can an opponent be encouraged beyond the line?"

Soren gave him a dry look.

Soren: "Without magic, striking, lifting, or lying about a medical emergency."

Cassian: "Your rules have become suspiciously personal."

The fourth cord waited in Soren's hand. He held it out to me.

A strip of dyed cloth should not have rattled me after Foundation routes and city-sized return wards, yet my hand hesitated. Refusing wouldn't hurt anyone, winning wouldn't expose a conspiracy, and losing would only bruise my pride. That was what felt unfamiliar: stakes small enough to survive.

Elira watched from beneath Maelin's blanket without nodding me forward. She knew better than to make the choice easy to pin on her. I took the cord.

Soren tied the last one around his waist. Talen stood near the square with the emptied bowl tucked under his good arm.

Talen: "I call boundaries."

Aira: "I call everything else."

President Valmont: "You call nothing that enters the official record."

Aira: "Then I call with unprecedented freedom."

Elira held out her hand for Soren's score slate, and he passed it over without ceremony.

Elira: "First to three points. Clean take, visible possession. If Maelin stops the round, Maelin wins."

Maelin: "Finally, a sensible competition."

We stepped onto the square.

Twelve flagstones across, damp moss still darkening the seams, storm-stripped trellises crowding two corners above the terrace wall. No crowd, no ranking light waiting to turn footwork into bloodline proof.

Aira raised one hand.

Aira: "Competitors ready. Dignity unprotected. Begin."

Soren moved first, cutting one precise step across the center that forced everyone else to adjust. Leon turned to track him. Cassian used Leon's blind side to dart for his cord, and Leon slapped the hand away in outrage.

Leon: "That was not honorable."

Cassian: "It was not magic, striking, lifting, or medical fraud."

Leon: "You used Soren to block my line of sight."

Cassian: "He came that way."

Soren's fingers grazed Cassian's cord. Cassian spun, his heel stopping a breath short of the boundary line. Talen pointed at the stone.

Talen: "Inside. Barely."

Cassian: "Barely is where legends keep their furniture."

Talen: "I can change the call if you continue speaking."

Cassian looked delighted.

I had watched all three and gone nowhere, waiting for danger big enough to justify committing. Soren saw it immediately.

He stepped straight in without a feint, shoulders square, hands visible. I braced for the trick behind the direct line. His left foot cut outside mine, I shifted back, and he pivoted past me to snatch Leon's cord instead.

The blue-gray strip snapped free. Elira chalked the slate.

Elira: "Ashvale, one."

Leon stared at his empty waist.

Leon: "You were facing Haru."

Soren: "I was facing the square."

Cassian: "He is unbearable. I respect it deeply."

Leon retied his cord with angry precision.

The second round opened faster. Leon went straight for Cassian, who retreated laughing and tried to bait him over the line. Soren angled toward me again. This time I moved before certainty caught up.

I stepped inside his reach, crowding a duelist built for distance. His eyes shifted. I reached for the cord at his right hip. My fingers brushed cloth.

Behind me, Elira let out a single dry cough.

My head snapped toward her, and Soren took my cord so cleanly I felt the tug before I saw the cloth in his hand.

Elira: "Ashvale, two."

Haru: "You coughed."

Elira looked down at the score slate.

Elira: "I have lungs. They are occasionally theatrical."

Haru: "You nearly-"

The rest of the sentence smelled of graves. I bit it off.

Elira's eyes lifted to mine, steady and sharp.

Elira: "Do not use me to make losing feel noble."

No comfort in that, and no cruelty either. I had looked out of fear, and out of habit, and Soren had simply beaten me to the tie.

Soren held out my cord.

Soren: "Point stands."

Elira: "Obviously."

I walked back to my mark with warm ears and tied the cord again. No ward flared. No one died. The sting stayed the exact size of a lost point, and I had almost forgotten feelings could stay that small.

Across the square, Leon finally caught Cassian's cord without a trick: one failed grab, a second that Cassian mocked, and a third timed straight into the mockery.

Leon held the cloth aloft.

Leon: "One."

Cassian stared at him, then let out a sharp, genuine laugh.

Cassian: "There you are."

Elira marked Leon's point.

Rhea checked her travel timepiece.

President Valmont: "Thirty-two minutes until the noon hearing-three minutes left before Maelin clears you for prep."

Aira: "President Valmont has entered the dangerous phase where she pretends timing is not enthusiasm."

President Valmont: "Zero extra rounds if commentary continues."

Aira clapped both hands over her mouth.

Round three. Soren sat at two, Leon at one, Cassian and I at zero.

I tried not to care about getting on the board, which failed the instant Aira dropped her hand. Soren expected me to overcorrect after the cough, guarding his right hip and leaving his forward shoulder open as bait. Leon watched Cassian. Cassian watched everyone like a cat at an unguarded banquet.

I moved at Soren. He pivoted to close his right side, and while my eyes stayed on the front tie, my hand didn't.

At the last step I planted short and reached across for the loose tail at his left hip, where the knot had slipped around during the previous exchange. Soren caught my wrist. Grip wasn't banned, and neither was turning into it.

I rolled with his pull instead of fighting it, closing half a step inside his guard, and swept the cord free with my other hand.

For one second I just stared at the ordinary weave, still warm from his coat.

Elira struck the slate with chalk.

Elira: "Aerlen, one."

Joy hit me before caution could audit it, bright and ridiculous, followed a beat later by guilt over Cael, Elira's pale face, and Krail's petition waiting indoors.

Soren eyed the cord in my fist.

Soren: "You saw the knot turn."

Haru: "I did."

My breath steadied in the cold air.

Soren: "Good."

He didn't inflate the point into a metaphor. Behind him, Talen caught my expression.

Talen: "You are allowed to look pleased."

I glanced toward him.

Talen: "It does not wrong the dead."

His braced hand rested against the metal bowl, speaking with the plain gravity of someone who knew survival did not require paying penance for every decent minute. I let the relief stay until I reached my start mark.

Round four opened with Cassian still at zero and therefore the most dangerous person on the stones. He loitered near the corner boundary.

Leon: "You are planning something irritating."

Cassian: "I am hurt by your certainty."

Leon: "You moved your knot to the back."

Cassian: "I am adapting. You used to praise that when Haru did it."

Aira: "Historical note: he absolutely did not."

Soren came after me without his earlier patience. I barely kept my cord through the first pass. His hand grazed my coat, I spun inside the reach, and he adjusted before my heel settled. For three fast beats, the square shrank to pure footwork: no Black Circle, no dread, just a sharper duelist forcing me to work. I almost laughed.

Soren caught the sound and smiled once.

That was when Cassian swept behind us, used the clash the same way he'd used Soren against Leon, and snapped the cord straight off Soren's waist. He held it overhead.

Cassian: "Beauty remains admissible."

Talen: "Both feet inside. Unfortunately."

Elira marked the slate.

Elira: "Veyr, one."

Soren glanced from Cassian to me.

Soren: "I was watching the wrong threat."

Cassian bowed.

Cassian: "Put it on my family crest."

Leon: "Your family crest already means that."

Cassian clutched his heart. The garden broke into laughter, and even Rhea let out one breath before disguising it as a cough. Aira saw and didn't write it down, which might have been the kindest record choice she made all week.

We lined up for a fifth round. Leon shifted stance. Cassian dropped his grin. Soren knotted his cord higher. Elira leaned forward with the slate, bright-eyed despite the gray tiredness under her lashes, while Aira began comparing Leon's shoulders to a government filing cabinet.

Maelin: "Done."

Four competitors froze with four different objections on their faces. Maelin looked thoroughly satisfied.

Maelin: "A complete victory."

Elira: "The score is unfinished."

Maelin: "And staying that way."

She checked the pulse crystal in her palm as Soren untied his cord.

Soren: "Good."

Leon: "Good?"

Soren laid the cloth back inside the box.

We gathered the cords. Cassian tried to claim moral victory and was overruled by every authority present. Leon argued that his point against Cassian ought to carry into any resumed session, and kept arguing with the registration card even after Elira reminded him he'd watched Rhea read the rules aloud. Talen dried the bowl himself, and Soren asked before taking the wet cloth from him.

By the time the others headed inside, Rhea's travel timepiece read eleven thirty-one. Maelin went indoors to fetch the bitter noon draft, leaving Soren at the low east terrace wall where Lake Velis still showed past the lower slope, Talen on the bench with his brace unbuckled across his knee, and Elira resting in her chair beside me.

Soren looked down at the practice cord still coiled in my hand.

Soren: "If the brackets resume, do you want to compete?"

Haru: "Aurelis' position depends on the Council review."

Soren: "I did not ask for Aurelis' position."

Dark water moved below the far wall under a low slate sky heavy with mist. I tried again.

Haru: "My fighting could turn the bracket into evidence against me. If I win, it proves Black Circle students cannot compete safely. If I lose while holding back, it proves hiding my power skewed the rankings. If I withdraw-"

His tone was exact enough to strip away every impressive excuse. Elira watched me over the top of her blanket without stepping in.

Haru: "I want one match where losing costs pride instead of a life."

Saying it left me rawer than summoning any Circle.

Haru: "I want to be angry about a point. I want to practice until something ordinary improves. I want to face someone who wants to beat me without trying to own what winning means afterward."

Soren's scarred fingers rested along the garden wall.

Haru: "And I do not know if that match exists for me now."

Soren looked toward the damp flagstone square.

Soren: "It did for one point."

Haru: "There were no relays."

Soren: "Then relays are part of the problem. Not the point."

He made no promise Valemere could keep the distinction clean. He already knew what institutions did to matches after the fact.

Soren: "I have not withdrawn. The bracket can stay suspended without becoming dead. Your answer can too."

Talen flexed his bare fingers. The tremor was smaller, not gone.

Talen: "Everyone assumes I want to return."

Soren turned toward him.

Talen: "My family calls it reclaiming my future. My instructors call it recovery. Reporters call it courage because they do not have to hold the cup afterward."

He glanced at the water stain darkening his sleeve.

Talen: "I do not know whether competing again would be desire or an argument with Lucien conducted through my own hand."

Elira: "You do not have to know before your hand does."

Talen met her eyes. She had written to him after the tournament without promising repair, and she offered no false reassurance now either.

Talen: "What about you?"

Elira: "What about me?"

Talen: "Do you want to return?"

Her fingers rested on the score slate. Once, her answer would have snapped out fully formed, duty and ambition dressed in the same coat. Now she took her time.

Elira: "I want to know what my magic is when it is not proving I deserved the rank people already gave me."

No gold light rose at her wrist. Maelin had barred output, and Elira didn't need magic to make the question land.

Elira: "Competition may be part of that. It may not. I resent not knowing."

Talen nodded.

Talen: "That sounds more honest than courage."

From inside the house, Aira yelled that the medicine had arrived and smelled like a disciplinary hearing.

Elira pushed up carefully. I stepped near enough to offer an arm without assuming, and she took my forearm to steady herself. Talen watched without turning the sight into a promise for his own recovery.

Talen: "One request."

Rhea had returned to the doorway, her seal visible at her wrist. Talen looked straight at it.

Talen: "Do not enter this morning as testimony."

Rhea lowered her hand.

Talen: "The water hold can stay a practice note under my control. The rest stays here. I wanted one hour to spill water badly among students. I do not want the Council improving it."

President Valmont: "Granted."

Soren: "Valemere copy remains closed."

Aira appeared behind them carrying a steaming cup and visibly stopped herself from reaching for her notebook.

Aira: "I hate personal growth when it is inconvenient."

Talen: "You may record that."

Aira: "Finally."

At a quarter to twelve, Soren sealed three of the practice cords inside their wooden box and left the fourth folded on the bench beside Elira. The score remained on her slate: Ashvale two, Aerlen one, Varek one, Veyr one. No winner. No adjusted standing.

Soren: "Bring it back when the brackets reopen."

Talen tucked his metal bowl under his good arm as their paired escort lights flared pale blue at the gate. Minutes before the house chime struck noon, the Valemere pair had cleared the lake road, leaving only faint boot prints across the wet grass.

Elira carried the spare cord inside with unhurried steps and laid it straight across Krail's petition, covering the word containment without erasing it.

The hearing opened at noon through five relays.

Aurelis had refused to let Krail summon us into an isolated chamber. Rhea cited medical restriction, Valen cited historical caution, and Aira called it refusing to let anyone put Haru in a fancy jar, earning herself a seven-minute ban from official phrasing.

So the preliminary review came to the Lake Velis sitting room instead, through the portable Council relay panel Rhea set upright on the hearth mantle beside our folding mirror.

The central Council frame opened onto the chamber. Senna stood at the primary rail in her silver-gray robe. Above her sat Krail in a tiered seat of dark glass, handsome the way a polished blade could be, iron-gray hair immaculate and a Red Circle crest glowing cleanly inside a legal seal at his wrist. Delegates from Drakenshard, Valemere, Aurelis, Sol Aeternum Conservatory, northern civil-service schools, and three minor academies filled the surrounding benches.

Noctis' official seat remained empty. Its absence watched harder than any face in the chamber.

Senna rested one hand steady on the black glass of the primary rail.

Magistra Voss: "This preliminary hearing is to decide whether emergency limits are needed before the full witness review. We are not here to classify Haru Aerlen. We are here to examine sequence, risk, and basic safety rules."

Krail smiled faintly from his tiered seat.

High Councilor Krail: "Magistra Voss is correct. This body must not rush classification. That is why provisional containment is a mercy to all parties."

Leon kept his voice low enough that the mirror missed it.

Leon: "There it is."

Krail leaned forward slightly, hands folded over the petition seal.

High Councilor Krail: "A young woman died. She was restored through an illegal doctrine corrupted by Noctis. We have all grieved the conduit who paid that cost. But grief cannot blind us to the greater event. An unranked student unleashed force through the public relay network, shut down multiple systems, broke known magical law, and now stays alone in close quarters with our main resurrected witness."

Nobody in the sitting room moved.

Elira's hand tightened on the arm of her chair. I wanted to reach for her and held still, not out of deference to Krail, but so Elira could choose whether she wanted my hand while an entire chamber watched for proof I had already claimed it.

Her fingers lifted, palm up.

I laid my hand in hers. Across the mirror, Krail's eyes sharpened. Good. Let him record the difference.

Magistra Voss: "Miss Vale, do you wish to answer the proximity concern?"

Elira: "I do."

Her free hand stayed steady along the wooden arm of her chair, her voice carrying clearly through the glass.

Elira: "I am Elira Vale of Aurelis. Yellow Circle. Primary witness to Dominion Severance. Survivor of Votive Return corruption. Current patient under Head Healer Maelin. Current partner of Haru Aerlen by my own decision before, during, and after the events under review."

High Councilor Krail: "No one disputes your dignity, Miss Vale."

Elira: "You dispute my ability to consent."

Krail's smile held.

High Councilor Krail: "Trauma complicates consent."

Elira: "It does. That is why I am under medical care, why my choices are witnessed, and why I have friends rude enough to make me eat bread before proceedings."

Aira murmured beside the side table.

Aira: "History will thank me."

Elira never looked away from the mirror.

Elira: "But trauma does not transfer ownership of my decisions to a Councilor who has never asked me what I want."

The first transcript crystal above Senna's rail brightened. Krail leaned back.

High Councilor Krail: "And what do you want?"

The trap snapped open cleanly. If she named me, they would call it dependency. If she named safety, they would call me a threat. If she named freedom, they would call it unsupervised recklessness.

Elira smiled, sharp and exact.

Elira: "I want the Council to stop confusing possession with protection."

The second crystal brightened. Beside the bookcase, Professor Valen's eyes warmed.

Magistra Voss: "Recorded."

High Councilor Krail: "Mr. Aerlen."

Hearing my name in his mouth made the Black Circle go dead still behind my ribs.

High Councilor Krail: "Do you accept that your presence creates risk?"

Haru: "I do."

I held Krail's gaze across the glass without flinching. Down in the chamber, several delegates shifted in their seats. Krail's smile deepened.

High Councilor Krail: "Then you concede-"

Haru: "No."

The word cut cleaner than force. I kept my fingers laced with Elira's where she had placed them.

Haru: "My presence carries risk. My absence carries risk too. Isolation caused the old Circle Zero failure. Forcing people apart let Noctis turn witnesses into open routes. Locking me up would not remove danger. It would just move danger into a room with fewer people able to say no."

Senna's pen stopped mid-stroke. Across the chamber, even the whispers died.

High Councilor Krail: "You speak as if you understand ancient catastrophic systems better than the Council."

Haru: "No. I speak as someone the ancient catastrophic systems keep trying to turn into a tool."

The cold pressure surged behind my sternum. Ozone. Metal. Behind me, I felt everyone in the sitting room notice and hold their ground. That was the difference.

Rhea stepped squarely into the mirror's field beside Elira's chair, council red stark against the pale sitting-room wood.

President Valmont: "Aurelis submits a counter-proposal. No separation order. No forced containment test. No closed-door ranking panel. Instead: shared visit logs, voluntary medical check-ins, and open Black Circle safety checks with witnesses present."

High Councilor Krail: "You are normalizing the abnormal."

President Valmont: "No. I am refusing to make being unusual illegal before it has broken a single law."

Cassian muttered from his chair.

Cassian: "That goes on a banner."

Krail raised one hand.

The chamber lights dimmed with cold, official calm as a second document unfolded above the Council rail. Senna's expression tightened.

Magistra Voss: "That filing was not in the docket."

High Councilor Krail: "It arrived under neutral seal."

The empty Noctis seat stayed empty, yet the document opened anyway, black frost lacing its edges. In Lake Velis, the house wards woke with a low hum. Elira's pendant warmed, pulsing a silent question through its seven open lines.

She touched the crystal once, steady and unafraid.

Krail read the first line aloud before Senna could intervene.

High Councilor Krail: "Added theory: staying close to a Black Circle mage may override a witness's free will through a grief-bound mana link."

The words hit the sitting room like scentless poison. Aira's papers scattered upward. Leon swore. Cassian's red sigil ignited in his palm. Professor Valen went pale.

The phrasing did not belong to modern law. It was older than Krail. Older than Noctis.

Behind Senna, black frost bloomed outward from the empty Noctis chair across the chamber's glass wall, and a voice I knew too well poured through the legal seal wearing perfect calm.

Lucien: "Do forgive the interruption. I thought the Council might appreciate a more honest question."

Elira pushed straight to her feet.

Maelin: "Sit down."

Elira did not. Neither did I.

The Black Circle opened behind my ribs, not as a blaze or grief, but as a door refusing to become a weapon. Inside the mirror, Lucien's frost-framed smile sharpened.

Lucien: "If Haru Aerlen's mercy is not domination, prove it while everyone is watching."

The Council chamber fractured.

Every transcript crystal turned black.

And in the Lake Velis sitting room, the seven open rings inside Elira's pendant began to sing.

===== EPISODE 20 =====

# Episode 20: **The Trial of Proximity**

The sound inside Elira's pendant was not music.

Music wanted to be heard. This wanted to be obeyed.

Seven open rings rang in seven different pitches, each one a question sharpened until the air itself tried to answer. The Lake Velis sitting room bent around them. The windows became mirrors. The mirrors became doors. The doors became witness rails, polished black and waiting.

Lucien had not entered the house. That was the worst part. He had stepped straight into the argument, twisting old rules into an invasion that didn't even need a body to cross our doorstep.

The Council chamber remained visible in the central mirror, though only in pieces. Senna stood at the main rail with one hand pressed to a cracked record crystal. Krail's seat glowed behind her, sealed behind emergency glass. Delegates shouted without sound. Across from them, the empty Noctis chair was occupied by absence itself: black frost sketching the outline of a person who refused to spend a body on contempt.

Lucien's voice came through every reflective surface at once.

Lucien: "A simple test. Let the Black Circle remain near the woman it restored through grief and prove her will is untouched."

Elira's hand found the crystal. Beneath her fingers, it burned warm and alive.

Maelin moved first, stepping in front of Elira with no magic raised, only the full authority of someone who had long ago stopped being impressed by catastrophes.

Maelin: "Patient consent is suspended under hostile interference."

The pendant answered with a single low note.

Lucien laughed softly.

Lucien: "A healer tries to remove her from the question. How kind. How familiar."

The low note sharpened. The house's witness ward clicked shut against Maelin's healer seal, pinning her authority rather than her body.

I felt the spell before I saw it, a cold metallic taste behind my sternum as the old house magic recoiled from its own thresholds. Lucien was using Krail's petition as a frame and Noctis spell grammar as pressure, but the engine beneath it was older: a proximity trial built after an ancient disaster to decide whether a safeguard's witnesses remained people or had become extensions of his will. Fear had designed it. Noctis had sharpened it.

Aira: "Haru?"

Her voice was tight, pen already moving in her open notebook even as the room tried to turn every written note into evidence against us.

Haru: "It is testing whether anyone near me can act independently."

Leon: "Again?"

Haru: "No."

The nearest window caught my reflection, though the eyes staring back were wrong: too black, too still, too easy for frightened people to believe.

Haru: "This version tests whether emotional closeness counts as contamination."

The room understood before I finished. Cassian's humor vanished. Rhea's face became marble. Elira did not look away from the mirror.

Elira: "Lucien is attacking our relationship."

Lucien: "I am examining a public risk."

Elira: "You are hiding behind public language because no honest spell would carry you."

For the first time, the frost outline in the Noctis seat flickered. A tiny thing. Satisfying.

Then the crystal rang again, and the sitting room split into stations.

Pale circles appeared across the floor, each open at one side. Aira's lit blue-white around scattered notes. Leon's flowed in water-thin lines at the windows. Cassian's burned red beneath his chair. Rhea's sharpened into crisp council lines at the doorway. Professor Valen's formed a record sigil near the bookcase. Maelin's steadied beside Elira's chair.

Mine did not appear. Elira's did, gold and black, open on the side facing me.

Lucien: "The trial offers mercy. Each witness may step away from Haru Aerlen's field and answer free of influence."

The floor between us darkened into a path leading toward the far side of the room, away from me and away from the table where we had eaten bread, argued, and revised the pendant with human hands.

High Councilor Krail's voice cut through the mirror.

High Councilor Krail: "Magistra, this is an unauthorized breach. I request containment-"

Magistra Voss: "Denied pending survival."

I liked her more with every crisis.

Lucien: "Miss Vale. You first."

The path away from me brightened. Elira's breath caught as the crystal pulsed at her throat. I felt the trial lean toward her wound, offering an explanation that would make pain simpler: that she stayed out of fear, or power, or because the Black Circle had trained her body to return to me.

Fear in polite clothes always sounded more reasonable than cruelty. I released her hand so every witness, along with Lucien and Krail, could see it. The Black Circle stirred, offended by the distance, and I kept my palm open at my side.

Haru: "Elira chooses."

Lucien: "A useful line."

Elira turned toward me. For one second, I saw the night of the storm in her eyes: the cut, the cold, the memory of dying in a rescue that others had twisted until mercy looked like a wound.

Then she stepped away from me. The room gasped. I did not move. That was the hardest thing I had done since watching her die.

Elira crossed to the far side of the room. The open gold circle followed her without dragging or binding, simply asking whether she would remain herself outside my reach. She stopped alone beside the cold fireplace, and the pendant's ringing softened.

Lucien: "Good. Now answer. Do you love Haru Aerlen because you choose him, or because the Black Circle made itself necessary to your survival?"

The question was obscene because it dressed up as philosophy. Elira lifted her chin.

Elira: "I loved him before I knew how much danger surrounded him."

The first open ring dimmed.

Elira: "I chose him before his name became public."

The second dimmed.

Elira: "I feared him once, when he showed me the Black Circle. Then I understood the fear was not of him, but of what the world would do if it saw him as a thing."

The third dimmed.

Elira: "I wanted him after I died because being alive returned my body to me, and to no one else."

The fourth dimmed.

Her face flushed, yet she did not look down.

Elira: "And last night belonged to me as much as to him."

Aira made a strangled sound and wrote so hard her pen sparked. Cassian stared at the ceiling with heroic dedication. Leon turned red and pretended the window required inspection. Rhea looked like she was calculating whether dignity could survive friendship. Maelin only nodded once.

The fifth ring dimmed. Lucien's frost outline sharpened.

Lucien: "A lovely speech. Still just the habit of keeping him close."

Elira smiled.

Elira: "Then let someone else ask."

She turned toward the blue-white station.

Elira: "Aira."

Aira's station flashed.

Aira: "Oh, excellent. I was hoping the ancient relationship court would notice me."

Elira: "Ask me something Haru would not want you to ask."

I looked at her.

Haru: "Elira."

She did not look back. Aira's expression changed, the joke vanishing while the friendship stayed.

Aira: "Do you ever stay with him because you are afraid he will break without you?"

The sixth ring flared. The room held its breath. Elira's smile vanished.

Elira: "Yes."

Her fingers curled lightly against the cold stone mantel. The ring stayed bright, and Lucien's silence sharpened with interest.

Elira: "Sometimes. More often since the Wounded City. I see him watching the world for threats. I see him making himself smaller so no one else panics. I see the Black Circle answer grief faster than he wants it to. Sometimes I am afraid that if I step away, he will decide the safest version of himself is loneliness."

The sixth ring burned painfully bright.

Elira: "But that fear is mine. It is not proof that he owns me. It is proof that I love someone who is wounded too."

The light steadied.

Elira: "And when I stay, I am not staying because he cannot survive without me. I am staying because I refuse to let fear teach either of us that love is containment."

The sixth ring dimmed. Aira wiped at her face angrily.

Aira: "Recorded, unfortunately."

Lucien: "One ring remains."

I knew before it moved. The seventh ring was mine, waiting in the crystal like a blade wrapped in velvet.

The Black Circle opened beneath my skin, just enough to answer. Shadows deepened across the sitting room. Beyond the windows, Lake Velis turned from blue to black glass, and every open circle on the floor leaned toward me.

Lucien: "Haru Aerlen. If Elira Vale asks you to let her face danger without your intervention, will you obey?"

There were easier questions. Would I kill? Would I die? Would I burn Noctis down to its foundations? Those had answers I could give with enough restraint. This one found the part of me that still heard Elira's body hitting the Wounded City stone.

I looked at her across the room. She did not soften the question for me, because she loved me.

Haru: "No."

The seventh ring screamed. Every window cracked. Krail stood in the Council chamber.

High Councilor Krail: "There. There is the confession."

I swallowed the cold taste in my mouth.

Haru: "If she asks while forced, hurt, misled, or cornered by someone else's rules, I will not obey the words. I will answer the person beneath them."

The scream faltered.

Haru: "If she asks as herself, with risk named honestly, then yes."

The Black Circle pressed against my ribs like a storm wanting permission. I did not give it.

Haru: "I will hate it. I may fail once and need my witnesses to stop me. I will not pretend love makes restraint easy. But I accept that protecting Elira cannot mean becoming the only door she is allowed to use."

The seventh ring dimmed enough to let the room breathe.

Elira crossed the floor back to me.

Lucien: "Careful. The trial has not closed."

She kept walking.

High Councilor Krail: "Miss Vale-"

Elira reached me and took my open hand. The seventh ring went dark because return had been chosen, and the pendant fell silent.

For one heartbeat, the old house became only a house again.

Then the central mirror shattered inward. No glass flew.

Instead, the reflection of the Council chamber folded into a narrow black corridor, and at the end of it stood Lucien Voss in full Noctis uniform, pale hair silvered by frost, eyes colder than any spell should make a living person. It was a relay-body: illegal, dangerous, and sharp as a perfect lie before it cut.

Lucien: "Then let us test return."

Behind him, twelve small reserve lights flared down the dark span-Blue, Red, Yellow, and three faint green points nearly swallowed by dark. Noctis student crests. Cael had not been the only conduit-track student. Iven Sahl's name burned in my memory from the funeral. The lights flickered like trapped breaths.

Nera stepped forward from the side hall doorway, where Senna's rear-gate escort had quietly brought her and Darian in out of the Council mirror's range during the opening procedural motions-Darian newly clear of Noctis's crumbling house arrest through Senna's emergency line while Oric stayed back at Aurelis to guard the archive. She looked silent as guilt and twice as pale.

Nera: "Those are students."

Lucien looked at her through the corridor.

Lucien: "Those are reserves."

The Black Circle opened. This time, everyone felt it.

The relay-body stepped through the mirror. One polished black shoe touched the Lake Velis floor, and frost spread from the heel in a perfect Noctis sigil. The second shoe crossed after it. Lucien arrived without breath, without warmth, and without enough of a pulse for Maelin's healer charm to recognize him as alive, yet with more than enough substance to hurt us.

Nera moved between him and the corridor lights.

Nera: "Do not strike the relay-body."

Cassian already had fire in one hand. He stopped before throwing it.

Nera: "The trapped students are carrying the return load. If his body breaks, the backlash hits them."

Lucien smiled.

Lucien: "Still useful. How reassuring."

Nera went white. He had not raised his voice. One sentence snapped years of training back into her posture: shoulders squared, hands visible, guilt standing at attention.

Nera pulled her re-riveted Noctis binding bands out of her evidence pouch and snapped both split clasps back over the healed pale scars on her wrists so the corridor would recognize an officer's authority. Darian stepped beside her out of the doorway and struck his own snapped Noctis ring against the floor. The sound was ugly and human. Nera's shoulders lowered. Lucien noticed him then.

Lucien: "Darian Thorne. You always did mistake proximity to courage for possession of it."

Darian: "I brought enough to stand here."

Lucien: "Then spend it."

The relay-body lifted one hand.

Every reserve light behind him screamed, silent in the air yet shrieking straight through the pendant. Twelve pulses struck Elira's crystal in different rhythms: panic, cold, drained magic, a child's heart forced too fast by a conduit brace. Elira doubled over. Gold light burst from beneath her collar and scattered across the floor in broken arcs. I caught her shoulder.

The Black Circle surged toward Lucien's raised hand.

Nera: "Those are their pulses! If you erase the signal, you erase our only route to them."

I stopped. Lucien's smile widened. He had wanted the hesitation.

Then he crossed the room faster than a reflection should move.

Leon threw a water wall between us. Lucien passed through it; the water froze around his outline and crashed to the floor in his shape after he was already beyond it. Cassian changed tactics before the ice finished breaking, sending fire along the floor instead of at Lucien to burn the Noctis sigil beneath the relay-body and sever its cleanest anchor.

Lucien staggered half a step.

Cassian: "You do have feet. I was beginning to think you arrived by arrogance alone."

Lucien turned his hand. The burned sigil inverted. Black frost climbed Cassian's flame and sank into his right wrist. His Red Circle went dark. He swore, dropped to one knee, and drove the affected hand against the stone before the cold could enter his elbow. Leon flooded the line, and steam exploded between them.

Lucien emerged from it beside Elira. He did not attack me. That would have been simpler. He pressed two fingers against the pendant at her throat, and Elira stopped breathing. The room vanished from her eyes.

Lucien: "Do you remember the exact instant your choice stopped belonging to you?"

Cold spread through the crystal. Elira's body arched. The pendant projected the Wounded City across every wall: Cael inside the return geometry, Elira stepping forward, the hook closing, my face when her pulse stopped. Memory edited for cruelty. In this version, Elira smiled when the hook took her, I reached too slowly because part of me wanted the Black Circle seen, and Cael looked relieved to die.

Elira saw all three lies while her body remembered the real pain. Lucien leaned closer.

Lucien: "Choice is only the story survivors tell before someone stronger edits the record."

I seized his wrist. My hand passed through cold light and closed around something solid at its center: a narrow black relay rod hidden inside the body. Every reserve light behind him flared. Children cried through the crystal. I could not crush it, and Lucien knew. He looked at my hand locked around the rod and spoke softly enough that only Elira and I heard.

Lucien: "There. Your mercy has a handle after all."

Elira moved. Still unable to breathe properly, still trapped inside the false memory, still hers, she drove her forehead into Lucien's face. The relay-body jerked backward at the neck while my grip stayed clamped on the inner rod. His fingers left the pendant.

Elira fell against me, dragged in one ragged breath, and raised her Yellow Circle with the next. No elegant ring. No academy form. Gold fire wrapped her fist.

Maelin: "Elira, no sustained..."

Elira hit Lucien across the mouth. The impact cracked the relay-body from jaw to collar. Gold light flooded the fracture and exposed the black rod in my hand. For the first time, Lucien looked surprised by pain.

Elira: "You do not get to tell me what I remember."

Blood appeared at the corner of her mouth, forced up by raw power tearing through channels nowhere near healed enough to carry it. Maelin caught her as her knees failed.

Maelin: "Done. Your body is done."

Elira tried to raise her hand again. Maelin trapped it against her own shoulder.

Maelin: "You chose the first strike. I am choosing medical restraint before the second kills you. Be angry later."

Elira shook with fury, then stopped.

Lucien touched the crack in his borrowed face. Gold burned beneath his fingers. The reserve lights pulsed erratically as the damaged body began drawing harder from them to repair itself. Aira caught the pattern.

Aira: "He is cycling through the lights. Third, seventh, twelfth, then back to third."

Nera looked into the corridor. The seventh light pulsed green at its outer rim, flickering blue-white inside. Iven.

Nera: "The relay carries a route list. If we catch one cycle, we can keep the path open after he shuts it."

President Valmont: "Method?"

Nera was already loosening the re-riveted clasp on her right wrist band.

Nera: "I go in. Darian holds me. Aira calls the cycle."

Darian grabbed her arm.

Darian: "No. We go in."

Nera: "The corridor knows my old command seal."

Darian: "And Lucien knows your guilt."

They stared at each other. No time for a perfect answer. Rhea turned the choice into clear, strict orders instead.

President Valmont: "Nera steps in one body length. Darian holds her from behind. Leon guards the doorway. Cassian burns only the floor marks. Aira calls the retreat whether we get the list or not."

Nera: "Accepted."

Darian: "Accepted."

Lucien laughed through the fracture in his face.

Lucien: "Aurelis turns panic into committees with admirable speed."

President Valmont: "And Noctis turns children into batteries. I prefer our delay."

Leon drove water into the shattered mirror frame, spreading a blue border around the corridor to give the threshold a physical edge. Cassian burned the frost away from Nera's path in short left-handed bursts of red flame while his darkened right wrist spasmed at his side. Aira tracked the cycling lights.

Aira: "Third. Seventh. Twelfth. Third. Seventh, go."

Nera stepped into the corridor. Darian locked both arms around her waist. The cold tried to pull them apart by making each body feel like the other's restraint. Nera cried out. Darian loosened his grip just enough for her to choose it again.

Nera reached, and the seventh light recoiled.

Nera: "Iven Sahl. Noctis first-year. Conduit track. Reacts badly to cold braces. Linked to Cael Nox."

The light steadied. A small slate of black glass formed beneath it. Lucien moved toward her.

I stepped between them with my hand still closed around the relay rod, holding without crushing. The Black Circle turned once under my skin, and every shadow in the room aligned behind me. Lucien stopped.

Haru: "You wanted to know what I protect."

The words came out colder than I intended.

Haru: "Watch."

Behind me, Nera tore the black slate free. The corridor convulsed.

Aira: "Retreat!"

Darian pulled. Nera came backward with the slate against her chest. The threshold snapped at her leading shoulder. Leon closed his water border around it, yet one blade of black glass crossed before the seal completed, cutting Nera from collar to upper arm. Darian caught her.

Maelin could not leave Elira, so Rhea threw a red compression seal across the wound. Temporary, painful, enough.

Nera did not look at the blood. She looked at the slate. One name remained visible.

**IVEN SAHL: ACTIVE RESERVE ROUTE / LOCATION WITHHELD**

Under it, eleven registry positions flickered without names: a route, not a rescue.

Lucien saw what she had taken. The warmth left his expression completely. He reached through the cracked relay-body and closed his hand around the rod I held. For one second, we both touched the same tether, his fingers cold enough to burn.

Lucien: "You have mistaken one stolen name for progress."

Haru: "You noticed the theft."

His eyes sharpened. Good. I opened my hand.

He expected resistance. My release made him pull too hard, and the relay-body staggered backward into its own corridor. Cassian burned the last floor sigil. Leon slammed the water border shut.

Elira, pale in Maelin's arms, kept her hand down at her side, eyes locked on the cracked mirror. The gold fracture her single strike had torn from jaw to collar split wide under Leon's border slam, and the relay-body shattered inward. Every fragment carried Lucien's face for one falling instant before dissolving into frost that blew back down the corridor without touching the students behind it. The twelve lights remained, and so did Lucien's voice.

I crossed back to Elira. Maelin kept one arm around her ribs without blocking the hand Elira held out for me. Elira's fingers tightened around mine to anchor me where I stood.

The frost inside the broken mirror formed Lucien's smile.

Lucien: "Come back to school, Haru Aerlen. The world wants to know what you are. I will show them what you protect."

The corridor snapped shut.

The Council chamber returned in broken fragments, Senna's voice cutting through static.

Magistra Voss: "Emergency session suspended. Aurelis, secure your students. All schools, lock conduit registries now."

The mirror went black. No one moved.

Maelin broke the stillness by throwing a roll of bandage at Leon's head. He caught it on reflex.

Maelin: "Compression on Nera's shoulder. Darian, keep her sitting. Cassian, show me your wrist. Elira, if you raise that hand again I will personally redefine free will as staying conscious."

Everyone moved. Pain made the room honest faster than procedure had.

Nera sat against the overturned table with Rhea's red seal still clamped over the cut, blood soaking the collar of her borrowed coat. Darian held the bandage where Leon placed it and counted each breath she tried to hide. Cassian's right hand would not produce flame; the skin stayed unburned, yet black frost sat beneath the Red Circle line like ink trapped under glass. Elira's pulse skipped every seventh beat. Maelin heard it and went terrifyingly quiet.

Maelin: "No more Yellow magic today. Not one spark."

Elira: "The corridor..."

Maelin: "Closed. Your channels are not."
