Elira looked at the black slate in Nera's lap. The list slots were fading. Iven's name remained, while the eleven unnamed lights did not. Aira saw the first disappear.

Aira: "No. No, no. Darian, angle the slate toward me."

Darian: "I am holding pressure."

Leon took the slate without removing his hands from Nera's shoulder. Water rose from his wrist in a thin, clear sheet and held the glass at eye level. Aira opened her notebook as the second light vanished.

Aira: "I need rhythm, color, position. Call them."

Nera's lips had gone pale.

Nera: "First: Blue, fast triple pulse, first-year cadence. Second..."

She stopped. The second was gone. Nera struck the floor with her good hand.

Nera: "I knew it."

Darian tightened the bandage.

Darian: "Then know the next one."

Cruel wording from anyone else. From him, a rope. Nera looked back at the slate.

Nera: "Third: Green. Weak pulse against the cold. Younger than Iven. Fourth: Red, brace interference on the second beat. Fifth: Blue..."

Aira wrote furiously. Mira was not there, and the Green copy table was hours away across the hills at Aurelis. No duplicate hands waited automatically. So Rhea tore the Council petition in half and wrote on the blank backs. Professor Valen took the margins of her historical notes. Cassian, his right wrist frost-locked and his reserves nearly spent, used his left hand to copy colors onto the paper wrapping from the food basket. Leon kept the slate steady with water while holding Nera still.

Elira reached for a page. Maelin slapped her fingers away.

Maelin: "You are a patient."

Elira: "I can dictate."

Maelin considered the compromise, then snatched a clean bandage wrapper from her kit and took a pen in her free hand.

Maelin: "Dictate."

Elira tracked the visible order while Nera named cadence.

Elira: "Sixth spot dimmed before fifth. Mark a break in the line. Seventh is Iven-weak Green outside, faint blue-white shiver at the core. Eighth: Blue, flickering in pairs with ninth-Red, fast short pulse."

The slate grew cold enough for Leon's water support to freeze. He swore and increased pressure. The glass cracked.

Aira: "Do not let it split through a position."

Leon: "I had planned to crack it artistically."

Cassian looked up from his food-wrapper copy.

Cassian: "That is usually my department."

The joke lasted one breath. Then the tenth light vanished, and Nera lost sequence. She stared at the blank position, breathing too fast.

Nera: "I do not know."

Aira: "Recorded. Eleventh."

Nera: "I should know."

Aira: "You do not. Eleventh."

Work small enough to survive panic. Nera swallowed.

Nera: "Yellow. Held-down crown rhythm. Maybe a senior. Twelfth, Green, flickering, no, wait..."

The final light folded inward.

Elira: "It changed before disappearing."

Aira: "How?"

Elira closed her eyes, replaying it.

Elira: "Green outside. Blue-white at the core. Like a lower crest hiding a borrowed rank."

Nera looked at her.

Nera: "Conduit masking."

Aira wrote the phrase across three pages.

The slate erased everything except Iven Sahl's name. Then a Noctis seal surfaced beneath it.

**UNAUTHORIZED REGISTRY POSSESSION**

Black fire caught the lower edge. Leon released the water support before the flame could travel into his Circle, and the slate dropped.

Haru: "Do not touch it."

Rhea threw a Council evidence case over the burning glass. The case sealed. Black light hammered once against the lid and went dark. Inside remained one name and eleven empty slots. Across the room sat five incomplete copies made on a petition, history notes, food paper, Aira's notebook, and Maelin's bandage wrapper. The copies disagreed on two colors and three pulse orders.

They agreed children were there.

Nera looked at the mess of paper.

Nera: "Noctis will say the record is broken."

Rhea locked the evidence case.

President Valmont: "It is broken. We pulled it out while bleeding, off an enemy spell powered by captive kids. The damage is part of the proof."

Aira underlined the sentence.

Maelin finished binding Nera's shoulder and moved to Elira. Elira did not resist when the healer guided her onto the sofa, and that frightened me more than resistance would have.

Maelin: "You bought one strike. Your body charged interest."

Elira touched the blood at her lip.

Elira: "He felt it."

Maelin: "So did you. Only one of you is my patient."

Elira looked at me, furious that Lucien had made violence necessary and unwilling to let fury erase the cost.

Elira: "Record both."

Aira did. Then Rhea spoke.

President Valmont: "Recovery leave is over."

Elira looked at the silent crystal, then at me. Her eyes were gold, steady, alive, and furious.

Elira: "Then we go home."

---

Going home required paperwork. That felt obscene for several reasons and necessary for several worse ones.

Rhea did not let anyone rush for the carriages until she had three sealed records, two medical clearances, one Council travel objection, and Aira's handwritten list copied twice because the first copy had jam on the corner.

Aira: "History can survive fruit."

President Valmont: "History can survive legibility."

Aira copied it again.

Elira sat near the window while Maelin checked her pulse for the fourth time in ten minutes. Pale beneath her cloak with dried blood faintly tinting the corner of her mouth and every seventh heartbeat still skipping under Maelin's thumb, she kept both hands folded still and her breathing even so no clerk could mistake physical injury for broken will. Her pendant was quiet. Yet her gaze kept returning to the empty space where Lucien's black corridor had stood.

I saw it because I was watching too closely, then made myself look away before watching became another form of taking. Maelin noticed, of course.

Maelin: "Progress. Irritating, but progress."

Haru: "Was that for me?"

Maelin: "Unfortunately."

Elira's mouth moved toward a smile that did not quite arrive. I crossed the room slowly and stopped before I reached her chair.

Haru: "May I?"

The question changed the air, because the entire morning had been a machine designed to make asking feel theatrical. Elira looked up at me, her chin rising clear and deliberate.

Elira: "Yes."

I knelt beside her chair, wanting to be lower than the argument for once.

Haru: "I am sorry he used the archive."

Elira's fingers tightened once on the chair arm.

Elira: "He did not use the archive."

I waited. She looked toward the splintered Council frame on the mantle.

Elira: "He used the idea that private things become dirty when hostile people see them."

The room quieted around that. Aira stopped writing. Leon looked down. Cassian's expression lost its easy edge. Elira's voice stayed calm, each word chosen from somewhere painful and exact.

Elira: "The Moonlit Archive is still ours. Lake Velis is still ours. Last night is still ours. The fact that he tried to drag them through a trial does not make them his evidence."

I bowed my head in recognition.

Haru: "Then I will remember that before I get angry."

Aira: "Before?"

Haru: "During."

Elira touched my shoulder.

Elira: "Better."

The portable folding mirror beside the bread basket chimed, and every person in the room looked ready to destroy it. Senna's seal appeared in the small undamaged glass with visible strain lines.

Magistra Voss: "I am cutting in on an emergency witness line. It stays clean for about ninety seconds."

Rhea stepped into frame immediately.

President Valmont: "Report."

Magistra Voss: "Krail is trying to spin that attack as proof that Lake Velis triggers unstable old magic. I shut down the session before he could enter it into the record."

President Valmont: "Can he reopen?"

Magistra Voss: "Yes. Not today if I keep being professionally unpleasant."

Aira whispered from beside the table.

Aira: "Notebook Senna."

Rhea ignored her. Senna's eyes moved to me.

Magistra Voss: "Mr. Aerlen, the Council will ask why you did not destroy the hostile corridor when the trapped Noctis students appeared."

Haru: "Because I did not know what would happen to the students connected to it."

Magistra Voss: "Good. Say exactly that later. Do not improve it."

Elira almost smiled again. Senna looked at her.

Magistra Voss: "Miss Vale, the Council will ask whether the proximity trial altered your stated feelings toward Haru Aerlen."

Elira: "It clarified my anger."

Magistra Voss: "That is acceptable if followed by medical confirmation."

Maelin leaned toward the folding mirror.

Maelin: "Her anger is stable."

Magistra Voss: "Noted."

The small glass crackled, Senna's image distorting around the edges.

Magistra Voss: "One last point. Since locking down its main dorm wing after Cael's funeral, Noctis has now sealed the inner annex completely and blocked outside checks, claiming new magic contamination. Even without the scrap you took from the corridor, we managed to pick up partial crest traces on our own."

Nera, standing near the side hall with her bandaged shoulder and her re-riveted binding bands tucked beneath her sleeves, lifted her head.

Nera: "That means they moved students before sealing."

Darian's jaw tightened.

Magistra Voss: "We suspect so."

Nera's re-clasped metal bands clicked together as her hands curled into fists.

Nera: "Send the signatures. We need to match them before Noctis moves the routes again."

Magistra Voss: "Not yet. We have partial crest signatures."

President Valmont: "Nera."

Nera did not look away from the folding mirror.

Nera: "I know the conduit track. I know how they hide weak crests under training labels."

Senna studied her for half a second, then nodded.

Magistra Voss: "Through Aurelis protection channel only."

The folding mirror flashed. Twelve small lights appeared above the table, each one blurred where the name had been scrubbed away: Blue, Blue, Green, Red, Blue, Yellow, Green, Blue, Red, Blue, Yellow, Green. Twelve students, whose names had been rubbed thin enough that these lights had to stand in.

Nera approached them as if walking toward a grave. Darian stood beside her. Elira stood too. Maelin made an objection with her entire face, yet Elira ignored the face and did not cast. That was their compromise.

Nera touched the air beneath the first blue light. Her mouth tightened.

Nera: "First-year."

She moved to the second.

Nera: "Second-year. Binding-compatible."

At the third, green, Nera flinched.

Nera: "Too young for conduit track."

No one spoke. Then the seventh light pulsed weakly, green at the outer ring. Iven's name already existed on the stolen corridor slate, yet this was the first outside trace confirming the route independently of Lucien's own trap. Nera stared at it, matching it against the slate's seventh slot.

Nera: "That external pulse matches the seventh line-Iven's exact cadet cadence."

Darian: "How did the Council sweep catch his crest trace under masking?"

Nera's voice became very quiet.

Nera: "Cael once gave him a winter-drill thermal charm whose weave still leaves a faint blue-white shimmer under his Green crest."

Elira closed her eyes.

Haru: "Confirming Iven Sahl from outside."

Nera nodded once.

The seventh green light flickered blue-white at its core-echoing the nested blue-white glow beneath Green that Elira had spotted on the slate, though here it traced Cael's thermal charm rather than Noctis masking. Confirming his identity from the outside didn't free him, yet it made him harder to erase. Senna's image broke apart.

Magistra Voss: "Time's up. Get back to Aurelis. The academy has stronger wards against old magic than Lake Velis if Noctis tries this again."

President Valmont: "Under escort."

Magistra Voss: "Under witnesses."

The folding mirror went dark.

Nera remained beside the lights until they faded, then turned toward me. Fear showed in her face, directed at what she needed from me rather than at me.

Nera: "If Lucien uses them the way he used Cael..."

She could not finish. She did not need to. The Black Circle waited for my answer, and so did the room.

I wanted to promise impossible things: no one else will die, I will tear Noctis open, I will bring them all back. Every one of those promises had teeth. I made myself give the only answer that did not pretend I owned the future.

Haru: "We find the route first."

Nera's face twisted, steadied if not satisfied.

Haru: "Then we decide with witnesses present."

Elira's hand slipped into mine. This time no trial answered. Only the house, old and tired and perhaps a little relieved, releasing the door wards one by one for departure.

By the time we packed, the afternoon sky could not decide whether to rain. Elira changed into her formal white-and-navy academy uniform with gold trim, Professor Valen altering the collar quickly by hand so the crystal could sit visible at her throat over a pale cloak. I pulled on a plain black coat over my dark shirt. No one bothered pretending a Green crest still waited inside the lining.

Outside, Lake Velis shone dull silver while two Aurelis vehicles waited at the gate: a wide eight-seat council coach and a four-seat medical carriage. Rhea checked the travel seals, Maelin argued with the luggage because apparently even bags could be medically irresponsible, and Aira tried to organize everyone into a seating order that did not accidentally imply I was either prisoner or king.

Aira: "This is harder than it looks."

Leon: "No one thought it looked easy."

Aira: "Excellent. Then my suffering is visible."

Cassian leaned against the lead carriage door with his right arm tucked stiffly inside his coat, watching the lake.

Cassian: "Do we need a formation name?"

President Valmont: "No."

Cassian: "Witness diamond?"

President Valmont: "No."

Cassian: "Protective social rhombus?"

Leon: "That one offended geometry."

Elira stood beside me on the porch steps, wrapped in her pale cloak with the crystal visible at her throat. The wind moved her hair across her cheek. She did not fix it immediately, and that small delay brought back the bedroom, the morning, and how ordinary gestures turned heavy when the world kept trying to translate them into public risk.

I lifted my hand, then stopped. Elira glanced at me.

Elira: "You can move my hair."

Aira, already climbing into the carriage, made a strangled noise and turned away with excessive dignity.

I tucked the strand behind Elira's ear. The pendant did not flare. No trial opened. No ring sang. No Council crystal recorded the motion unless Aira was lying about looking away, which was possible. Elira's eyes softened.

Elira: "See?"

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "Practice knowing."

The phrase had become both wound and cure. I nodded.

At the bottom of the steps, Nera stood apart from the others with Darian beside her. She kept looking west, though Noctis was hidden beyond the hills, the twelve blurred crest signatures still weighing down her posture. Elira noticed too and walked down the steps before Maelin could object. I followed, not too close.

Nera straightened when Elira approached, old Noctis training still moving in her body after her mind had crossed the line. Elira did not comment on it.

Elira: "You are allowed to be afraid for them without becoming responsible for everything Noctis did."

Nera's mouth tightened.

Nera: "That sounds generous."

Elira: "It is not. It is practical. Guilt makes bad maps."

Darian looked at her then, surprised. Nera let out one breath that was almost a laugh and not one at all.

Nera: "Aira said something similar with worse phrasing."

Aira called from the carriage window.

Aira: "My phrasing survives under pressure."

President Valmont: "Your phrasing causes pressure."

Elira smiled faintly, then looked back at Nera.

Elira: "When we find them, you will see things you wish you had stopped earlier."

Nera's eyes shone.

Elira: "So will I."

Nera looked at the crystal at the place where Dominion had killed her. Elira did not hide it.

Elira: "We keep moving anyway."

Nera nodded once. No absolution, no forgiveness forced from the future, only direction.

Professor Valen climbed into the following medical carriage beside Maelin and the supply crates. When the rest of us entered the wide council coach, I sat beside Elira because pretending otherwise would give Krail's argument more respect than it deserved. Rhea, Nera, and Darian shared the facing bench with the evidence case and documents. Leon rode opposite me near the window, Aira wedged herself into the corner with her notebooks, and Cassian claimed the end seat nearest the door because he said it had the best dramatic exit potential. Outside on the box, the Aurelis driver told him to stop narrating.

As the restoration house receded behind us, Elira's hand found mine beneath the edge of her cloak, hidden from the road yet open to our witnesses. Aira saw and said nothing. That was how I knew she understood.

The carriage turned toward Aurelis, carrying the last warmth of Lake Velis into a world already preparing arguments against it.

The road back did not stay quiet.

At the first ridge marker, every carriage wheel locked. Wood screamed against the axle. Horses reared, and the driver shouted from the box as the carriage slewed sideways toward the drainage drop.

Leon hit the window with one palm. Water burst from the roadside ditch and braced the downhill wheels. Cassian reached for flame with his frost-darkened wrist. Nothing answered. He switched hands without comment and burned through the iron locking pin under the nearest axle.

Nera looked past them to the road marker. Its gold travel crystal had turned black around one sentence:

**RETURNING NOCTIS WITNESSES: HOLD FOR ORIGIN REVIEW**

Nera: "Do not break the marker. The hold transfers to the people named."

The carriage slid another foot. Elira tried to stand, and Maelin's remote medical seal flashed from the following carriage before her feet reached the floor. Elira sat back down with visible hatred.

Rhea threw open the door.

President Valmont: "Who can release the axle without answering origin?"

Aira was already halfway under the bench, pulling luggage straps free.

Aira: "No one releases it. We shift the weight, lift the locked wheels, and move the carriage past the marker without asking permission."

Leon: "That is your plan?"

Aira: "My plan is ropes. Develop criticism while tying one."

Darian and Leon looped the straps through the roof brace. Cassian cut the second pin. Rhea anchored the rope to a roadside cedar with her limited seal. Nera climbed onto the uphill step so the hold spell would keep tracking her instead of shifting to the medical carriage behind. The marker brightened around her name. She looked afraid, yet stayed on the step.

Haru: "Ready."

I took the rope with everyone else. No Black Circle: just shoulders, boots, wet leather, and six people pulling badly together.

The locked side of the carriage rose. The driver urged the horses forward. For one breath, the vehicle balanced on two wheels above the drop. Elira gripped the seat. Aira shouted left when she meant right, corrected herself, and no one died of the error. The carriage lurched beyond the marker and slammed back onto the road. The black hold vanished.

Nera jumped down after it cleared and nearly collapsed. Darian caught her injured side carefully. Cassian looked at his useless right wrist, then at the smoking pin he had cut with his left hand.

Cassian: "Heroics remain banned. Improvised road engineering appears legal."

Aira: "Barely."

Behind us, the marker returned to gold as if nothing had happened. Rhea copied the hostile sentence into her travel log. Before the carriage moved again, Nera scratched Iven's name into the harmless side of the road marker with a loose stone: proof that an origin hold had tried to stop witnesses from reaching someone Noctis had already hidden.

The gold crystal attempted to smooth the letters away. Cassian wedged the burned iron pin beneath the marker and jammed its cleaning charm.

Cassian: "Improvised road engineering. Still legal."

The name remained as we continued toward Aurelis.

For the first twenty minutes, the carriage held a silence full of people deciding which thoughts could survive being spoken aloud. Rain tapped lightly against the roof. The old house wards faded from my awareness one thread at a time until only Elira's pendant remained warm beside me.

Leon broke the quiet.

Leon: "I am going to ask something unfortunate."

Aira did not look up from her lap.

Aira: "That is your natural tone."

Leon ignored her and looked at me.

Leon: "If the Council orders you separated from Elira during the review, what happens?"

The carriage changed, because the question was useful. Elira's hand stayed in mine beneath the cloak. Rhea looked up from the document in her lap. Cassian stopped watching the road. Nera and Darian listened from the opposite bench as if the answer might teach them whether crossing from Noctis had truly meant entering a place where hard questions could be asked without punishment.

I considered the easy answer. *I won't allow it.* The Black Circle liked that answer. For that exact reason, I did not give it.

Haru: "I do not know."

Leon frowned, thinking it through.

Haru: "Separation after the Black Circle reveal is not the same as secrecy before it. Before the reveal, distance protected the secret. Now forced distance could repeat an old pattern: isolate the safeguard, call lockdown 'safety,' and leave fewer people able to challenge what happens next."

Rhea nodded once.

Haru: "But if I say separation is impossible, Krail argues Elira is necessary to my control and therefore compromised."

Elira's thumb moved once across my knuckles.

Haru: "If I accept separation too easily, Lucien argues witnesses are decorative."

Leon looked toward the rain-streaked window.

Leon: "So there is no clean answer."

Haru: "No."

Cassian leaned back.

Cassian: "There is rarely a clean answer. There is usually a best next inconvenience."

Aira pointed her pen at him.

Aira: "Do not accidentally become wise. It will ruin morale."

Cassian: "My apologies."

Elira spoke then.

Elira: "If they order separation, I answer first."

Rhea's eyes sharpened.

Elira: "Not Haru. Me."

Maelin, riding in the following carriage, was not present to object, though the air almost felt like it objected on her behalf. Elira continued anyway.

Elira: "They are framing this around whether I ruin Haru's control or he ruins my free will. I will not let them debate my presence while treating me like part of the scenery."

Nera's face changed with quiet recognition. Noctis had turned students into scenery all the time: useful pressure, a spare conduit, a moral lesson, a warning. Darian looked at Elira with respect sharpened by grief.

Darian: "They will say trauma makes your answer unreliable."

Elira: "Then Maelin answers second. As medical authority. Rhea third, as student protection. Aira fourth, because records survive things dignity cannot."

Aira placed a hand over her heart.

Aira: "I am moved and insulted."

Elira: "Good. Stay alert."

Rhea was already writing the order down. Leon looked at me again.

Leon: "And you?"

Haru: "I answer after."

That cost less to say than it would cost to do. Elira heard that too. She did not praise me; she squeezed my hand once. The rain grew heavier for a stretch, then began to break.

For a while, the carriage wheels made the only steady sound. Then Nera spoke.

Nera: "Noctis teaches that the first answer belongs to the highest authority in the room."

President Valmont: "Aurelis frequently teaches the same thing with better curtains."

Nera looked startled.

President Valmont: "We are not innocent. We are responsible."

The sentence settled over the carriage. I thought of Aurelis halls, rank seating, students stepping back from me, Green Circle observers learning to write because nobody had given them swords that counted.

Haru: "Responsibility is better than innocence."

Elira looked at me.

Haru: "Harder."

She smiled faintly.

Elira: "You would choose the harder word."

Haru: "I learned from someone severe."

Rhea looked up.

Elira: "He means me."

President Valmont: "I assumed."

The carriage reached the first outer Aurelis road marker in late afternoon as the clouds parted into pale, too-bright sunlight ahead of the valley. The marker's crystal lit as we passed, flickered black for one heartbeat, and settled into gold.

Everyone saw. No one panicked. Aira wrote it down. Leon watched the road. Cassian warmed the carriage with a left-handed heat charm while his right wrist remained wrapped and useless beneath his sleeve. Rhea sent a coded notice ahead. Elira kept holding my hand.

Returning to Aurelis would not be a single arrival. It would be a thousand small choices not to let old fear decide who spoke first.

## Coda: Heroics Banned

Cassian objected to the phrase heroics banned until further notice for exactly nine minutes. Aira timed him.

Cassian: "Some of us have branding."

Aira: "Some of us have casualty projections."

Leon: "You have branding?"

Cassian looked wounded.

Cassian: "I have presence."

Elira, pale against my shoulder, opened one eye.

Elira: "You have volume."

That ended the objection more effectively than policy. For a few breaths, the coach held laughter so fragile no one leaned on it. As the final valley curve brought Aurelis's eastern bridge towers into view between wet cedar slopes and cold afternoon glare, Nera kept naming possible students behind the twelve reserve lights until her voice frayed.

Cassian stopped joking first. That was how everyone knew the map had become real to him. He tapped Iven's name on Aira's sequence sheet with two fingers.

Cassian: "Fine. Heroics delayed."

Aira wrote it down.

Aira: "Progress."

===== EPISODE 21 =====

# Episode 21: **Return to the Academy**

Aurelis did not welcome us back. It braced.

The carriage crossed the eastern bridge in late afternoon beneath a sky too bright for the mood of the academy. Lake Velis fell behind us in silver flashes between cedar trunks, and the restoration house vanished into the ridge as if the mountain had folded a secret shut.

Elira sat beside me with her hands folded over the pendant.

She had changed into a formal white-and-navy academy uniform trimmed in gold. Professor Valen had altered the collar herself so the black crystal could rest visible at her throat when Elira chose, hidden when she did not. Today she wore it out in the open, an argument pinned right above her pulse. I wore black.

Green cloth felt like a lie I no longer had the patience to wear. Aira had looked at the coat once, looked at me, and kept her mouth shut. That silence told me plenty.

Leon rode opposite us, one knee bouncing until Rhea threatened to classify it as a hostile tremor.

Cassian leaned near the window, red hair catching the glare, eyes sharper than his smile. His right wrist stayed wrapped beneath his sleeve after the relay frost, every small reach favoring his left hand.

Nera sat across from him with her re-riveted Noctis binding bands hidden under plain cuffs and a fresh compression bandage crossing the shoulder Lucien's corridor had cut. Darian Thorne rode beside her, having slipped Noctis house arrest through Magistra Voss's emergency line before noon while Oric Sen held Aurelis's archive desk behind them, severed from Noctis in every way that mattered.

Aira had three notebooks open across her lap at once.

Haru: "That cannot be efficient."

Aira: "Efficiency is for people whose enemies do not weaponize footnotes."

Elira: "She has a point."

I looked toward Rhea.

President Valmont: "Do not drag me into this. I have four copies of the same emergency order because three different offices will try to misplace it."

The carriage wheels struck the paved academy road. My sternum tightened.

Old Aurelis magic rose from beneath the stones to meet me: cold pressure, ozone, and copper. Alert, waiting to see what stepped onto its tiles.

The academy knew the Black Circle had come back through its gates. So did everyone else.

Students lined the outer road despite Rhea's crowd order. Some leaned from upper balconies. Some crowded behind window glass. Others pretended to study notice crystals while staring so hard their wrist mana flickered.

Green Circle students clustered near the lower fountain steps. Mira Castellan stood at the front, curly auburn hair tied back and a notebook hugged to her chest. Finn hovered beside her clutching a bundle of scrolls with an expression of pure scholarly terror, while Pella, another Green records aide, gripped her slate like a buckler.

When our carriage rolled past, nobody cheered. I was grateful for that.

Then a Green Circle boy I did not recognize placed one hand over his crest and bowed, brief and unshowy, just enough to say he had seen the record and knew seeing was not owning.

Others followed. Green first, then Blue, then a handful of Red. No Yellow students moved.

Then Soren Ashvale, standing under the visiting school arch in Valemere colors, touched two fingers to his scarred hand and gave a formal duelist bow. That broke the freeze.

Elira's hand found mine on the seat.

Elira: "Breathe."

Haru: "I am."

Aira: "Barely."

I drew a full breath and let the Black Circle stay quiet beneath my skin.

Instructor Dren met us at the main gate, wearing the exact stern scowl he brought to every morning drill. After everything else, his predictability felt almost like mercy.

Instructor Dren: "Aerlen."

Haru: "Instructor."

Dren looked me up and down.

Instructor Dren: "You are taller when everyone stops pretending not to look."

Cassian choked on a laugh. Dren ignored him completely.

Elira stepped down beside me, and Dren's eyes flicked from the pendant to her face.

Instructor Dren: "Vale."

Elira: "Instructor."

Instructor Dren: "Medical restrictions?"

Maelin materialized behind him with a healer's satchel and the posture of judgment given legs.

Maelin: "No heavy magic, no standing through endless hearings, no playing martyr, no duels, and no pretending that holding your temper counts as rest."

Elira: "I agreed to most of those."

Maelin: "You agreed to all of them."

Dren grunted.

Instructor Dren: "Good. Then you will both hate the next hour."

He turned toward the central courtyard.

Rhea's emergency authority had cleared the main path into a witness corridor. Student Council officers stood at intervals beneath hovering faculty wards. At the far end beside the great fountain, Magistra Senna's Council seal burned over the stone, carrying the sharp bite of ink and cold granite.

The repaired fountain no longer rippled backward. It watched normally now, which somehow put my teeth on edge. Professor Halden waited beside its rim, his hair noticeably more silver than it had been before Cael's funeral. His hands were empty, which made him look twice as dangerous.

Haru: "Professor."

Professor Halden: "Aerlen."

His gaze shifted to Elira.

Professor Halden: "Vale."

Elira: "Professor."

All our tangled history hung between us: his early suspicion, my concealment, the old observatory, and his decision not to lock me in a cell when he had the chance.

Professor Halden: "I have been asked to lead Aurelis's internal watch on the Black Circle."

Leon muttered under his breath.

Leon: "That sounds comforting."

Halden's eyes cut toward him. Leon straightened.

Professor Halden: "It is not meant to comfort."

Aira: "Spectacular. We are doomed by branding."

Halden let the remark pass, though his jaw twitched.

Professor Halden: "I refused twice. The first request from the board called it classification. The second, from High Councilor Krail's office, called it containment readiness. I accepted only after Magistra Voss rewrote the orders."

President Valmont: "Witness stability."

Professor Halden: "My task is to record whether Haru Aerlen remains answerable under pressure, not to decide what he is."

I studied his face.

Haru: "And if I do not?"

Halden's mouth hardened.

Professor Halden: "Then I record that too, with witnesses standing beside you, before anyone turns fear into a locked room."

It was the closest thing to trust Halden could afford. I took it.

Above the fountain, Senna's remote seal flared open.

Magistra Voss: "Aurelis, report."

President Valmont stepped forward, crisp as flint.

President Valmont: "Haru Aerlen, Elira Vale, and registered witnesses have returned under escort. No Black Circle outbreak on the road. One Noctis hold trap at the outer ridge marker was bypassed and logged. From Lake Velis, we matched the seventh slot on Nera's stolen slate to Iven Sahl."

Magistra Voss: "Confirmed on our end as well. Drakenshard and Valemere have sealed their student registries. Three minor academies report unauthorized relay pings. Noctis Dominion College has refused our conduit audit."

Color drained from Nera's face. Darian's fists clenched at his sides.

Magistra Voss: "After Noctis's delegation returned from Cael's funeral and locked their dormitory wing, eleven conduit-track students stopped answering roll. Overnight, Iven Sahl was taken from Aurelis's dissenting guest wing. That makes twelve living students on the board."

The courtyard went dead quiet. Eleven taken inside Noctis's locked wing after the funeral, and Iven pulled from Aurelis's dissenting wing overnight. Twelve living students on Lucien's board.

Nera stepped into the seal's light.

Nera: "Then our slate read true."

Magistra Voss inclined her head once.

Darian: "Magistra."

Magistra Voss: "Both counts align. Eleven Noctis-wing transfers, plus Iven Sahl."

The name hit like a second blow on an unhealed bruise. I remembered Iven from Cael's funeral: pale, first-year, standing in the separate Noctis cluster, holding onto a story about a borrowed thermal charm as proof Cael had been kind when nobody was watching.

Elira's pendant warmed against her throat.

Haru: "Lucien showed us reserves."

Professor Halden: "Say that again."

I laid it out for Halden and Dren slowly: the Noctis corridor, the hanging crest lights, Nera stepping one body-length into the dark, the slate she tore free, and Lucien's single word. Reserves.

By the time I finished, Dren's knuckles were white, Maelin had stopped pretending she was only here to monitor Elira, and President Valmont's council sigil burned dark crimson.

Magistra Voss: "Then the Council has probable cause for a protective audit of Noctis."

High Councilor Krail's voice sliced across the projection.

High Councilor Krail: "The Council has cause to lock down the unclassified student who provoked Lucien Voss into threatening children."

The fountain water flattened into glass. Krail's image formed beside Senna's, sharp and unwelcome.

High Councilor Krail: "Do not confuse timing with innocence. Voss is a criminal, and Aerlen is the excuse criminals are rallying around."

Elira stepped forward. Maelin hissed a warning, but Elira kept her hands still and let her voice carry.

Elira: "No. Lucien organized cruelty long before Haru stepped into public view. Talen Mire proves it. Cael proves it. Nera and Oric prove it. Noctis' buried doctrine proves it. You do not get to blame Haru for the rot his exposure dragged into the light."

High Councilor Krail: "Miss Vale, you remain under trauma review."

Elira's smile had frost on it.

Elira: "And you remain determined not to hear what the trauma actually points to."

Murmurs rippled through the courtyard, tight with anger in Elira's favor. Krail heard them. His expression stayed smooth, yet Red Circle pressure slipped through the remote seal like a blade testing silk.

The Black Circle answered under my ribs, hungry and cold. I pinned it down before it broke surface.

Halden's eyes snapped to my chest.

Haru: "Recorded?"

Halden swallowed once.

Professor Halden: "Recorded."

Krail smiled thinly.

High Councilor Krail: "How cooperative."

A sharp crack split the air.

A black fracture tore vertically down the fountain's water column from rim to basin. Too old for Lucien's frost, too deliberate for stray mana. Gold-black letters burned across the mist above the stone.

**CIRCLE ZERO SAFEGUARD REVIEW: FIELD RESPONSE REQUIRED**

Mira's notebook hit the paving stones. Another line scrolled beneath the first.

**DOMINION ROUTE DETECTED BELOW ACADEMY INFRASTRUCTURE**

Professor Valen's hand froze over her slate.

Professor Halden: "Impossible."

President Valmont: "Explain impossible quickly."

Professor Valen: "Noctis should have zero access to the lower observatory after the Foundation locks."

The fountain mist answered before she finished.

**ACCESS POINT: OLD TOURNAMENT MEDICAL ANNEX**

Nera flinched as if struck.

Nera: "That is where conduit-track students were evaluated before matches."

Darian: "Where Cael was prepared."

Panic in the courtyard sharpened into direction. Lucien hadn't only stolen students in Noctis. He had left a hook buried under Aurelis itself, inside the wing where visiting students were supposed to be safe.

Dren pivoted toward the lower path.

Instructor Dren: "Combat team."

Leon rolled his shoulders. Cassian bared his teeth in a joyless grin, left hand curling into a fist. Aira snapped two notebooks shut and kept the third open. Rhea fired off three perimeter orders before anyone else drew breath.

Elira stepped up beside me.

Maelin: "Absolutely not."

Elira: "I won't cast anything heavy."

Maelin: "You are walking straight into a Dominion route."

Elira: "I know what I am walking into."

Maelin's eyes narrowed.

Maelin: "That is not a medical exemption."

I looked down at Elira. The trial's last condition still echoed inside my ribs: if she asks as herself, with the risk named plainly, then yes.

Haru: "She comes if she chooses."

Maelin glared at me as if torn between fury and reluctant respect. Elira's knuckles brushed mine once, brief and grounding, then we turned toward the old medical annex under a hundred watching eyes.

---

The first person to break formation and follow us was Mira.

She ran three steps, caught herself because sprinting after an emergency escort looked like panic, and settled into a brisk walk with Finn and Pella half a pace behind her.

Rhea spotted them without turning around.

President Valmont: "Castellan."

Mira stopped short.

Mira: "President Valmont."

President Valmont: "This route is restricted."

Mira flushed, glanced at me and Elira, then back toward the glowing warning still fading above the fountain.

Mira: "Then restrict me properly."

Finn sucked in a breath as if he had just watched a friend step off a roof. Aira's brows shot up. Rhea turned slowly.

Mira held her notebook tighter, hands trembling, voice steady.

Mira: "Green Circle students have been used as audience, rumor, and cover since this started. Our notes mattered in the Foundation gallery when nobody else bothered to write down what mercy looked like. If Noctis dug a route under our own floors because no one important watches ordinary students first, then you need someone ordinary on the record."

The courtyard went still. Even Dren waited.

Mira: "I am not asking to fight Lucien. I would die in three seconds and embarrass everyone. I am asking to witness what happens to students who are easy to ignore."

Finn raised one shaking hand beside her.

Finn: "I can index erased records."

Rhea turned her glare on him. Finn looked like he deeply regretted existing, yet Pella stepped up beside him and raised her slate an inch higher.

Finn: "Quietly."

Pella: "We can keep count."

Aira's mouth softened with something close to pride. Rhea checked Dren.

Instructor Dren: "Behind the combat line."

Maelin: "Behind my medical line."

Professor Halden: "Where nobody can claim their notes were tampered with."

Aira: "That is three different lines and none of you drew a map."

President Valmont: "Then you are drawing it."

Aira: "I regret being competent."

Mira's shoulders dropped an inch, tension settling into focus. Rhea stepped forward and pressed a coin-sized crimson council seal onto Mira's notebook cover, then onto Finn's scroll strap and Pella's slate.

President Valmont: "You are not down there to prove bravery, or to turn Green Circle students into martyrs. You leave the instant Dren, Maelin, Aira, or I give the word."

Mira: "Understood, President."

Finn tucked his scrolls tight under one arm and straightened his posture.

Finn: "Understood."

Aira leaned down toward him.

Aira: "If I tell you to leave in a very polite voice, sprint."

Finn: "That sounds backwards."

Leon: "It is not."

The second interruption came from a Yellow Circle senior in spotless white and gold, wearing the bright certainty of someone who thought emergencies were stages for rebuilding reputation.

Senior: "If the Black Circle is active on academy grounds, the Yellow Circle should be represented."

Elira turned slowly. The senior lost half his color.

Elira: "Represented for whom?"

Senior: "For senior student oversight."

Elira: "No."

The senior tried to look past her at me. Elira stepped squarely into his sightline.

Elira: "If you want to be useful, report to shelter coordination and keep first-years away from rumor crystals."

Senior: "I am a Yellow Circle..."

Elira: "So am I. Rank is not usefulness. Go be useful."

The senior retreated, stiff at first, then considerably faster once Maelin looked at him.

Haru: "You enjoyed that."

Elira: "A little."

Haru: "Good."

She blinked, then smiled despite the warning script, the twelve missing kids, and the dark annex waiting ahead. That small spark didn't erase the dread, yet it reminded us what we were walking down to protect.

At the eastern colonnade, the crowd thinned to faculty aides, council runners, and students pretending to have errands near the restricted wing. Nobody bowed here. They watched.

One Blue Circle boy took a single step backward as I passed.

My chest tightened, though the Black Circle stayed still. Elira saw it and kept her hands at her sides, honoring our rule.

A small Green Circle girl by the colonnade pillar saw the boy flinch. Fear crossed her face, followed fast by fierce, reckless fairness.

Girl: "He saved Cael."

The Blue student flushed. I stopped walking, and the whole escort stopped with me.

I met the girl's eyes.

Haru: "I tried to."

The correction cut across the colonnade. The girl blinked, confused.

Elira knelt smoothly despite Maelin's quiet grunt of protest.

Elira: "Cael saved me. Haru tried to save him before that. Both are true."

Girl: "But Cael still died."

Elira's gold eyes never wavered, alive because of the boy we were still learning how to mourn without turning him into a speech.

Elira: "He did."

The girl looked back up at me.

Girl: "Are you angry?"

Every adult in the colonnade went silent. I thought about giving her a neat, harmless lie, then decided she deserved the truth without theatrics.

Haru: "I am. But anger does not get to give orders."

The words felt strange coming out of my mouth, less like advice and more like a guardrail I needed for myself. The girl nodded with solemn gravity, then took one step aside, clearing the path without shrinking away.

The Blue student looked down in quiet shame. I didn't absolve him, and I didn't glare at him. Fear wasn't a crime. We kept walking.

At the annex gate, Lady Seraphine Morn waited in tactical black with red trim, hair pulled tight, one hand resting against the iron gate ward.

Cassian straightened immediately.

Lady Seraphine: "Veyr."

Cassian: "Lady Morn."

Lady Seraphine shifted her gaze to me.

Lady Seraphine: "Aerlen."

Haru: "Lady Morn."

Her eyes swept Elira, the crystal at her collar, and the column behind us.

Lady Seraphine: "The gate holds three clashing locks: medical archive, tournament authority, and visiting custody. Whoever rigged it wanted investigators arguing on the steps."

President Valmont: "Can you open it?"

Lady Seraphine: "I can."

President Valmont: "Cleanly?"

A faint edge touched Seraphine's mouth.

Lady Seraphine: "No."

Dren stepped up beside her, hand on his hilt.

Instructor Dren: "Then open it loudly."

Seraphine pressed her palm flat to the ward. Sharp Red Circle light flared around her fingers. Dren laid his combat seal beside it, Rhea locked her council mark above both, and Valen threaded older Aurelis script beneath the hinge. Halden refused to let the gate unlatch without reading every syllable between the wards as it broke.

Aira scribbled every layer down while Mira watched wide-eyed.

Finn whispered to Aira.

Finn: "The verbs are not boring."

Aira: "Then make the nouns work harder."

The iron gate groaned inward. Cold antiseptic herbs and dried ink drifted out of the stairwell, stale as an inspection report nobody ever meant to read aloud.

Elira's fingers brushed mine once before we stepped over the threshold. I walked down as Haru Aerlen, and the Black Circle followed behind my ribs, answerable for every inch.

---

The annex did not welcome us all at once. It sorted us by color.

Green. Blue. Red. Yellow. Black.

The gate crystal lit each circle in order until it reached me, where it failed and left a dark ring around my wrist, an empty space where old Aurelis classification refused to name what the courtyard had already seen.

Halden leaned over the crystal.

Professor Halden: "Interesting."

Aira: "Professor, please stop calling ominous traps interesting while we are standing inside them."

Professor Halden: "Would you prefer I find them dull?"

Leon: "Frankly, yes."

Leon shifted his weight forward, shoulders squared. Halden ignored him, which remained his favorite teaching tool.

Valen touched the crystal rim with one gloved finger.

Professor Valen: "It is not hiding him."

President Valmont: "Then what is it doing?"

Professor Valen: "Refusing to log him under medical custody."

The annex crystal hunted my wrist for the shattered Green crest it used to log, struck only the dark hairline scar beneath my skin, and spat out a blank error bar. Haru Aerlen stayed unlisted.

Being unclassifiable wasn't freedom. Things outside a ledger were usually where cages got built.

Elira studied the dim stone instead of touching her pendant.

Elira: "Log that the annex failed to classify Haru without asking him to perform."

President Valmont: "Logged."

Halden's pen scratched fast. Seraphine watched me with a soldier's sharp eye.

Lady Seraphine: "Can you still move?"

Haru: "I can."

I held her gaze without flinching, grateful she hadn't wasted breath asking if I felt fine.

Ten paces down the hall, a glass case held rows of visiting tournament clearance badges. Each carried a school seal, a color band, and a thin strip for medical notes. Most were blank.

One was not.

Nera stopped so fast Darian nearly walked into her.

The badge was Noctis white. Someone had scraped the student's name raw off the bone strip, leaving only the health note inked cleanly beneath:

**CONDUIT CANDIDATE RESPONSIVE TO EXTERNAL CROWN PRESSURE**

Nobody breathed. Crown language didn't belong in a modern tournament file, not unless someone had been testing older Dominion tools under Aurelis's roof.

Valen went pale in the way scholars did when a modern nightmare turned up an older footnote.

Professor Halden: "Professor."

Professor Valen: "Crown pressure isn't a tournament term."

Lady Seraphine: "Noctis?"

Professor Valen: "Or something Noctis dug up and copied."

The glass shuddered. A faint blue-white line bled across the scraped name strip.

Nera whispered into the glass.

Nera: "Iven."

Darian: "Are you sure?"

Nera shook her head, then stopped herself.

Nera: "No. I am afraid."

Mira stepped closer, the red observer seal glowing on her notebook cover.

Mira: "They scrubbed his name and kept his function. That means the room cared what he could carry, not who he was."

The glass cracked down the center. Old record magic hated being called out plainly.

Finn stared at the hairline split, swallowing hard.

Finn: "Someone deleted the name on purpose while leaving the use-tag intact. The erasure left a seam."

Aira's pen flashed across the page.

Aira: "Documented. Moving."

At the next turn, rough corridor stone gave way to white infirmary tile, easy to scrub clean. The air turned frigid. Shoulder-high brackets lined the walls where monitoring crystals once sat. Leon touched the nearest bracket, and condensation immediately beaded over his fingertips.

Leon: "Used recently."

Lady Seraphine: "How recently?"

Leon closed his eyes, blue light tracing his wrist.

Leon: "After the funeral."

The sentence landed like a bolt sliding shut behind us. Somebody hadn't just left old traps down here. Someone had worked this wing after Cael was buried, while the Council thought Noctis was frozen.

Rhea's voice dropped to ice.

President Valmont: "Pull every Aurelis internal access log."

Aira flipped a page.

Aira: "Requesting now."

President Valmont: "No. Seizing now. This entire wing is under student protection evidence hold."

Seraphine's mouth curved faintly.

Lady Seraphine: "Aggressive."

President Valmont: "Necessary."

Up ahead, Dren raised one fist. Everyone froze.

From down the tiled hall came a steady scrape. Porcelain against metal. Spoon against bowl. Once. Twice. Three times.

Mira's face went white.

Mira: "Why is that worse than screaming?"

Maelin, who had marched straight down through the gate despite swearing earlier she wouldn't touch ancient nonsense, answered quietly.

Maelin: "Because someone is trying to make captivity sound domestic."

Elira's eyes hardened. Dren didn't wait for speeches; he drew his blade low and walked straight toward the sound. We followed at his heels.

---

The spoon sound stopped at a tiled vestibule whose walls were covered in layered inscriptions. Beyond a heavy ajar door lay the first examination room.

Halden ran his gaze across the wall script.

Professor Halden: "These were altered."

Professor Valen: "No. Overwritten. Older Aurelis grammar sits underneath. Noctis just traced over the scar."

Cold settled deeper behind my ribs.

Haru: "This wing connects to Circle Zero."

Valen glanced back at me.

Professor Valen: "It may connect straight to the failure."

Dren pushed the heavy door wide, and we stepped into the first examination room. Its brass lintel plate read:

**VISITING STUDENT RECOVERY ROOM - CROWN FIELD BLOCK**

Cael had been locked inside here between preliminary Noctis evaluations before the Crown Field match. The stone didn't have feelings, yet mana remembered habits, and this room had been trained by fear. Too many iron anchor rings bolted beneath the bed frame. Too many drain sigils masked as healer monitors.

Valen stopped dead on the threshold, refusing to set foot inside until Dren and Maelin had swept the room. Even then, Nera stayed by the overwritten wall near the doorway, pressing two fingers lightly to the tile.

Nera: "Noctis teams were told Aurelis demanded extra readings after cross-school matches."

Darian: "And Noctis handlers stayed to supervise."

Leon: "So Noctis used Aurelis infirmary rooms to prep conduits?"

Nera's jaw tightened.

Nera: "They did."

Mira's pen scratched loud across her paper. Aira leaned over her shoulder.

Aira: "Dates, room number, witnesses. Keep the verbs boring. Boring verbs survive court."

Beneath the bed, Lucien's first trap exhaled.

Ink-thin black rings slid across the white tile toward the doorway, straight at Mira and Pella. I surged forward, then checked myself as Elira's fingers caught my sleeve. She wasn't holding me back. She was reminding me I wasn't alone.

Leon moved first. Three ribbons of water snapped from his crest, sweeping under the ink rings to lift the floor film and break their grip on the tile. Cassian followed with a thread of red flame from his left hand, his wrapped right wrist braced tight against his ribs, burning the feed current in the air above the rings rather than the rings themselves.

Aira pointed straight left.

Aira: "Third wall bracket!"

Dren's blade shattered the iron bracket before I finished turning. The black rings vanished in a puff of cold ash.

The Black Circle stayed quiet beneath my coat. Everyone looked at me anyway, then let out a collective breath.

Leon scowled at the relief on their faces.

Leon: "Obviously that worked."

Cassian clapped his shoulder with his good hand.

Cassian: "Careful, Varek. Smile any harder and you will ruin your brand."

Leon: "I hate every one of you."

Elira laughed softly, and the room felt one fraction less like a tomb.

Just beyond the recovery room, an open stone arch led into a lower side chamber where twelve slate tablets hovered over a cracked stone basin. Each tablet listed a crest color, age, conduit rating, and route susceptibility. The name lines had been scorched clean, yet old record magic kept flaring dimly around the blanks.

Finn stepped up to the basin without waiting for orders, scrolls tucked tight.

Finn: "Whoever wiped them used a set pattern. I cannot pull the names back cleanly without tripping a backlash, yet I can prove twelve active student files were erased on purpose."

Aira clicked her tongue in approval.

Aira: "Boring proof wins trials."

Nera hovered near the seventh tablet, pointing with a trembling hand at a faint blue-white shimmer clinging to the blank space.

Nera: "Winter-drill weave. Cael built a thermal charm like this for Iven."

Darian looked away, throat working. Elira stepped up beside Nera.

Elira: "Then he is in the record. That is where we start pulling him out."

Nera blinked back tears and gave one sharp nod.

Behind Finn's basin, the rear wall parted smoothly without anyone touching a stone. Lucien wanted us looking inside.

A wide circular room dropped half a flight below the annex floor, older than the corridors above. Seven chairs ringed a sunken relay well, each fitted with white metal and black thread restraints. Above the well hung twelve small crest lights, ghostly hooks waiting to yank twelve missing students straight through Aurelis's own magic lines the second the right trigger dropped.

The Black Circle slammed upward so hard the wall sconces guttered dark.

Elira stepped straight in front of me, meeting my eyes, never flinching from what lived inside my chest.

Elira: "Haru."

I froze. If she asks as herself. She was standing there as herself, and I stopped.

Lucien's smooth voice floated up from the sunken well.

Lucien: "Touching. He takes a leash well."

Elira's face turned to carved marble.

Elira: "He listens. There is a difference."

Lucien: "In desperate women, the two look remarkably alike."

The jab was aimed at her, yet it struck the whole room. Aira's pen stopped dead. Rhea's council seal flared crimson. Maelin looked ready to figure out how to slap a man through a relay mirror.

My anger rose clean and sharp, entirely mine. Lucien believed that lie down to his marrow: that love under fear was weakness begging for hierarchy.

Elira didn't glance back for my permission.

Elira: "You keep mistaking fear for inferiority because you have never understood how people act when they are terrified and still refuse to yield."

Lucien: "Fear narrows choice."

Elira: "Of course it does. Pain narrows choice. Institutions narrow choice. That is why consent under pressure has to be guarded instead of mocked. You manufacture the pressure, wait for someone's knees to buckle, and call their collapse proof that you own them."

A faint chime rang through the ancient stone beneath our feet.

Valen caught her breath.

Professor Valen: "That line."

Professor Halden: "I heard it."

Lucien's image stayed composed, yet frost crept harder up the rim of the relay well. Elira had struck the structural pin.

Lucien: "And you dress interference up as affection."

Elira: "I use affection as a reason to stay present while asking better questions."

She raised one hand toward the twelve crest lights.

Elira: "First: who benefits if Haru acts alone?"

The black threads strung from the well shivered.

Aira answered first, cold and quick.

Aira: "Lucien."

President Valmont: "Krail's containment bloc."

Professor Halden: "Anyone looking for one hidden weapon to blame instead of a rotting system."

Nera: "Noctis."

Elira: "Second: who benefits if Haru does nothing?"

Leon: "Lucien."

Mira: "Whoever holds the missing students right now."

Finn: "The erasure ledger."

Elira: "Then neither alone nor nothing works. Third: who is present enough to refuse?"

Light bloomed gently along the ancient floor seams, warm enough to remind the circular room it had once been built for healing before someone turned it into a trap. The cold weight behind my sternum shifted.

Haru: "Everyone here."

Lucien's lip curled.

Lucien: "A crowd is not a chain of command."

President Valmont: "Correct."

Aira: "Try to keep up."

Leon muttered under his breath.

Leon: "Stop baiting the remote sadist."

Cassian: "Let her work."

Lucien's patience snapped. Frost slammed outward across the well, dimming all twelve lights.

Silver-gold archive threads gathered around Professor Valen's hands instead-while Elira kept her own fingers still, guiding the anchor questions solely through the cold shimmer of her remade pendant with zero Yellow spark.

Maelin: "Watch both channels, Valen. Not one drop from Vale."

Professor Valen: "My channels, not hers."

Seven silver-gold needles lanced out from Valen's palms and pinned the air around the well, exposing the black grammar threads binding each light to the seven chairs. Each thread carried a glowing label: Obedience, Return, Proof, Reserve, Use, Property, Final.

Cael's last note had rejected every one of those words.

Darian swore softly. Nera's plain cuffs split open as her re-clasped Noctis binding rings flared blue-gray, snapping around the threads. She did not sever them; she indexed them, carrying every lesson she and Oric had survived.

Nera: "Thread one hooks into Noctis' dormitory basement. Thread two links to delegation mirror residue. Thread three..."

Her voice cracked.

Elira: "Nera."

Nera swallowed hard.

Nera: "Thread three runs straight through Cael's old conduit scar."

Lucien had built his bridge out of the open wound Aurelis left behind after Cael died. The Black Circle surged at my feet, eager to wipe the whole chamber out of existence. I held it down as a thin ring of shadow around my boots.

Haru: "How do we drop the hooks without dragging the kids through?"

Professor Valen: "Split the weight."

Professor Halden: "Dangerous. Each hook is built to bait one strong mage into grabbing it. If Haru grabs them all, Lucien claims Black Circle takeover. If we slash them blindly, the students eat the backlash."

Leon rolled his neck.

Leon: "So we each carry a piece."

Halden blinked at him.

Leon: "What? I listen sometimes."

Cassian: "Mark the calendar."

Instructor Dren: "Focus."

Witness magic hated secrecy, so we broke the circuit right in front of Lucien's eyes. Leon drowned Obedience beneath flowing water so it couldn't lock. Cassian scorched Return at the edges without touching the names underneath. Rhea pinned Proof under strict council law. Aira dissected Reserve in ink until the word looked obscene. Mira gripped her pen with trembling hands and wrote along the glowing air beside Use: a person cannot be a function. Finn wrapped Property in his seam-tracking marks. Nera held Final, tears running down her cheeks while her rings bit deep.

Professor Valen anchored the center with her seven silver-gold needles while Elira held the anchor cadence steady through her pendant alone. I stayed on the outer ring, hands empty.

Lucien: "Still hiding from yourself, Aerlen."

Haru: "Still hiding behind children, Voss."

Frost cracked sharply inside the well. Halden caught it instantly.

Professor Halden: "He is holding these hooks on pride as much as craft."

Lucien: "Your ambition is showing, Professor."

Professor Halden: "Good. It means I am still a flawed man, not a doctrine pretending to be clean."

One by one, the threads parted. Obedience dissolved in Leon's water. Return unraveled in Cassian's flame. Proof buckled, Reserve emptied, Use snapped as Mira's hand steadied, and Property cracked under Finn's ledger script.

Final fought back.

Nera screamed as the seventh thread turned pitch black and yanked inward, trying to turn her re-clasped binding rings into a fresh conduit tether. Darian lunged and caught her shoulders. Maelin cursed, Professor Valen's silver-gold net flared to hold the perimeter, and I crossed the ring in two strides.

Nobody tried to stop me this time.

I set one palm above the black thread and opened the Black Circle solely as a boundary: a wall with a door cut through it.

Haru: "Final does not belong to you."

Lucien: "Then whose is it?"

I looked straight at Nera, shaking, furious, and still standing.

Nera: "Nobody's."

The seventh thread shattered.

Eleven crest lights shot upward through the ceiling and scattered back into the wider relay net, free of Aurelis' traps.

One light stayed behind. Small, pale green beneath a blue-white shimmer-Iven Sahl's trace.

Instead of rising, it darted sideways toward a low stone archway beside the recovery room stairs, opening into an old service tunnel.

Leon stepped forward.

Leon: "That pulse is local. Right underneath us."

Dren drew his blade clean. Cassian raised a left-handed flame.

Lucien's whisper drifted up out of the empty well, soft and poisonous.

Lucien: "One left, then. Let us see what the Black Circle does with a boy who still belongs to Noctis."

---

Nobody charged the tunnel mouth. That single choice kept us alive.

The blue-white pulse shivered at the edge of the dark, followed by a thin sound like breath trapped inside glass. Every protective instinct in my chest lunged toward it. Elira stepped half a pace closer, close enough for the pendant to raise its silent question between us: were we answering the boy, or a trap shaped like him?

Haru: "Both."

Elira: "Then we take them apart piece by piece."

Rhea's council seal flared beside the low archway.

President Valmont: "Protocol first."

Leon stared at her as if the word had slapped him.

President Valmont: "Yes, Varek, even now."

Aira was already writing.

Aira: "Especially now. Protocol is how we stop Haru from becoming a tragic solution with good cheekbones."

Cassian glanced at me.

Cassian: "Harsh, though fair."

Haru: "Fair is enough."

Leon's mouth twitched into a brief, crooked grin, and the tension eased just enough for people to think straight.

Valen knelt at the tunnel threshold and held a strip of archive vellum over the opening. The edge browned without catching fire. Halden crouched across from her, his slate hovering over the floor sigils as his fingers traced the diagram's border on the stone.

Professor Halden: "Three layers. First, a distress lure keyed to familiar names. Second, a lock spell waiting for anyone trying to pull him out. Third..."

He paused, frowning as broken old circles glowed beneath the Noctis hooks.

Professor Halden: "The tunnel predates the annex. Noctis wove doctrine through it, yet they did not lay the foundation."

Valen's eyes sharpened.

Professor Valen: "Tournament annexes were built on top of older recovery halls. If this began as a pre-Circle witness infirmary..."

Elira finished the thought quietly.

Elira: "Then rescue lived down here before anyone sorted students into ranks."

Mira stepped close to Halden's diagram, still pale from holding Use.

Mira: "Can the older magic help us?"

Valen laid her palm flat on the floor stone outside the tunnel.

Professor Valen: "Aurelis witness inquiry. We are not claiming patient custody. We are checking whether a living student is below and whether the path holds active traps."

The older floor circles flared gold. The Noctis hooks overhead jerked tight. Somewhere down in the dark, a muffled sound broke loose, a child fighting not to cry out.

The Black Circle surged in my chest. Instead of burying it, I forced it out onto my wrist as a thin rotating band of black and silver, open for every witness in the room to watch.

Haru: "Boundary only."

Halden's pen moved instantly.

Professor Halden: "Minimal cast. Witnessed. Purpose: boundary."

Dren kept his eyes on the dark tunnel.

Instructor Dren: "Useful."

He caught the weight of his own word and added quietly.

Instructor Dren: "By choice."

Leon stepped up to the mouth and sent a thin ribbon of water creeping along the stone floor, sliding cleanly around each white hook without brushing it.

Leon: "There are pressure plates. Emotional ones."

Aira looked up from her page. Leon scowled.

Leon: "I heard how it sounded. Keep writing."

The water ribbon touched the edge of the first hook, and a boy's thin whisper drifted back along the current.

Iven: "I didn't mean to be cold."

Nera clapped both hands over her mouth. Darian's eyes went flat with murder.

Leon shifted the water from a line into a shallow cup, holding the echo in place without letting the hook drag it back to trigger the trap.

Leon: "First hook runs on guilt."

Finn marked his scroll fast.

Finn: "Guilt lure logged. No custody transfer."

The white hook dimmed. Down the narrow throat of the tunnel, five more hooks lit in sequence like poisoned lanterns: Cold. Hunger. Shame. Obedience. Gratitude.

At the last word, Nera trembled violently.

Nera: "They drill gratitude into us as debt."

Darian gave one short, grim nod from beside her.

Elira crouched at the threshold and spoke gently into the dark.

Elira: "Iven Sahl, if you hear me, you owe nobody pain for warmth you were given."

The blue-white trace steadied and drifted a single inch closer. Alive. Listening.

Lucien's voice slid back through the cold air, thinner now.

Lucien: "How slow you are. Children suffer while you polish your scruples."

The hook named Gratitude flared bright. He wanted speed. He wanted panic to turn rescue into seizure.

Elira looked straight into the blackness.

Elira: "Children suffer because you built rooms that treat rescue like ownership."

Professor Valen drove the resonance pulse down through the ancient Aurelis foundation stones. The archway groaned wider, Lucien's voice cut off, and cold air spilled out across our boots.

From deep below, a child sobbed once before a gag spell snapped over his mouth.

Cassian lunged forward, and Dren caught him hard by the shoulder. The fact that Cassian let himself be held told me how badly that sound had cut him.

Instructor Dren: "Line holds."

Cassian's jaw flexed.

Cassian: "A child just..."

Instructor Dren: "I heard him. That is why the line holds."

Cold poured out of the tunnel mouth, thick with the sensory ghost of winter drill yards and numb fingers. Maelin swept low healer light across the threshold without crossing the stone line.

Maelin: "Real pain. His breath hitched, then a silence spell clamped down. That isn't a recording."

Pella pressed her slate tight against her ribs, voice barely audible.

Pella: "Did he hear us?"

Nera stared down into the dark.

Nera: "Maybe. Or the room wants us careless."

Mira swallowed hard, clutching her pen.

Mira: "How do we tell without hurting him?"

Valen turned slowly, struck by the question.

Professor Valen: "We stop demanding certainty first. We test in a way that never punishes the boy if we read it wrong."

The wall sconces dimmed slightly at the word boy.

Aira glanced up at the ceiling.

Aira: "Notice how it hates ordinary nouns."

Seraphine flicked a thin red thread six feet into the tunnel. It folded straight back against her palm.

Lady Seraphine: "Spatial loop."

Leon tested the air currents with water-sense, frowning hard.

Leon: "It stretches longer the faster we push."

Elira knelt beside the threshold despite Maelin's immediate glare and laid two uncasting fingertips-bare skin, zero spark-against the stone lip, letting permission rather than magic answer the ancient ward.

Elira: "Iven Sahl. You do not have to answer if answering hurts."

The tunnel stone shifted with a dull grind, shortening by the width of a single brick.

Aira dropped to one knee beside Elira, eyes bright.

Aira: "Look at the masonry. Commands lengthen the hall. Permission shortens it."

Valen stepped back to the ancient inscription carved beside the archway, reading the worn lettering aloud by touch.

Professor Valen: "Witness proximity... patient consent... no single bearer... room opens when pain is named by the one bearing it..."

She stopped abruptly. Halden stepped close and read the scarred final line softly.

Professor Halden: "Companion must be chosen before treatment begins."

Maelin spun around toward the open doorway of the recovery room just behind us. I turned with her.

Inside Cael's old room, the lone iron observation chair sat far back from the empty bed frame.

Haru: "There used to be two chairs."

Aira was already moving, crossing back into the recovery room with Mira and Finn trailing to the doorway. She dropped onto the white tile beside the bed and ran her bare fingers over the floor.

Aira: "Dust scar. Heavy legs, rounded feet. Dragged out recently enough that the tile underneath is still cleaner than the corner, yet not last night."

Maelin stepped in beside her, her brisk medical armor cracking as she stared at the empty space within arm's reach of the mattress.

Maelin: "A companion chair."

Valen crossed the threshold at last, standing beside the bed as if looking down into an open grave.

Professor Valen: "Original healing law required the injured student to pick someone to sit within reach before treatment seals locked."

Darian stared at the lone observation chair.

Darian: "Noctis infirmaries allow only one seat."

Nera looked sick.

Nera: "For the evaluator."

Care had once meant keeping someone close enough to hold your hand. Someone had scrubbed that chair out of the room and left a distant watcher in its place, then called the missing piece standard procedure.

Elira stood over the dust scar, fingers hovering above the clean tile.

Elira: "Cael was locked in here between Noctis prep drills before Aurelis's healers ever met him. While everyone argued over what his body proved, did anybody ask who he wanted beside him?"

Maelin shut her eyes. Nera's silence gave the answer.

I remembered Cael standing pale in the trial hall, apologizing for taking up space before Votive Return tore him apart. The empty patch of floor suddenly shouted louder than any spell trap.

Haru: "Put a chair back. As record."

Finn raised a hand from the doorway, swallowed once, and spoke fast.

Finn: "There are old visitor chairs in the supply closet at the end of the hall. Most are smashed, though one solid wooden one is left. Pella and I sat on it last month while copying maintenance maps."

Seraphine nodded toward the corridor.

Lady Seraphine: "Fetch it. Stay inside the red line."

Finn and Pella bolted down the hall and hauled the chair back together, bumping one leg against the doorframe and wincing. It was plain dark wood, one arm patched with mismatched screws, the seat worn smooth by decades of ordinary students.

Mira helped steady it at the threshold, then paused.

Mira: "Who sets it down?"

The question hung sharp in the air. If I placed it, the annex might read Black Circle interference. If Elira placed it, Lucien would twist proximity into his favorite lie.

Rhea understood immediately.

President Valmont: "Cael is not here to choose."

Nera stepped forward first.

Nera: "He chose Aurelis protection."

Darian: "He chose refusal."

Leon: "He chose to warn us."

Cassian: "He chose not to be used quietly."

Aira looked down at her open pages.

Aira: "He chose to put the truth in writing."

Elira's eyes shone in the dim lamp glow.

Elira: "Then we set it down as witnesses to his choices, never as replacements."

One by one, without making a spectacle of it, we touched the worn wood: Aira on the mended arm, Leon on the rail, Cassian on the seat edge, Nera and Darian on the legs, Rhea, Valen, and Halden along the back. Maelin touched it last.

Maelin: "For the patient."

Then Elira and I lifted it together and set it right over the dust scar beside the bed, close enough for someone lying there to reach out without sitting up.

A soft sigh breathed through the old ceiling vents.

Across the room, the lone observation chair split cleanly down its spine with a dry crack, collapsing inward without anyone laying a hand on it.

The dark absence ring around my wrist dimmed, and for one heartbeat the room flickered into what it had been before fear rewrote it: open curtains, twin chairs, monitoring lines waiting politely for permission. Cael wasn't in the room. The annex didn't pretend furniture could bring back the dead; it only showed the decency that should have met him while he lived.

Elira wiped one tear off her cheek with the heel of her hand and didn't apologize for it.

Lucien's voice slid coldly through the walls.

Lucien: "Moved by carpentry now, Miss Vale?"

Elira didn't flinch away from the chair.

Elira: "A chair never saved a conduit. Removing one helped build them."

Light flared along the far wall. Beneath layers of Noctis monitoring script, older Aurelis letters bled through the plaster like a bruise rising to the surface.

**NO TREATMENT WITHOUT CHOSEN PRESENCE.**

Halden stared at the letters as if an argument he had fought his whole career had just been settled in blood.

Professor Halden: "Aurelis stripped this law before Noctis ever copied the room."

Rhea whipped around toward Valen.

President Valmont: "Aurelis did this?"

Valen didn't flinch or defend the academy.

Professor Valen: "Old tournament healers grew obsessed with cold distance after Circle Zero failed. Chosen presence was treated like contamination. Noctis just inherited our scar and sharpened it into a weapon."

Mira's pencil moved fast across her notebook.

Mira: "Aurelis wound. Noctis blade."

Valen looked at the Green Circle girl with quiet respect.

Professor Valen: "Precisely."

Behind us, the service tunnel groaned and shortened by another brick.

From far down in the dark came two sharp metallic taps. Spoon against stone. Pause. Two taps again.

Nera gasped, color draining straight from her cheeks.

Nera: "Winter-drill code. Two taps means heard, being watched."

Iven hadn't been freed, yet the tremor from the restored room had reached him. He knew someone had answered the old law, and he was warning us before he spoke.

Leon crouched and ran a fresh ribbon of water over the threshold lip. It returned humming with two uneven, frightened pulses.

Maelin: "He moved on his own."

President Valmont: "Could someone force him to tap?"

Nera swallowed hard.

Nera: "A control spell forces an even, mechanical beat. Those taps were ragged. Scared. On purpose."

Elira knelt beside the restored bed rather than the tunnel mouth, speaking calmly so her voice carried down the corridor.

Elira: "Iven Sahl, you do not need to tap again. If someone is forcing your hand, you owe them no proof."

Silence answered from below. No tap came.

The tunnel shortened another brick, opening wide enough for one person at a time.

We gathered back at the threshold, leaving the worn wooden chair standing guard beside Cael's old bed.

Seraphine checked the dark bore ahead.

Lady Seraphine: "Now we move."

Dren nodded once.

Instructor Dren: "Slowly."

Lucien's voice scraped thin with irritation out of the well behind us.

Lucien: "Your slowness is pure vanity."

Haru: "No. It is how we stop building rooms like yours."

Dren stepped into the tunnel first. Leon sent cool water gliding ahead down the stone floor while Cassian warmed the damp air without sparking open flame. Aira marched behind them with her notebook open, followed closely by Halden, Maelin, Rhea, Mira, and Finn, while Seraphine, Valen, and Pella held the upper annex gate and seals.

Nera froze at the lip as the smell of winter drills drifted up from below. The re-riveted binding rings locked around her scarred wrists trembled.

Nera: "If I hear a bell down there, I might stop moving."

Rhea paused beside her.

President Valmont: "Then the whole line stops with you."

Nera exhaled shakily, nodded, and stepped down beside Darian.

Elira looked up at me and tucked the black pendant neatly beneath her altered navy collar so its glare wouldn't blind us in the narrow dark.

Haru: "Still your choice."

Elira: "Still yours."

We stepped down into the cold together, close enough to see each other breathe, never rushing. The ceiling pressed lower with every pace, pipes sweating iron and mint along the stone while Iven's pale trace pulsed weakly ahead. Behind us sat a badly mended wooden chair in an empty recovery room, proof that someone had once cared enough to keep a place beside the bed, and ahead waited a frightened boy listening in the dark.

---

## Interlude: Pella - The Chair Registry

While Lady Seraphine kept watch at the outer annex lock behind the descending column, Professor Valen stepped just inside Cael's upper recovery annex room with Pella under a single desk lamp. Mira had drilled one habit into every Green records aide since the Foundation gallery: never trust an erasure until you check the underside.

Pella tipped the badly mended companion chair onto its side. Beneath thick layers of gray varnish, lamplight caught a scratched brass tag bearing three stamped digits and a carpenter's repair stamp dated fifteen years back.

Across the landing in the storage closet, Professor Valen held the lantern steady while Pella paged through the battered supply ledger. Seven times over fifteen years, the chair had been moved. Never burned. Never broken up for kindling. Every clerk who hid it had written down a fresh lie to keep it out of an inventory purge: spare hall bench, damaged classroom prop, unsorted archive wood, nonessential frame.

Pella copied every false label onto a clean sheet to fold into Mira's archive the moment they reopened the hall, neat and plain, then underlined the real entry beneath them.

Companion chair. Preserved off-ledger. Unknown protector.

Stepping back to the upper annex gate and seals, Professor Valen asked softly if an old chair's tag really mattered with everything waiting below.

Pella set the chair carefully upright just inside the open recovery doorway where Seraphine and Valen could watch it from the upper gate, straightened her sleeve, and glanced toward the stair descending toward the lower service tunnel where Haru, Elira, Mira, and Finn had vanished minutes earlier.

Pella: "Somebody risked keeping it when the rules wanted it gone. So yes. It goes in the record."

===== EPISODE 22 =====

# Episode 22: **The Boy Beneath the School**

The tunnel had opened only after the annex stopped mistaking command for courage.

Dren took point with Leon and Cassian clearing the damp stone ahead, followed in a steady line by Aira, Halden, Maelin, Rhea, Mira, Finn, Nera, and Darian, while Elira and I stepped down last from Cael's old recovery room, leaving Lady Seraphine, Professor Valen, and Pella to hold the upper annex gate and seals. By then we knew three things: Iven Sahl was alive below us, the path punished rushing, and every step had to be slow enough for the old magic to trust us.

Fear still pushed the back of the line faster than our pace.

Dren stopped it with one word.

Instructor Dren: "Line."

Everyone snapped into place, because the dark ahead tightened whenever anyone rushed.

The stone ceiling pressed low enough that Cassian had to duck, keeping his frost-bandaged right wrist tucked close to his ribs. Old pipes ran along both walls, slick with condensation that smelled of rust and bitter mint. Above us, the academy sounded distant, like a tidy lecture hall trying to disown its own basement.
