Elira: "Rhea."

Rhea exhaled once.

President Valmont: "Advanced Mana Theory first period was moved from classroom three to lecture hall nine. Officially, for space and observer seating."

Aira: "Observer seating."

Finn unrolled the first map on the table.

Finn: "Lecture hall nine has tiered seating."

Mira: "And an old demonstration pit."

Cassian stopped chewing.

Leon: "A pit."

Mira nodded miserably.

Mira: "Not a modern one. Maintenance calls it a central working circle, lower than the benches, round, built so everyone above can look down."

The Black Circle stirred. Elira touched my wrist with two fingers, a reminder rather than restraint. I breathed.

Haru: "Who requested the room change?"

President Valmont: "Deputy Registrar Pellon, under instruction from Academic Safety Review."

Aira: "Krail."

President Valmont: "His signature is not on it."

Aira: "Krail with cleaner boots."

Maelin held out a hand, took the map from Finn, and wore the expression healers reserve for patients who describe a terrible idea as tradition.

Maelin: "No."

President Valmont: "Agreed."

Elira: "Has Halden seen this?"

President Valmont: "He filed an objection at sixth bell."

Haru: "Wait. Sixth bell this morning, or yesterday?"

President Valmont: "Yesterday evening. Before Pellon even submitted the room change."

Aira brightened.

Aira: "He objected before they filed?"

President Valmont: "Professor Halden submitted a standing objection to any room arrangement that places Haru Aerlen below observers, Elira Vale on open display for staring, or Green Circle witnesses in back containment rows. He titled it 'Preemptive Refusal of Predictable Cowardice.'"

For a second, nobody spoke. Then Cassian laughed.

Cassian: "I am beginning to like him."

Leon: "That is unsettling."

Mira's eyes went wide.

Mira: "Can professors title objections like that?"

President Valmont: "Apparently."

Aira wrote something down with visible reverence. Elira pressed her knuckles to her mouth.

Haru: "Where is class now?"

Rhea's expression sobered.

President Valmont: "Still lecture hall nine unless we force the change. Senna is in Council session. Valen is arguing old classroom rules. Halden is standing outside the doors refusing to begin until the seating changes, while Dren and Seraphine keep observers out of the pit."

Leon: "Observers?"

Finn unrolled the second map.

Finn: "Faculty safety reps, Council note clerks, two visiting academy reps, and three people claiming to be building inspectors."

Aira: "Building inspectors?"

Finn: "One of them wore opera gloves."

Cassian: "Unlikely, though intriguing."

Maelin looked sharply at Rhea.

Maelin: "Why bring this to them before fixing it?"

President Valmont: "Because if we settle every condition behind closed doors, the first lesson becomes that ordinary life is something adults secretly arrange around Haru and Elira."

Elira's posture changed, subtle enough that only someone watching closely would catch it. Rhea had caught it.

President Valmont: "You have the right to see the room before you walk into it."

Elira: "And the right to refuse."

President Valmont: "Full right."

She tapped the corner of the seating map rather than folding it away.

The room waited for us to decide, which mattered more than any filing. I looked at Elira.

Haru: "What do you want?"

She studied the tiered lines, the sunken central circle, the observer alcoves, and the back rows labeled for Green Circle overflow in handwriting too neat to be innocent. Her thumb brushed the edge of her pendant, then dropped.

Elira: "I want to attend class."

Haru: "In that room?"

Elira: "No."

Mira let out a small breath of relief and looked instantly guilty for it. Elira turned to her.

Elira: "What do Green students want?"

Mira froze.

Mira: "I am not authorized to speak for all Green students."

Aira: "Excellent survival instinct. Answer for yourself."

Mira swallowed.

Mira: "I want not to sit in the back just because someone decided low rank belongs farthest from the danger."

Finn nodded.

Finn: "I want rows where every student can leave without crossing a pit."

Leon stared down at the map again.

Leon: "No pit."

Cassian: "I want to hear the building inspectors justify opera gloves."

Maelin: "Denied as primary objective."

Cassian: "Secondary?"

Maelin: "Also denied."

Rhea rolled the map back up.

President Valmont: "Then we do not enter lecture hall nine as arranged."

Haru: "Will that count as refusing instruction?"

Rhea's smile was thin.

President Valmont: "Only if Academic Safety Review wants to explain why the first ordinary class after ruling against containment needed a pit to put him in."

Aira: "I would enjoy taking minutes on that explanation."

Elira reached for her tea. Her hand trembled once before steadying, slight enough that most people would have missed it, clear enough that she knew I had seen. She drank anyway.

Elira: "Then we go."

Maelin: "Slowly."

Elira: "At your pace."

Maelin: "With the brace."

Elira: "Already buckled."

Her voice stayed quiet, though it carried cleanly across the room.

Maelin: "And no dramatic speeches on the walk."

Elira glanced at me.

Elira: "That one is for you."

Haru: "I have given very few dramatic speeches."

Aira: "Quantity is not the only metric."

The warning bell for first period rang while we were still in the cottage. Reduced volume, single tower. Rhea had ordered the cap after Sera asked whether safe had to be noisy. The bronze note moved over Aurelis gently, almost hesitant. Elira closed her eyes.

Her fingers stayed away from the pendant. Mine stayed away from the Black Circle. Maelin watched both choices and wrote neither down.

Outside, the academy was waiting, and it did not look like a battlefield. That made it harder.

The path from the witness cottage crossed the east garden, passed the fountain, and curved under the old stone arcade where first-years usually complained about assignments with the gravity of people who had not yet seen what real trouble did to a schedule.

They were out there now, trying to look ordinary.

Green Circle students gathered along the low wall with notebooks in plain sight. Blue support students stood in pairs, pretending their spacing had nothing to do with watching the path. Red Circle heirs lingered beneath the arcade, a few with family attendants hovering far enough back to claim they weren't interfering. Several Yellow seniors waited near the fountain with expressions held neutral so tightly they looked brittle. Nobody shouted. Nobody bowed. Nobody called me myth.

That quiet had not grown on its own; Rhea had built it. Council aides stood at intervals along the path, leaving the way wide enough that approaching required intent. Dren waited beside the fountain with arms folded, Seraphine beside him, her red circle dim at her wrist while her gaze swept the crowd like a blade taking attendance.

Professor Valen appeared halfway along the arcade with three thick history books tucked under one arm and a pale Council clerk trailing behind her.

Professor Valen: "Classification under uncertainty is hardly new. If the Council wants to pretend it invented caution this morning, it can start with the older room rules I flagged-from before the current standards even existed."

Council Clerk: "Professor, those are four hundred pages."

Professor Valen: "Then the Council will remain cautious for some time."

Elira's mouth curved.

Elira: "I missed her."

Haru: "She has been around us all week."

Elira: "I missed watching her make paperwork suffer."

Aira: "A universal comfort."

As we reached the fountain, the low murmur around us shifted.

*Haru. Elira. Black Circle. Valise. Is she cleared? Did Sera really refuse Noctis recovery? Why is the bell so quiet? Can he hear us?*

I could. Not with magic, just proximity, training, and the ugly precision with which fear aimed itself. I kept walking without answering.

Elira walked beside me, shoulder brace hidden under her jacket, pendant in plain view, chin level. Aira followed one pace back with an open notebook. Leon and Cassian flanked the outer grass awkwardly enough to deserve partial credit for not looking like bodyguards. Mira and Finn walked ahead with Rhea, carrying the seating maps like evidence from a crime scene that had not yet confessed.

On the fountain rim, a small square of ward paper waited.

Sera's cup, drawn in a child's careful, uneven hand, leaning slightly left. Below it, in letters that changed size halfway across the line, someone had copied:

**BELL HEARD. NOT TOO LOUD. CUP STAYED.**

Elira stopped. So did I. The chatter around the fountain quieted in widening rings.

Aira reached the rim first without touching the paper.

Aira: "Ward transfer from the trauma wing. Sender status?"

Rhea checked the corner seal.

President Valmont: "Sera authorized a single copy to the public fountain. No response required. No visit requested. Nothing beyond the text."

Elira's eyes shone. She blinked once and left everyone else to pretend not to notice.

Haru: "Good."

That was the only word I trusted not to overreach.

A boy near the Green cluster whispered too loudly.

Green First-Year: "She can write?"

Mira turned, sharp without raising her voice.

Mira: "She can choose what gets copied."

The boy flushed red.

Green First-Year: "I meant-"

Mira: "I know. Say it better next time."

He shut his mouth and stared down at his boots. That, too, was a lesson.

The drawing stayed on the fountain rim because Rhea said moving it before the interval ended would turn care into tidying. We walked on.

The academic wing smelled of ink, damp stone, floor polish, and the faint panic of officials discovering that students understood how public moments worked better than committees did.

Outside lecture hall nine, the corridor was full, though Rhea's aides kept clear lanes to the exits.

Halden stood before the closed doors with a slate under one arm and the patience of a cliff that had read the rules and found them lacking. Dren flanked his left, Seraphine his right. Behind them stood three faculty safety reps wearing the sour looks of men who had arrived to inspect a hazard and realized they were the ones under review.

One of the building inspectors wore opera gloves. Cassian spotted them at once.

Cassian: "Magnificent."

Maelin: "No."

The inspector bristled without knowing why.

Halden's gaze swept over us, pausing on Elira's shoulder, my hands, Aira's notebook, Mira's folio, Finn's maps, and Rhea's council mark before he gave one crisp nod.

Professor Halden: "You are on time."

Aira checked the corridor clock.

Aira: "We are seven minutes late."

Professor Halden: "Class has not begun."

President Valmont: "Why?"

Halden turned toward the doors.

Professor Halden: "Because the assigned room is unfit for teaching."

One of the faculty delegates cleared his throat.

Delegate: "Professor Halden, lecture hall nine is certified for high-risk demonstrations."

Halden looked at him.

Professor Halden: "Today is not a high-risk demonstration."

Delegate: "With respect, the presence of Haru Aerlen-"

Professor Halden: "Is the attendance of an enrolled student."

The delegate's mouth shut. Krail would have hated that answer, which made me like it immediately. Elira stepped forward.

Elira: "Professor, what is today's lesson?"

Halden's gaze moved to her. For a heartbeat, something almost gentle softened his austere face before settling back into gravel.

Professor Halden: "Classification under uncertainty."

Aira's pencil started moving.

Elira: "Does the lesson require a sunken pit?"

Professor Halden: "No lesson requires a sunken pit unless the instructor lacks imagination."

Seraphine's mouth twitched. Dren examined the ceiling as if he had refused to witness humor in an official corridor.

The delegate tried another angle.

Delegate: "The hall was chosen to give safety staff clear sightlines in case anything unusual happens."

Fear hit Mira's face first, followed quickly by insult, which was turning into one of her better brands of courage.

Mira: "Sightlines for whom?"

The delegate looked at her as though a Green Circle student had spoken out of a supply closet.

Delegate: "Safety staff."

Finn held up the map.

Finn: "Then why are Green Circle seats marked rear overflow while Yellow Circle seats hold tier center?"

The delegate blinked.

Finn: "If the goal is safety, good sightlines shouldn't go by rank prestige. If the goal is rank prestige, stop calling the room choice safety."

Aira muttered under her breath.

Aira: "Finn Castellan, terror of furniture."

Finn did not smile; his hands were shaking too hard for that. Mira stepped half a pace closer to him without touching.

The delegate looked to Rhea for rescue.

President Valmont: "Answer him."

Delegate: "The seating follows standard academy rank."

The corridor went cold, and not from me. Elira spoke without raising her voice.

Elira: "Then it follows the wrong standard. A class coming back after what everyone witnessed cannot seat students by the exact rank system that caused half this harm and pretend the layout is neutral."

Halden looked back at the delegate.

Professor Halden: "There is your answer."

Delegate: "Professor, with respect-"

Lady Seraphine: "You keep using that phrase for someone offering remarkably little of it."

The delegate stopped.

The opera-gloved inspector tried a softer route.

Inspector: "Could the class proceed if Haru Aerlen takes the lower circle voluntarily?"

The Black Circle held still behind my ribs. So did I.

That word was the snare. *Voluntarily.* Noctis had bled it dry; Council paperwork had polished it until a trap could check its reflection in the shine. Agree to keep the peace, and the record would claim I chose the pit. Snap back too hard, and the record would claim the Black Circle resisted oversight. Let Elira speak for me, and they would write down that she was steering me.

Aira's pencil stopped. That quiet told me the corridor had turned into a test.

Mira glanced at me, then away, knowing stares could press just as hard as rules. I breathed once.

Haru: "No."

The word stayed flat in the hall. The inspector's brows rose.

Inspector: "No?"

Haru: "I do not consent to seating that makes me the lesson before the lesson starts."

Aira's pencil moved again, relieved rather than triumphant.

Inspector: "The precaution is not symbolic."

Haru: "Then remove the symbol."

Silence held, tight and workable. Elira's fingers brushed mine once, a quiet check rather than reward.

Halden pushed open the doors to lecture hall nine.

Inside, the tiered benches rose above a central stone circle. Small placards marked the back corners for Green Circle overflow. Looking at them turned something cold in my chest, older than Aurelis pressure: rooms taught people their place before anyone spoke a single word.

Halden walked down into the pit alone. For one absurd second, I thought he meant to teach from it. Instead he set his slate on the stone, lifted one hand, and dissolved the demonstration circle. The stone stayed sunken, though the old boundary runes went dark one by one until the pit looked like nothing more than a badly planned floor.

Halden climbed back up to the doorway.

Professor Halden: "Class will not be held here."

The delegate stiffened.

Delegate: "You cannot simply refuse an assigned hall."

Professor Halden: "I can when the hall undermines the lesson."

He looked over at us.

Professor Halden: "Courtyard."

Leon stared.

Leon: "Outside?"

Professor Halden: "Most concepts survive air."

Cassian: "This may end up my favorite class."

Seraphine looked straight at him.

Cassian: "Academically."

The relocation took nine minutes, and Aira logged every one. Not because nine minutes mattered on their own, but because someone later would try to call it disorder, student unrest, or Black Circle trouble to prove the pit had been necessary after all.

So Aira wrote, Finn copied, and Mira kept witness timestamps. Rhea sealed the move under Student Council safety authority and Halden's faculty direction. Dren guided students down the stairs in mixed groups instead of ranks, and Seraphine made the building inspectors carry their own chairs when they asked where observers went.

Out in the east courtyard, the space became a classroom without banners or rings.

Students took benches, fountain ledges, low walls, and patches of grass where the morning dew had mostly dried. Green and Blue students mixed near the middle because Mira and Finn got there first and claimed it before anyone could label a back row overflow. Leon sat beside a Green first-year who froze for two seconds and then tried hard to act as if sharing a bench with Leon Varek happened every Tuesday. Cassian sat behind them and handed the boy an apple slice without comment.

Elira picked a stone bench by the fountain where she could rest her bad shoulder against the back. I sat beside her, close because we both chose it rather than because a floor plan put us there. Aira settled on the grass at our feet with her notebooks fanned out like a small legal barricade. Rhea stayed near the courtyard arch, observing rather than presiding, while Maelin leaned against a pillar and watched Elira's breathing while pretending not to monitor half the school.

## Advanced Mana Theory - The Release Seam

Halden stood before us with no chalkboard.

Professor Valen arrived carrying the lesson alongside Soren Ashvale and Talen Mire-who had ridden in that morning from Valemere's nearby delegation lodge under Magistra Voss's audit summons with the broken tournament panel they had recovered after the suspension rather than let anyone else interpret Talen's withdrawal readings. Soren held one end of the safety-ward frame, and Talen carried the other with his good hand while his braced arm stayed tucked against his coat. The waist-high silver frame was split across one corner, yet its center still hummed with the clean sheen of a spell that had passed every standard inspection.

Students crowded closer before remembering old habit and giving the frame room.

Professor Valen: "Suspended bracket equipment. Valemere logged the failure during inventory."

Soren lowered his end onto two stone blocks while Talen set down the other.

Soren: "Competitor status still holds and standings stay frozen. We brought proof, not a request to restart."

Leon looked disappointed by the second half and relieved by the first.

Halden lifted his slate and wrote three words in the upper corner.

**OBSERVATION. INFERENCE. CLAIM.**

He drew a single line underneath them.

**UNCERTAINTY IS NOT PERMISSION TO INVENT.**

Professor Halden: "This panel passed standard inspection. It fails only when incoming mana turns uneven or a caster pulls back. Today you will determine why."

His eyes crossed me without lingering.

Professor Halden: "No Black Circle correction. No overpowering the spell. No pulling on Mr. Mire's magic without fresh permission before each test. If you make the panel look stable without finding the fault, you fail."

Cassian: "A class that punishes surface polish. Leon is in mortal danger."

Leon: "Your collar is crooked."

Cassian checked it on reflex. Aira laughed before he could pretend otherwise.

The first repair group went straight for the visible crack. Leon laid Blue pressure along the silver border, Cassian threaded left-handed heat underneath while keeping his wrapped right wrist clear, and a Yellow senior filled the gap with enough clean light to make the frame hum. The split sealed over. Inspection runes along the edge turned green one by one.

For six seconds, the repair looked flawless.

Talen's brace began to vibrate. He pulled his arm tight against his coat.

Talen: "Stop."

Leon cut his spell before Halden could echo the word. Cassian followed a beat later. The Yellow senior hesitated just long enough for the courtyard to see it, then dropped her light too. The panel stayed green.

Talen: "It reads lower output as damage."

Soren: "Show them only if you want to."

Talen unfastened the outer strap of his brace. A thin thread of Blue light shivered through his palm, caught by the frame from three paces off. Every time his output dipped, the newly mended corner flared brighter, yanking back as if correcting him. Elira leaned forward.

Elira: "That support lattice is mine."

Her voice came out sharper than surprise.

Soren: "A later Valemere version."

Elira: "My original outer seam opened when support withdrew."

Soren: "This one does not."

Elira stood up before Maelin's warning glance could stop her.

Elira: "Someone stripped out the release path and kept my name in the design log."

Nobody told her to calm down. That helped.

Cold pressed behind my sternum as the Black Circle read the panel without asking: nine overloaded joins, a false green inspection loop, and an original release seam buried under heavier reinforcement. I could have quieted all nine with less effort than it had once taken to keep the shattered false Green crest active at my wrist.

Pain pulsed beneath the fingernail Maelin had wrapped after the lower channel. My hand twitched forward anyway. Elira caught it.

Elira: "If you stabilize it, we lose the defect."

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "Your hand does not."

Quiet enough to sting, public enough that I could not smooth it away. I slid both hands into my pockets.

The panel kept humming without me. A strange mix of pride and uselessness settled in my chest: I was built for every crisis, and standing still while other people solved a room felt dangerously close to not being needed.

Being unneeded in one moment was not the same as being worthless. I held onto that until my fingers stopped flexing inside my coat.

Talen looked down at the frame.

Talen: "I can test the withdrawal."

Maelin: "You can offer. Halden can still decide the hardware is too stupid to deserve your nerves."

Talen almost smiled.

Talen: "One low-output hold. When I say stop, nobody keeps measuring."

President Valmont: "Condition logged. Readings remain yours unless you choose to release them."

Talen stepped up and held his braced hand near the silver border. Soren moved in a pace, then stopped.

Soren: "Support?"

Talen: "Only if I ask."

His faded Blue Circle opened. The panel drank the first pulse, and the inspection runes stayed green. Talen let his output drop by a fraction.

The frame clamped down on the weakening line. His breath hitched.

Talen: "Stop."

The panel did not let go.

Elira broke the construct. Gold light struck the silver frame from the side, shattering the smooth repair. The crack split open twice as wide, and the courtyard wards barked one sharp alarm before Cassian smothered it with heat. Soren took a step toward Talen and halted.

Soren: "Support?"

Talen cradled his shaking wrist.

Talen: "Just the brace."

Soren buckled the loose outer strap and kept his hands clear.

Elira glared at the split panel. The Yellow senior glared back at her.

Yellow Senior: "You wrecked our repair."

Elira: "Your repair heard *stop* and tightened its grip. It was already broken."

Her anger had real color now, not defending me or answering Krail, just Elira Vale as a mage-architect staring at stolen work turned dangerous by someone else's shortcut.

Halden tapped the row of inspection runes along the silver edge, still glowing green right beside the widened crack.

Professor Halden: "Observation?"

Aira: "Talen's brace vibrated before any rune reported instability."

Professor Halden: "Inference?"

Elira: "The ward treats pulling back as a fault and drags power out of the channel trying to leave."

Professor Halden: "Claim?"

Soren: "This panel is unsafe for tournament play."

Professor Halden: "Supported for this panel under these conditions. Not yet universal."

He turned to the courtyard.

Professor Halden: "Fear can be observed, though it cannot testify beyond what it knows. Neither can pride in a tidy patch."

Mira had been leaning forward from the Green benches, squinting at the silver edge.

Mira: "Stronger light keeps washing out the paper."

Nobody else caught it except Finn, who was already pulling thin archive strips from his folio, cheap dust-treated paper that darkened under mana stress. They slid two beneath the corner, and the leftover Blue and Yellow traces still lingering in the frame turned both strips black on contact.

Finn: "We need lower output."

Mira swallowed.

Mira: "Mine."

Professor Halden: "The frame may snap a strip and chill the hand holding it. You may pass."

I stepped toward the heavy corner to take some of the load for her. Mira saw me reach.

Mira: "Please do not make it gentle for me."

I stopped. She was scared, and turning the test soft would have protected my conscience more than her skill.

Haru: "Tell me where to hold."

Mira pointed to the heavy end of the frame rather than the safe one. I tilted that corner clear of the stone block so she could reach underneath, holding the weight without smoothing a single line of mana.

Her Green Circle opened. Small, steady light entered the third paper strip and left most of it pale, except for one narrow bruise along the buried seam. Finn logged the time. The fourth strip tore as the frame twitched. Mira flinched, kept her fingers clear, and changed the angle on the fifth instead of pushing harder.

Three dark branches surfaced along the underside of the silver edge.

Elira knelt beside them. Maelin opened her mouth to object; Elira pointed at both knees planted flat on the grass as if kneeling were a medical defense. Maelin let it go.

Fine gold points drifted over the paper, weak enough to leave Mira's Green signal visible beneath them while tracing the old strain mark by mark.

Elira: "There. The original release seam. They buried it so the shields could take harder hits."

Soren's jaw tightened.

Soren: "To cut down on match stoppages."

Talen: "They turned surrender into malfunction because stoppages slowed the bracket."

The courtyard went quiet around that. Not every cruelty began with Lucien; some started with a schedule someone wanted to keep on time.

Elira traced one quadrant in the air without touching the metal.

Elira: "I can cut this seam open. One section only. If I try the whole frame now, my output will blind Mira's reading and Maelin will get creative."

Maelin: "Accurate."

President Valmont: "Talen decides whether his channel goes near it again."

Talen flexed his fingers inside the strapped brace, waited a beat, and unhooked only the cuff clasp.

Talen: "Give me ten minutes. Same stop rule. Only the cut quadrant."

Nobody filled those ten minutes with speeches.

Leon and Cassian held the frame steady while arguing over whose earlier patch had hidden more of the fault. Finn numbered the remaining strips. Mira redrew the dark branches twice because her first sketch made one fork look too certain. Aira noted the exact beat Talen had said *stop* against the beat the frame had tightened. Soren sat beside Talen without hovering. Elira worked.

Her first gold seam collapsed, and she swore under her breath. Her second opened too wide and nearly spilled load into the neighboring quadrant.

Professor Halden: "That is not a release. That is the whole frame giving out."

Elira: "I saw it."

Professor Halden: "Your expression suggested you wanted the mistake to feel ashamed."

Elira: "It should."

On the third try, she used less light. The result looked unimpressive: one crooked gold break in an otherwise smooth silver border.

Talen stepped back to the mark.

Soren: "Support?"

Talen: "Stand where I can see you."

The Blue pulse entered the cut quadrant. One breath. Two. Talen lowered his hand.

Talen: "Stop."

The crooked gold seam parted cleanly. His mana left the panel instead of being dragged back into his palm. The other three quadrants flared red, one false green rune shattered, and the frame stayed broken.

Talen stared at his hand.

Talen: "That one listened."

Elira sat back hard in the grass, wearing the fierce grin she usually hid behind competence. One quadrant. No miracle fix. No restored bracket. Just a broken panel with one honest exit.

It was the best thing we had built all week. Soren faced Rhea.

Soren: "Valemere will not accept frozen standings as a win. When competition resumes, we want to meet Aurelis properly."

Cassian: "Finally, a diplomatic stance with some spine."

Leon: "Aurelis was ahead."

Soren: "Then you should welcome the chance to prove it."

Leon's chin came up, accepting the challenge. Talen snapped his cuff clasp shut.

Talen: "I will not endorse restarting matches while safety wards treat pulling back as an attack. I will help test them if my readings remain mine. That is not a promise to compete."

President Valmont: "The Board asked for future resumption standards, not a restart date. Your condition goes into the audit record, not the bracket."

Talen: "Good."

Elira was still watching the crooked gold seam.

Elira: "I want my own research track. Wards built to let go when asked. Tested on injured casters, uneven power, early surrender, pulling back mid-spell, and every Circle rank."

Professor Halden: "That is not a small project."

Elira: "I did not ask for a small one."

Talen: "My readings stay mine."

Elira turned to him immediately.

Elira: "You approve every use, every copy, and every comparison. You can walk away without your withdrawal turning into failed data."

Soren: "Valemere can lend old panel schematics. Not ownership."

Mira held up one of the pale pressure strips.

Mira: "Green baselines have to stay visible."

Elira: "Unedited, on the main sheet."

Finn: "And copied before heavier tests scorch them."

Elira: "Captured first, every time."

The answers came fast because the design belonged to her, not because every solution was already in hand.

Halden studied the split panel and the girl sitting in the grass beside it.

Professor Halden: "You may have laboratory access after medical clearance. Access is not project approval, and today's cut is not a finished design."

Elira: "I know."

Professor Halden: "You look pleased."

Elira: "I am glad there is work nobody can finish for me before I start."

A Council filing crystal arrived at the edge of the grass in a clerk's shaking hands. Rhea did not touch it.

President Valmont: "Class is still in session."

Krail's recorded voice pressed once against the crystal seal. Halden set the shattered inspection rune right on top of it.

Professor Halden: "It can wait beside the other false result."

The clerk backed away.

Maelin handed Elira a folded slip from the trauma wing.

**CLASS FIRST.**

Sera had asked whether we made it through. Elira pressed a hand to her mouth, eyes bright before she looked back down at the panel.

Professor Halden: "Assignment: one page on what failed. If your paper includes the words *fixed*, *universal*, or *destiny*, start over."

It took Soren, Leon, Mira, and the Yellow senior together to haul the panel back toward storage, since the metal refused to turn lighter just because we had learned something from it.

One quadrant opened when asked. Tomorrow, the other three would still be broken.

---

Afternoon classes passed in stiff, careful quiet, and by the time long blue shadows stretched across the east walk, Aurelis looked less sure of itself. Students moved between halls with the wary exhaustion of people who had survived one ordinary day without trusting ordinary to hold.

Rhea found me beside the herb garden behind the council annex. The difference between being found and being summoned meant I stayed where I was without asking why she had come.

She stood by the low stone wall with her hands clasped behind her back and her council mark dim at her wrist.

President Valmont: "I used to hate Green Circle students."

I looked over at her. Her expression did not budge.

President Valmont: "Not personally. That would have been easier. I hated what our treatment of them showed about Aurelis while everyone congratulated themselves for not being Noctis."

Garden wind moved through the rosemary between us.

President Valmont: "I thought if I made procedure sharp enough, it would stop being cruel by accident."

She looked toward the academic wing.

President Valmont: "It did not."

That cost her to say aloud. Rhea Valmont did not confess; she entered corrections into the record.

Haru: "Do you resent me?"

The question slipped out before I could file it down into something safer. Rhea turned her head.

Haru: "For dragging all of it into the open."

She weighed the question with the same severity she gave rulings.

President Valmont: "Sometimes."

Her honesty steadied me more than reassurance would have.

President Valmont: "Being out in the open makes work. It exposes cracks I wanted to patch before anyone walked across them, and it stops me from pretending fixing things is a private virtue."

She met my eyes squarely.

President Valmont: "I do not resent you for surviving loudly enough that Aurelis had to listen to itself."

I had no answer ready, and she did not ask for one.

President Valmont: "That is not comfort. It is a position."

Haru: "I understand."

Rhea's mouth tightened by a fraction.

President Valmont: "I believe you do."

Then she walked back toward the annex, leaving the rosemary and the answer behind.

## Elira Vale - Useless Light

Maelin cleared ten minutes of low-output practice after checking Elira's pulse twice and making her repeat the limit without sarcasm. Elira managed it on the third try.

The west terrace sat empty after the afternoon bell. No healer trailed her up the steps, and no witness seal opened along the parapet.

Old chalk marks scarred the flagstone. Unused target rings leaned against the stone wall. Beyond the railing, the sunken fountain basin and the east courtyard roofs caught the lowering sun in narrow strips of gold. Elira sat down on a bench first, letting the irritation at needing to sit stay plain irritation instead of turning it into disobedience.

She opened a fresh notebook to the first page.

**RELEASE-RESPONSIVE WARD DESIGN**

The heading looked too official, so she drew one clean line through it, keeping the words legible while demoting them from a verdict back to a question. Beneath it, she wrote:

**How does a ward know someone has changed her mind?**

Other questions crowded in faster than ink. How did a frame tell surrender from losing control without checking the speaker's rank first? Could an injured mage step down a spell at a different pace than a healthy one? Who owned a failed reading? What happened when someone withdrew after a ward had already borrowed her strength?

Elira closed the book before the page turned into another room she had to rescue before supper.

Tomorrow she would ask Halden for a lab key. Talen would decide whether his data crossed the threshold. Mira's dust strips would stay inside the core method, not tucked into a footnote as a charming low-rank detail. Valemere could fight over authorship later.

That work belonged to tomorrow. The remaining six minutes belonged to her.

Elira lifted her right hand, keeping the taped palm crease relaxed, while the Yellow Circle beneath her collarbone brightened softly, well under Maelin's cap.

Gold light gathered above her palm: no shield, no blade, no healing lattice, no witness seam, no proof that she deserved the rank pinned onto her before she knew its cost.

She shaped one crooked ring, then another worse one. The third broke into seven bright sparks and drifted upward in no tactical formation whatsoever. Elira smiled. No committee would have graded it, and that was the whole relief.

A servant crossed the lower walk, glanced up, saw a Yellow Circle student idling with harmless shapes, and kept walking without asking for a demonstration or praising her stability.

Elira turned her wrist. The seven sparks drifted down across the terrace and touched the flagstones without a sound. Wherever one landed, a hair-thin gold line traced what boots and rain had nearly worn off the stone: half an old practice circle, muddy heel scrapes, a crooked arrow, the spot where someone had chalked **AGAIN** and rubbed it out.

The light did not mend any of them. It just showed where they had been.

Elira watched the crooked lines warm the stone until nothing happened. No hidden system answered, and no crisis arrived to justify the spell.

When the tenth minute ended, she closed her fingers and let the Yellow Circle fade. She tucked the notebook under her arm and went inside before anyone could ask what the light had been for.

---

Evening came without asking permission.

The cottage lamps lit themselves one by one as the sky behind the trees bruised violet. Maelin had left two covered bowls on the table beside a note reading **eat before arguing ethics with furniture**. Beneath it, Aira had added in smaller ink: **furniture declined comment pending counsel**.

Elira read both notes and made the quiet sound that had almost become laughter again.

We ate at the front window because the table was there, the soup was warm, and neither of us had the patience to carry dinner somewhere more meaningful. Outside, council aides changed shifts along the garden path, and two first-years walked past arguing over whether Halden had technically taught outdoors or committed architecture. Near the fountain, someone stopped to copy Sera's cup note into a slate.

Elira's spoon clicked softly against her bowl. Beneath my ribs, the Black Circle noticed and stayed down, listening the way something dangerous listens to rain once it learns rain is not an attack.

I kept my wrist resting on the table where she could see it. The black-and-silver ribbon lay against the wood, one loose tail slipped free from the day's work. Elira noticed that too.

She finished three bites before speaking.

Elira: "Your knot is loose."

Haru: "I know."

She reached across the table slowly enough that asking was built into the reach. I turned my wrist up.

Her fingers were warm as she retied the ribbon, smoothing the twist rather than pulling it tight until the silver edge caught the lamplight without glaring. The Black Circle shifted once under my skin, closer to memory than threat.

Elira let go when the knot held.

We ate the rest of the bowls in quiet that did not feel fragile. Fear was still in the room, just given a chair and conditions instead of the whole house. A spoon stayed a spoon. Soup stayed dinner because Maelin had threatened both of us, and hunger had not turned political yet.

Outside, the bell tower marked the evening hour at a bearable volume.

Elira glanced toward the dark window, then back at me.

Elira: "Leave the lamp on."

---

## Coda: Haru and Elira - First Bell

At dawn, the academy lifted the volume cap and tried a full morning bell for the first time since the rescue.

It rang badly.

The east tower started half a breath early. The central spire answered a pitch too low. When the west dormitory bell took its turn, the bronze cracked sharp on the third note and shuddered into silence like someone clearing their throat in front of history.

Startled laughter carried up the east garden path from students heading out of the dorms, ragged and uncoordinated before fear could twist the sour note into an omen.

Haru stood at the witness cottage window with one hand on the frame, waiting for the Black Circle to mistake the clangor for an alarm. It stirred, listened to the laughter beneath the iron echo, and settled back down.

Elira came up beside him with a blanket pulled over her shoulders and sleep still softening her face.

Elira: "Terrible bell."

Haru: "Structurally brave."

She looked sideways at him.

Elira: "That was almost a joke."

Haru: "I regret it already."

Across the garden, the cracked bell tolled once more, off-pitch and unapologetic, and nothing followed except morning.

===== EPISODE 29 =====

# Episode 29: **What Cael Kept**

The room did not belong to Cael anymore.

That was the first lie the morning offered, and the easiest one to refuse.

The eastern wing had stayed quiet since the funeral, though never empty. Aurelis did not know how to be empty while people were still trying to survive inside it. Healers crossed the corridor with trays. Council aides moved in careful pairs. Green Circle students carried copied witness statements between archive tables and public boards. Somewhere below us, the old annex still held its breath around the places Noctis had tried to make children disappear cleanly.

Cael's room was quiet in a different way. The door stood half-open.

No drill-master waited behind it. No obedience line burned against the threshold. Noctis Dominion College did not own the first sound of the morning.

It did not own the silence either.

I stood outside with Elira beside me and Leon on my other side, close enough that his shoulder nearly touched the doorframe. He had not entered. None of us had. Maelin had unlocked the room herself, then stepped back with the brisk tact of a healer who understood that some wounds needed witnesses and some needed air before they could become either.

Maelin: "Eight minutes."

Leon did not look at her.

Leon: "Is that medical advice?"

Maelin: "It is a threat wearing a clock."

Cassian leaned a shoulder against the opposite wall behind us, keeping his voice low.

Cassian: "Good to see the rules stay consistent."

Aira's pencil moved once, then stopped. Even she knew some first lines should not be stolen too quickly. Elira looked at me.

Elira: "Haru?"

Her voice held the question no one else wanted to ask. Do you need to be outside? Do you need to be inside? Do you need to pretend either answer is simple?

I looked through the door.

The bed was made. Too neatly. Even during the nights he slept here under Aurelis protection, Cael had kept the room spare, refusing to unpack more than he had to before the Wounded City took him. President Valmont had already packed his personal clasp, broken calibration bead, and notebook for the funeral handover, leaving only a spare issue training coat draped over the chair back, an empty desk blotter, and morning light touching the narrow support beam badly painted across the ceiling. Small things.

Noctis had taught Cael that small things were tests. Warm food meant gratitude would be demanded. An unlocked door meant a better lock waited elsewhere. A quiet room meant someone was listening for the wrong breath.

Aurelis had tried to teach him otherwise, and had run out of time.

That thought entered me hard enough that the Black Circle stirred under my shirt.

Elira's hand moved near mine without touching. Choice.

I breathed until the dark settled.

Haru: "Leon should enter first."

Leon flinched as if I had struck him.

Leon: "Why?"

The answer was not tactical, which made it harder to say.

Haru: "Because you learned beside."

Leon stared at the room. His jaw tightened. For a moment, old pride rose in him, looking for a way to make grief angry enough to stand upright. Then it gave way without noise. He nodded once and stepped over the threshold.

He did not sit on the bed. He did not touch the uniform. He crossed the room slowly, hands open at his sides, and stopped beside the chair. Beside.

Aira wrote the word down with no ornament.

On the desk lay a folded paper, unsealed and weighted beneath a small gray stone that kept the window draft from lifting it. The stone was ordinary river-smooth creek slate, the kind students picked up along Aurelis's east drainage walk because their hands needed something to hold while adults argued over the future.

Mira had found the paper wedged beneath the lifted edge of the desk blotter during post-rescue room clearance, weighted it down under Cael's river-slate stone so the breeze would not scatter it, and refused to open it without witnesses. That was why we were here.

Leon looked at the paper and did not reach.

Leon: "Who is supposed to read it?"

No one answered right away.

In Noctis, silence would have turned into rank. The highest seat would decide, the rest would obey, and afterward everyone would pretend the decision had always been obvious.

Here, the silence stayed difficult.

Rhea stood just outside the threshold in full council uniform, her red Circle lowered but visible. Nera and Oric waited farther down the corridor, close enough to witness, far enough not to crowd the room Noctis had never let Cael own. Mira held two blank witness copies against her chest. Finn stood behind her with ink on his thumb and tight fear across his face. Elira stepped forward.

Elira: "No one is supposed to read it."

Leon turned.

Elira: "That is the point. It was left where it could be found, not forced into anyone's hand."

Aira's pencil resumed across her page.

Aira: "Voluntary recovery of personal record."

Mira: "Not recovery."

Everyone looked at her. Mira went red, but she held her ground.

Mira: "Sorry. I mean... recovery sounds like it was lost by accident. Noctis loses things by design."

Rhea's expression sharpened.

President Valmont: "Correction accepted."

Aira crossed out one word.

Aira: "Voluntary recognition of personal record."

Leon looked at the paper again.

Leon: "Then ask him."

The words landed so hard the room seemed to lose air.

Cassian closed his eyes. Leon swallowed.

Leon: "I know. I know we can't. I just..."

His hand curled once, then opened.

Leon: "He spent his whole life being answered over. I do not want to do it now because he is dead."

Elira's face steadied, grief sharpening into resolve.

Elira: "Then we ask what he already answered."

She nodded toward the desk.

Haru: "Mira."

Mira startled.

Haru: "Did Cael ever tell you what he wanted done with personal corrections?"

Mira held her notebook tighter.

Mira: "Back during the Foundation archive nights, he watched Finn and me copying late and said ugly copies survived better."

Aira made a sound caught somewhere between laughter and pain.

Mira: "He also said... he said if something was written before guilt edited it, we should not make it prettier."

Leon looked down.

Leon: "Then open it ugly."

Rhea entered only far enough to set a witness seal on the desk. It did not touch the paper. It marked the dark wood beside it.

President Valmont: "The record recognizes Cael Nox as a deceased Protected Witness of Aurelis. His personal paper will be opened by willing witnesses. Noctis has no custody claim over what is inside unless he named them."

From the corridor, Nera's breath caught at the word deceased. Oric stood beside her, never stepping in front. Rhea looked at Leon.

President Valmont: "You may decline."

Leon laughed once, quietly and without humor.

Leon: "I know."

He picked up the stone first.

No magic answered. No old law flared. No hidden command line opened beneath the desk. Only a stone, warm from morning sunlight.

Leon set it beside the witness seal, then unfolded the paper.

There were not many words. That hurt worse than a long letter would have.

Cael's handwriting was controlled almost to the point of damage, each letter trained into obedience and then forced, gently, into something less perfect.

Leon read aloud because his voice was the one that shook most honestly.

Leon: "If I do not survive the next correction, do not let Noctis call that proof that correction was wrong."

He stopped. No one pressed him. After a breath, he kept reading.

Leon: "I was not rescued so I could be useful. I am writing this because I keep forgetting. If I forget permanently, keep the sentence ugly. Do not make me noble enough that Noctis can admire me."

Aira put one hand over her mouth.

Leon read the last lines.

Leon: "I wanted to live. I chose anyway. Both are true."

The room held the sentence awkwardly, without neat edges.

Elira's eyes filled, and she did not wipe them. And I-Black Circle magician, world-breaking threat, surviving witness-stood in a dead boy's borrowed room with no power capable of mending a single word. That was as it should be.

Mira copied the statement by hand. Then Finn copied Mira's copy, blotting the word noble so badly he had to write it again in the margin. No one corrected him. The blot belonged to the record too.

Nera entered after the second copy was complete.

She did not ask to see the original. She stood before the desk and bowed, neither the Noctis obedience bow nor the formal Aurelis condolence bow, just something unfinished and human.

Nera: "He is right."

Oric followed her across the threshold.

Oric: "Noctis will try to use the sentence anyway."

President Valmont: "Yes."

Her red seal stayed flat on the dark wood of the desk. Leon looked up sharply.

President Valmont: "And because he named that danger, they will have to do it while his refusal sits in the same public record."

Aira lowered her hand.

Aira: "Ugly copy survives."

Cassian leaned against the doorframe with his arms folded too tightly.

Cassian: "We are making that a doctrine, apparently."

Elira: "No."

Everyone looked at her. Elira touched the pendant at her throat. Its seven open lines remained quiet beneath her fingers.

Elira: "Doctrine is too clean."

Haru: "Practice, then."

She looked at me.

Elira: "Practice."

The witness seal accepted the word without brightening. That felt right.

Later, the Council would ask for copies. Noctis would object to extending *deceased Protected Witness* because even death did not stop them from hunting for wording that gave them ownership. The public boards would carry three versions of Cael's statement: one formal, one handwritten, one blotched by Finn's shaking pen. Students would stop before the line *"I wanted to live. I chose anyway. Both are true."* Some would cry. Some would argue. Some would copy it badly into notebooks because bad copies were still copies, and perfect silence had served Noctis long enough.

First, we stood in the room. Eight minutes became twelve. Maelin did not interrupt.

The spare issue coat stayed on the chair. The empty desk blotter stayed flat. The badly painted beam held morning light like a mistake no one had bothered to hide. On the desk, the slate stone sat beside the witness seal, ordinary and stubborn.

Leon picked it up again.

Leon: "Can I keep this?"

Rhea answered carefully.

President Valmont: "It is not Council property."

Leon looked at Elira.

Elira: "It was holding his page down."

Leon looked at me.

I thought of Cael in the corridor, telling us stable meant quiet enough to move. I thought of his voice in the trial, the way he had learned to say no with his whole body already expecting punishment. I thought of the room he had not lived long enough to trust.

Haru: "Then let it hold something else now."

Leon closed his fingers around the stone. For once, he did not ask what. That was its own answer.

---

We carried the copies down to the Grand Courtyard before midday, and the public board refused the first one.

Not with magic. That would have been easier to hate. It refused with red tape.

The relay slate above the courtyard accepted the heading, accepted the witness date, accepted Rhea's seal, accepted the phrase personal document, and then dimmed when Aira tried to enter Cael's own words. The surface turned pale gray. A polite warning appeared in the center.

**DECEASED STUDENT STATEMENT REQUIRES NEXT-OF-INSTITUTION REVIEW.**

For three seconds, everyone in the courtyard went very still.

The courtyard had been learning that stillness was dangerous. Stillness gave old systems time to dress harm in procedure. Students gathered near the fountain, along the outdoor stair rails, under the silver-leaf trees, and around the lower Green Circle notice posts. They had followed us from the eastern wing at a distance that tried to look respectful and failed because grief made everyone terrible at pretending.

Mira stood with the handwritten copy pressed flat against her chest. Finn stared at the pale gray glass.

Finn: "Next of institution?"

Aira's expression became so calm I knew violence had passed through her and chosen handwriting as its weapon.

Aira: "No."

The board brightened, as if encouraged by response.

**NOCTIS DOMINION COLLEGE LISTED AS LAST REGISTERED ORIGIN INSTITUTION.**

Leon stepped forward.

Rhea caught his sleeve with two fingers before he could put his fist through academy property.

President Valmont: "Do not give it damage to report."

Leon: "It just called Noctis his family."

President Valmont: "It called Noctis his paperwork."

Leon looked at her, waiting for comfort. Rhea did not soften the difference into comfort.

President Valmont: "We are going to correct the paperwork."

Elira had gone pale with anger, Yellow Circle light gathering beneath her skin like sunrise behind storm glass. Maelin, standing behind her with a healer's bag and the posture of a woman prepared to tackle aristocracy if necessary, narrowed her eyes.

Maelin: "Vale."

Elira: "I know."

Maelin: "That was not an accusation. It was a reminder that your pulse has opinions."

Elira breathed once through her nose, then looked at the board.

Elira: "The board is using inheritance rules."

Halden, who had arrived with three archive slates and no apparent ability to stand somewhere unobtrusive, answered immediately.

Professor Halden: "Custody rules. Same root, uglier use."

Cassian: "Excellent. The board has ancestry issues."

Halden ignored him because Professor Halden had discovered one could survive Cassian only by refusing to feed him.

Professor Halden: "The Inter-National Council already certified Cael's Protected Witness standing in the funeral record, yet legacy transfer tables inside the public courtyard board still default back to origin-institution custody whenever a student leaves no direct blood heirs-likely until someone forces an updated override."

Aira: "Likely?"

Professor Halden: "I am trying not to accuse the board of malice without evidence."

The board flickered again.

**NOCTIS DOMINION COLLEGE LISTED AS LAST REGISTERED ORIGIN INSTITUTION.**

Aira: "Evidence is gaining confidence."

Students murmured around the fountain. Mira turned toward the Green Circle cluster.

Mira: "Copy the warning."

Finn blinked.

Mira: "Exactly. Before it changes."

Ink moved. Paper unfolded. The Green Circle notice steps filled with hands, pencils, cheap pens, borrowed styluses, and one student writing on the back of a lunch receipt because no one had told him evidence preferred dignity. The board dimmed.

Then, very slowly, it displayed a second line.

**OVERRIDE AVAILABLE BY BLOOD RELATION, ORIGIN INSTITUTION, OR COUNCIL CUSTODY AUTHORITY.**

The word custody struck the courtyard like a bell hit wrong.

Nera made a small sound behind us.

Oric stood beside her, not in front, while his hand opened at his side in a way that made every Noctis-trained student nearby watch it. Darian Thorne, once Noctis enough that politics still tasted his name before trusting it, looked at the ground with a face so controlled it became confession.

Rhea lifted her council seal, her voice level across the courtyard.

President Valmont: "Aurelis Council Authority rejects the custody claim. Keep Protected Witness continuity."

The board accepted her seal. Then refused the wording.

**PROVISIONAL POST-MORTEM EXTENSION REQUIRES ORIGIN CONFIRMATION.**

The Black Circle stirred beneath my skin, invisible still, waiting.

Courtyard lamps dimmed by a fraction. The fountain water stopped moving. Every old stone beneath my feet became aware of me at once. Elira's fingers closed over mine, an anchor rather than a restraint.

Haru: "It is wrong."

My voice came out quiet enough that only the nearest ring heard. Quiet gave the words room.

Haru: "Witness does not end because the witness can no longer defend the record."

The board listened. So did Aurelis. So did everyone else.

Halden's eyes moved from me to the fountain, then to the old crest above the central arch. His scholar's fear and scholar's hunger stood side by side on his face.

Professor Halden: "Say that again carefully."

I did not look at him.

Haru: "No."

That surprised him. Good.

Haru: "Not from me."

I turned to Leon. He looked furious enough to shatter and frightened enough to listen.

Haru: "You."

Leon stared at me.

Leon: "I am not council."

Haru: "No."

Leon: "I am not a legal witness."

Rhea spoke up beside us.

President Valmont: "You opened and read Cael Nox's personal document under Aurelis witness seal."

Leon flinched at the name.

President Valmont: "That gives you standing to object when his words are mislabeled."

Leon laughed once, bitter.

Leon: "Standing."

Elira: "Beside is standing."

The courtyard held that too.

Leon looked at the board, at the warning, at that registered-origin claim as if it had insulted someone in a language he had only just learned to hate properly. He stepped forward.

His Blue Circle rose at his wrist, dull and ragged at the edge because grief refused to channel cleanly.

Leon: "Cael Nox is dead."

The words hurt because he did not soften them.

Leon: "That does not make Noctis his answer."

The board flickered. Leon swallowed.

Leon: "He wrote a statement before he died. He said not to make him noble enough that Noctis could admire him. If this board sends his words to Noctis for permission, it is doing exactly what he refused."

His voice cracked on refused. No one moved to repair it.

Leon: "Enter objection. Personal witness. Leon Varek. Beside."

The board hesitated, stalling between acceptance and rejection.

Old systems hated being addressed by language they had not been built to digest. Mira raised her hand.

Mira: "Additional objection."

Rhea turned.

President Valmont: "Mira Castellan recognized."

Mira stepped onto the lowest fountain stair. Her Green Circle showed at her wrist, small and bright and shaking.

Mira: "Record witness. Cael Nox verbally instructed that ugly copies survive better and corrections written before guilt edited them should not be made prettier. Sending his statement back to Noctis is editing it."

Aira's whisper barely carried past my elbow.

Aira: "Oh, that is good."

Finn wrote so fast his pen skidded. Mira's voice steadied.

Mira: "Enter objection. Green Circle public witness."

The board flickered again. This time, the warning changed.

**CONFLICTING WITNESS CLAIMS DETECTED.**

Cassian exhaled.

Cassian: "There it is."

Aira: "What?"

Cassian: "The system admitting more than one person exists. Historic."

Rhea's seal brightened.

President Valmont: "Enter Council clarification. Death does not end witness protection when there is active pressure, a custody dispute, or a risk of hostile rewriting."

The board tried to dim. Halden stepped forward.

Professor Halden: "Enter faculty archive note. The old archive rules conflict with Aurelis's current record standards. This board has no authority to put an old school ahead of a witness's written wishes."

Elira stepped beside Leon.

Elira: "Enter opening witness. Elira Vale. Cael Nox wrote, *'I wanted to live. I chose anyway. Both are true.'* Any review that treats death as consent to Noctis custody contradicts the statement."

The board flashed white.

For one breath, I thought it would break.

Then older script surfaced beneath the modern warning, carved in pale light from inside the stone itself.

**DEAD WITNESS STILL WITNESS.**

The grammar was ugly. Older than standardization. More honest than the board had been all morning.

The fountain water began moving again.

Green Circle students copied the line so quickly the courtyard filled with scratching.

Aira stared at it with open hunger.

Aira: "I am in love with terrible grammar."

Cassian: "Do we notify Haru?"

Elira looked at me, and despite everything, her mouth trembled toward a smile.

The Black Circle settled. Not because the danger had passed, but because the answer had not needed me alone.

The board accepted the statement, though not gracefully.

**PERSONAL RECORD ENTERED UNDER WITNESS CONTINUITY.**

Then, after a pause that felt spiteful:

**ORIGIN INSTITUTION REVIEW BYPASSED.**

Breath returned to the courtyard unevenly: a sob from the Green steps, a laugh too sharp from Cassian, Leon bending forward with both hands on his knees, Nera covering her mouth, Oric closing his eyes, Rhea lowering her seal before her hand could shake publicly.

Elira leaned against me for half a second. Only half. Enough.

Then a relay bell rang from the council arch. Rhea's expression closed.

President Valmont: "Noctis response. Their campus blackout is still sealed against every Council inquiry into Lucien or missing students, yet their legal clerk punched a restricted custody-claim link through the outer gate trigger the instant the board flagged origin bypass."

Aira: "They stayed silent on missing children and woke up to argue paperwork."

Rhea looked toward the accepted record.

President Valmont: "They were waiting for the board to refuse."

The bell rang again. This time, the fountain displayed the incoming seal.

Noctis Dominion College. Formal black. Silver edge.

Lucien's voice did not come through first. That made me colder.

Instead, an older woman appeared in the relay projection. Her hair was iron gray, pinned so tightly it seemed less styled than disciplined. Her uniform bore Noctis rank marks I did not recognize, yet Nera went still enough that recognition passed through the students behind us like a draft.

Nera: "Director Vaust."

Rhea heard.

President Valmont: "Identify for record."

Nera swallowed.

Nera: "Deputy Director of Corrective Continuity. She trained Lucien."

Cassian's smile vanished.

Director Vaust looked over the courtyard projection as if counting weaknesses by posture.

Director Vaust: "Aurelis has entered a deceased Noctis student's private document without origin review."

Rhea answered before anyone else could.

President Valmont: "Aurelis has entered a deceased Protected Witness's personal statement under witness continuity."

Director Vaust: "You are stretching an emergency witness ruling into permanent post-mortem estrangement."

President Valmont: "We are relying on a recorded choice."

Director Vaust's gaze moved to Leon.

Director Vaust: "Leon Varek."

Leon straightened.

Director Vaust: "Your family will be disappointed to see you lend your name to disrupting official procedure."

Leon went very still.

There it was. Not a blade, a hook. Family, disappointment, reputation, the old vocabulary of making obedience sound like love. Leon opened his mouth. Nothing came out. Elira started to move.

He lifted one hand slightly. Stop. She stopped.

Leon looked at Director Vaust.

Leon: "My family has survived worse than my first correct sentence."

Aira made a wounded sound of admiration.

Director Vaust did not blink.

Director Vaust: "Cleverness is not standing."

Mira stepped forward.

Mira: "Neither is ownership."

The whole courtyard seemed to realize at once that a Green Circle student had interrupted a Noctis director in public.

Director Vaust's gaze moved to her.

She did not sneer or raise her voice. She simply looked, and every habit Aurelis had taught Green students about shrinking backward pulled at Mira's posture. Finn moved beside her. Then another Green student.

Then two more. No one stood in front.

Mira's hands shook. Her voice did not.

Mira: "Cael Nox's statement names the risk of Noctis admiration. Your objection proves why this matters."

Director Vaust: "And you are?"

Mira lifted her notebook.

Mira: "Still copying."

For one second, Cassian looked like he might propose marriage to the sentence as a concept. Director Vaust's eyes cooled.

Director Vaust: "Aurelis has let public witnesses mistake strong feelings for legal authority."

Halden answered, his voice carrying the dry flatness of a man discovering someone had insulted his favorite kind of evidence.

Professor Halden: "Public witness is not legal authority. It is making sure the proof is spread out. You may argue over what it means. You cannot erase copies that independent people have already read and written down."

Director Vaust: "Professor Halden. I expected better rigor from you."

Professor Halden: "Then you expected flattery."

Aira actually stopped breathing for a second.

Rhea's mouth twitched and died before becoming expression.

Director Vaust ignored the insult with professional discipline.

Her gaze moved at last to me.

Director Vaust: "Haru Aerlen."

The courtyard changed temperature. Elira's hand tightened around mine.

Director Vaust: "Do you endorse this misuse of a dead student's name?"

There were many traps in the question.

Endorse made me the judge. Misuse turned defending him into disrespect. Dead student's name turned Cael into an object I could either claim or abandon.

Lucien had learned from her. That was obvious now.

I looked at the relay projection and felt every eye in the courtyard arrive at my back.

The Black Circle did not rise. That was my answer before words.

Haru: "No."

Director Vaust's expression did not change, though the courtyard shifted around me as fear gave way to confusion. I continued.

Haru: "I do not endorse Cael's statement. It does not need my endorsement."

Leon looked at me.

Haru: "I witnessed it being read. I object to Noctis custody. I refuse to become the authority that makes his words valid."

Director Vaust: "Convenient restraint."

Haru: "Difficult restraint."

Elira's thumb moved once across my knuckle.

Haru: "He wanted to live. He chose anyway. Both are true. If Noctis wants to challenge that, challenge the sentence. Do not ask me to stand over it so you can accuse me of casting a shadow."

Director Vaust watched me for a long moment. Then she smiled.

It was not Lucien's smile. Lucien smiled like a blade pretending to be a mirror. Vaust smiled like a locked door that had never needed to pretend.

Director Vaust: "Very well. Noctis challenges the sentence."

Nera's breath gave way in a sharp whisper.

Nera: "No."

Director Vaust: "Cael Nox could not want to live and choose to die at the same time under pressure from Aurelis. The note is moving, legally shaky, and medically suspect. Noctis asks that you pull it down pending spirit-state verification."

Maelin's healer bag hit the stone with a thud.

Maelin: "Absolutely not."

Director Vaust looked at her.

Maelin: "No one is using half-necromancy jargon on a dead boy just because you dislike what he wrote."

The courtyard went silent enough to hear the fountain.

Director Vaust: "Healer..."

Maelin: "Senior Healer Maelin Orr. Medical objection. Ethical objection. Human objection, if your office still accepts those in any format."

Cassian leaned slightly toward me, whispering out of the corner of his mouth.

Cassian: "I am definitely notifying Haru."

I did not look away from Vaust. Rhea stepped forward.

President Valmont: "Aurelis rejects spirit-state verification. Cael Nox's death was witnessed, recorded, and properly laid to rest. Noctis will not reopen his death to rewrite his life."

Director Vaust: "Then Noctis files formal complaint."

President Valmont: "Accepted."

Director Vaust: "And requests that all copies be locked away immediately."

Mira, Finn, Aira, and half the courtyard answered together, ragged and loud.

Witnesses: "No."

It was neither neat nor rehearsed, and Rhea did not smile.

President Valmont: "Denied."

Director Vaust's projection dimmed at the edges.

Before it vanished, she looked at me one last time.

Director Vaust: "Power surrounded by mourners is still power, Haru Aerlen."

Haru: "Yes."

The answer caught her off guard more than a denial would have.

Haru: "That is why they are allowed to say no."

The projection winked out without thunder or threat, leaving only the accepted statement on the board, the old line beneath it, and the sound of too many students breathing like people who had just learned procedure could be survived if enough hands refused to let go of the page.

Then Leon sat down on the fountain step. Hard.

Cassian moved first, disguising it as impatience.

Cassian: "Elegant collapse. Very Blue Circle. Excellent posture until the end."

Leon covered his face.

Leon: "Shut up."

Cassian sat beside him.

Cassian: "Beside shut up or distant shut up?"

Leon laughed, and it came out broken. Cassian looked at the board and stopped joking.

For several minutes, no one asked the courtyard to move on. That became its own kind of ceremony.

Students approached the board one at a time. Not to bow or worship, only to copy. Some wrote the full statement. Some wrote only one line. Some copied the old grammar: *Dead witness still witness.* A Yellow Circle student hesitated before the Green steps, then asked Finn if he had spare paper. Finn gave him the lunch receipt copy without thinking. The Yellow student stared at it, then accepted it like a relic with grease stains.

Nera stood at the edge of the fountain, reading Cael's sentence again and again. Oric remained beside her.

Darian watched them both with the look of someone realizing walking away did not end when you left a school. It kept going every time you refused to bring that school's habits into a safer room.

Elira leaned more heavily against me. Maelin noticed instantly.

Maelin: "Vale."

Elira: "I know."

Maelin: "Your knowing has a terrible track record."

Elira closed her eyes for half a breath.

Elira: "Two minutes."

Maelin: "One."

Elira: "Ninety seconds."

Maelin: "Because grief apparently negotiates."

I almost smiled. Then Elira whispered against my shoulder.

Elira: "I hate that he had to write it."

The almost-smile disappeared.

Haru: "So do I."

I held Elira's gaze without looking away.

Elira: "I hate that it is good."

I understood that too. Sometimes a true sentence was beautiful because harm had cornered someone into making it exact. Admiring it felt too close to accepting the corner.

Haru: "Then we do not call it beautiful."

She opened her eyes.

Haru: "We call it kept."

Elira looked at the board.

Elira: "Kept."

Maelin gave us the ninety seconds and pretended it was because she needed to repack her bag.

At the end of them, Aira approached with three copies in her hands.

Aira: "Formal, handwritten, ugly."

Elira: "Those are the categories?"

Aira: "They are now."

She gave the formal copy to Rhea, the handwritten one to Mira, and the ugly copy to Leon.

Leon looked at the blotched page.

Leon: "Why me?"

Aira: "Because if I give you the neat one, you will try to become worthy of it, and I am too tired to watch that."

Leon stared at her, then folded the ugly copy with more care than he had used for any academy assignment in his life.

Leon: "Fine."

Cassian leaned over.

Cassian: "Frame it badly."

Leon: "I will burn you."

Cassian: "There he is."

Tension eased across the courtyard without pretending to heal. There was a difference, and for once the difference did not feel like failure.

Rhea placed a protective seal over the public board at noon, leaving the glass clear.

The statement remained visible behind ward-light while copies continued to multiply through hands the institution had once trained itself to ignore. Green Circle students made the first ring. Blue students joined next. A few Red. Yellow last, as usual, though not never.

By early afternoon, *Dead witness still witness* had appeared in six margins, three formal objections, one badly drawn poster, and a chalk line on the lower fountain stone that Dren walked past twice without ordering removed.

Not a doctrine, as Elira had said, but a practice, something imperfect hands could repeat and keep honest.

---

That evening, after Maelin forced Elira back to the witness cottage and Rhea disappeared into what Aira called the paperwork furnace, I returned to Cael's room alone. Or as close to alone as anyone let me be anymore, and they were right.

Cassian stood in the corridor with his back to the wall, pretending to inspect a ceiling crack. He had two spark-flints tucked inside his left cuff, his frost-wrapped right wrist braced close to his coat, and one pastry openly in hand. Leon sat three doors down with the slate stone in his palm, staring at nothing. Aira occupied the hall bench with a notebook and the posture of a person who would claim she happened to be there if anyone asked.

Elira had wanted to come.

Maelin had said no in a tone that made ancient magic reconsider its priorities.

So I entered without her.

The room looked smaller in evening light. Maybe it was. Rooms changed after records entered them: some became shrines, some became evidence, some became traps. I did not want Cael's room to become any of those things if I could help it.

I stood by the desk and looked at the empty space where the letter had been.

Power offered me several impossible kindnesses. It could trace the pressure of his hand on the paper, draw a shadow of the last quiet hour he spent at this desk before the final hearing, force the walls to answer in images bright enough to hurt. The Black Circle knew ways to make absence speak. That was the problem.

Absence was allowed to be silent.

I placed my hand flat on the desk.

Haru: "Thank you."

No magic answered. Good.

The jammed top drawer handle caught my eye.

I left it shut. President Valmont's staff had cleared his visible personal effects right after the funeral without forcing the stuck drawer, and I had no right to pry open a dead boy's jammed wood alone when stripping every trace from the room felt too much like clearing it for the next occupant.

Instead, I sat in the chair.

Not the companion chair from the annex. This one was plainer, narrower, and badly balanced. It creaked under me like protest.

For several breaths, I let myself imagine the life Cael had not had time to mistrust. Breakfast without evaluation.

Classes where wrong answers did not become discipline.

Leon asking terrible questions and learning better ones.

Aira forcing him to write footnotes on his own sarcasm.

Elira teaching him that no could be gentle without becoming weak.

Me learning whether he preferred tea or coffee or neither because Noctis had probably ruined both by attaching them to schedules. Small things.

The Black Circle stirred with grief sharp enough to become weather. I closed my eyes.

Haru: "No."

The word was not for Cael. It was for me: no restoration, no echo, no bending the room until loss became easier to look at.

Elira had died in my arms and come back because death had been forced through an enemy spell still tied to life. Cael had made his choice in a tangle of consequences none of us could clean up. Those were not the same. If I blurred them because grief wanted one more miracle, I would make every future death a test of whether I had loved someone enough to break the world.

That way lay worship, and hatred, and madness wearing mercy.

I opened my eyes. The room remained cruelly ordinary.

Cassian spoke from the doorway.

Cassian: "You still in there?"

Haru: "Yes."

The cold pulse behind my ribs stayed quiet.

Cassian: "Existentially or medically?"

Haru: "Both."

He stepped in without crossing fully past the threshold.

Cassian: "Good. Maelin requested clarification before threatening me."

Haru: "How considerate."

He looked at the desk, the bed, the folded training coat. His face changed the way it did when joking reached the edge of usefulness and politely stepped back.

Cassian: "I did not know him well enough."

There were many comforting lies available. I chose none.

Haru: "No."

Cassian let the answer sit without flinching.

Cassian: "Still angry."

Haru: "Yes."

My fingers curled once against my coat hem before I forced them flat.

Cassian: "Good."

I looked at him. Cassian shrugged.

Cassian: "Not because anger is noble. It is not. Mostly it is loud and bad at furniture. But if we skip it, Noctis gets to decide his death was meaningful enough that we are not allowed to be furious."

The chair creaked as I leaned back.

Haru: "Aira would make you write that down."

Cassian: "Aira would improve the grammar and ruin my mystique."

Aira's voice carried in from the hall.

Aira: "Your mystique has three spelling errors."

Cassian closed his eyes.

Cassian: "See?"

For the first time in Cael's room, I laughed, a small, rough sound that did not feel like betrayal. That mattered.

When I left the room, Leon was still sitting three doors down with the stone in his palm. He looked up.

Leon: "Did you..."

He did not finish. Did you see him? Did you feel anything? Did the room say goodbye? Did being Black Circle make death less final for you than for the rest of us?

I sat beside him on the floor. Cassian stayed by the door, and Aira's pencil stilled.

Haru: "No."

Leon looked down at the stone.

Leon: "Good."

That was not the answer I expected. Leon swallowed.

Leon: "I thought I wanted something. A sign. A message. Anything. Then the board tried to send his words back to Noctis, and I realized... I do not want more of him taken for answers."

The stone sat in his palm, dull and gray and doing no magic at all.

Leon: "I can keep this without making it speak."

Haru: "You can."

Leon nodded once, his shoulders giving a small, sharp shake. He did not apologize. That was also practice.

---

Later, Elira read the ugly copy in bed with a blanket around her shoulders and Maelin stationed outside the cottage door like a medical curse. I sat beside her, close enough for warmth, far enough that the page belonged to her hands. The lamp was low.

The cottage smelled faintly of cedar smoke and bitter tonic.

Elira read the sentence three times.

*I wanted to live. I chose anyway. Both are true.*

On the third reading, tears slipped down her face.

Elira: "I wish he had written something worse."

Haru: "Worse?"

Elira: "Messier. Petty. Unfair. Something that would make me angry at him instead of at everything."

Her hand tightened around the page.

Elira: "He was allowed to be unfair."

I thought of Cael's controlled handwriting, trained almost to damage. Even his final refusal had tried not to take up too much room.

Haru: "Then we can be unfair for him sometimes."

Elira looked at me.

Haru: "Not in the record. In the room."

She folded forward until her forehead touched my shoulder.

Elira: "I am furious that he saved me."

There it was. The sentence beneath all the careful ones.

I put my hand near her back and waited until she leaned into it before touching.

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "I am grateful."

Haru: "I know."

Elira: "I hate being grateful."

Haru: "I know."

The Black Circle did not move. It had no answer for guilt that would not become violence if mishandled.

Elira cried quietly, which was worse than sobbing because quiet grief kept trying to be considerate.

When she found her voice again, she spoke without lifting her head.

Elira: "Do not let me make his death into a debt."

Haru: "I won't."

Elira lifted her head.

Elira: "And do not make that your debt either."

I almost looked away. She caught my face gently with her uninjured fingers and the taped heel of her cut palm, mindful of her braced left shoulder before I could turn.

Her palms were warm. Still too thin from recovery. Still alive.

Elira: "Haru."

Haru: "I hear you."

Elira: "No. Answer."

The seven lines in her pendant glowed faintly. Witness, not command. I let out a slow breath.

Haru: "I will try not to make his death into my debt."

Elira: "Try honestly?"

Haru: "Try honestly."

She studied me, found the answer imperfect, and accepted it because perfect answers had done enough damage.

Elira: "Good."

Outside, the academy bell rang evening close.

It sounded better than the morning bell. I disliked that.
